metadata.title: Crossed simplicial groups and structured surfaces

extraction_notes.note: latex_facts reports the hand-written proof of Lemma A.10 ('Proof of the lemma:') as running to the end of the document, bibliography included; the proof node was cut at 'This proves the lemma and Theorem A.9', and the closing paragraph proving Theorem 4.14 was made its own proof node.

Several Example environments that define objects used later (cyclic, dihedral, paracyclic, subdivided and quaternionic categories, Delta-G-traces, Delta-G-closure, ribbon/Moebius graphs, I[n], Delta^T, classical/monotone nerves) were retyped as definitions.
Remarks 1.42 state expectations ('We expect ...', 'should then give'); kept as a remark with rigor conjectural rather than a conjecture.

Theorem 5.9 has no proof environment; the preceding paragraph ('Consider the functor ... cong X(S,M)') was taken as its proof. Several one-sentence lead-ins ('The following is then immediate.', 'This implies the following.') were emitted as prose proofs.

Informal restatements in the Introduction (connective covering, parity, twisted actions, expected invariants) and the three tables (types, planar correspondence, invariants) were not emitted as nodes; the formal versions in the body are.

The proof of Theorem 5.7 cites Theorem A.4 (contractibility of the tessellation complex) for simple connectivity of P(S,M); the statement about P(S,M) itself is Theorem 4.14 (equivalent via Proposition A.3). The \ref edge was kept as written.

nodes.name: Connective covering $\mathbbm{p}: \mathbb{G}\to GL(2,\mathbb{R})$
nodes.statement: { \mathbbm{p}}: \mathbb{G} \longrightarrow GL(2,\mathbb{R}).
nodes.label: eq:GG

nodes.name: Simplex category
nodes.statement:
At the basis of combinatorial topology lies the {\em simplex category} $\Delta$ whose objects are
the finite ordinals $[n]=\{0,1,\dots, n\}$, $n \ge 0$, with morphisms given by monotone maps.

nodes.name: Simplicial object
nodes.statement: {\em Simplicial objects} in a category $\mathbf{C}$ are functors $\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}\to\mathbf{C}$.

nodes.name: Crossed simplicial group
nodes.statement: A {\em crossed simplicial group} is a category $\Delta \mathfrak{G}$ equipped with an embedding $i:\Delta \to \Delta \mathfrak{G}$ such that: \begin{enumerate} \item the functor $i$ is bijective on objects, \item any morphism $u: i[m] \to i[n]$ in $\Delta \mathfrak{G}$ can be uniquely expressed as a composition $i(\phi) \circ g$ where $\phi: [m] \to [n]$ is a morphism in $\Delta$ and $g$ is an automorphism of $i[m]$ in $\Delta \mathfrak{G}$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: A category containing $\Delta$ with the same objects, in which every morphism factors uniquely as a $\Delta$-morphism after an automorphism.
differentia: the functor $i$ is bijective on objects
nodes.label: defi:csg

nodes.name: Canonical factorization
nodes.statement:
We will refer to the representation $u=i(\phi) \circ g$ in (2) as the {\em canonical factorization}
of $u$.

nodes.name: Automorphism groups $\mathfrak{G}_n$
Operations $g^*\phi$ and $\phi^*g$
nodes.statement_short: Unique completion of a square in $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$ defines the operations $g^*\phi\in\Delta$ and $\phi^*g\in\mathfrak{G}_m$.

nodes.name: Skeleton of a crossed simplicial group
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)] \item For every morphism $\phi: [m] \to [n]$ in $\Delta$, the association $g\mapsto \phi^* g$ defines a map of sets \[ \phi^*: \mathfrak{G}_n \longrightarrow \mathfrak{G}_m,\; g \mapsto \phi^*g \] The association $\phi \mapsto \phi^*$ makes the family $\mathfrak{G}=(\mathfrak{G}_n)_{n\geq 0}$ into a simplicial set. The maps $\phi^*$ preserve unit elements but not necessarily the group structure. \item For objects $[m],[n]$, the association \[ (\phi,g) \mapsto g^*\phi \] determines a right action of $\mathfrak{G}_n$ on the set $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta}([m],[n])$. In the case $m=n$, this action preserves the identity morphism. \item In addition, we have the identities \begin{align*} \phi^*(g \circ h) & = \phi^*g \circ (g^*\phi)^*h,\\ g^*(\phi \circ \psi) & = g^*\phi \circ (\phi^*g)^*\psi. \end{align*} \item Conversely, any sequence of groups $\mathfrak{G}=(\mathfrak{G}_n)$ with operations \[ (\phi,g) \mapsto (\phi^*(g),g^*(\phi)) \] satisfying the compatibilities (a) - (c), uniquely determines a crossed simplicial group. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: The groups $\mathfrak{G}_n$ form a simplicial set with a compatible action on $\Delta$-morphisms satisfying crossed identities, and such data determine a crossed simplicial group.
nodes.label: prop:skeleton

nodes.name: Proof of Skeleton of a crossed simplicial group
nodes.statement: \cite{fiedorowicz-loday}, Proposition 1.6.
nodes.statement_short: Cited from Fiedorowicz-Loday, Proposition 1.6.

nodes.name: Deviation from a simplicial group
nodes.statement: Note that a simplicial group is a particular example of a crossed simplicial group, corresponding to trivial actions of $\mathfrak{G}_n$ on $\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([m], [n])$. Therefore, in general, these actions and the identities in Proposition \ref{prop:skeleton}(c), describe the ``deviation" of $\mathfrak{G}$ from being a simplicial group.
nodes.label: exa:deviation

nodes.name: Extreme cases of canonical factorization
nodes.statement: Let us point out the following special cases of canonical factorization in a crossed simplicial group ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$: \[ \operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}([n], [0]) \cong \mathfrak{G}_n, \quad \operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}([0], [n]) \cong \{0,1,\dots, n\} \times \mathfrak{G}_0. \] The first identification follows from the fact that $\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([n], [0]) = \operatorname{pt}\nolimits$. Note that the simplicial set structure on $\{\mathfrak{G}_n\}$ can be deduced immediately from this identification: $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}(-, [0])$ is a contravariant functor on ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ and, by restriction, on $\Delta$. The second identification follows from the canonical identification of $\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([0], [n])$ with $\{0,1,\cdots, n\}$ given by evaluation.
nodes.label: ex:extreme

nodes.name: Forgetful functor to sets
nodes.statement: Let ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ be a crossed simplicial group. Then we have a functor \[ \lambda: {\Delta \mathfrak{G}} \longrightarrow {\mathcal Set}, \; [n] \mapsto \operatorname{Hom}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}([0], [n])/\mathfrak{G}_0 \] where $\lambda([n])$ can be canonically identified with the set $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta}([0],[n]) \cong \{0,1,\dots,n\}$. In particular, we obtain, for every object $[n]$ of ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$, a canonical group homomorphism \[ \lambda_{n}: \mathfrak{G}_n \longrightarrow S_{n+1}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Every crossed simplicial group has a functor $\lambda$ to sets and homomorphisms $\lambda_n:\mathfrak{G}_n\to S_{n+1}$.
assumptions: Let ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ be a crossed simplicial group.
nodes.label: prop:forget

nodes.name: Proof of Forgetful functor to sets
nodes.statement: Follows from the second identification in Example \ref{ex:extreme}.
nodes.statement_short: Direct consequence of the second identification of Example 1.4.

nodes.name: Signed linear order
Category $\Delta\mathfrak{W}$
nodes.statement:
We introduce a category ${\Delta {\mathfrak W}}$ with objects given by the sets $\{0,1,\dots,n\}$, $n \ge 0$. A
morphism $f: I \to J$ is given by a map of underlying sets together with the choice of a signed
linear order on each fiber $f^{-1}(j)$. Composition of morphisms is obtained by forming {\em
lexicographic signed linear orders}: Given $f: I \to J$ and $g: J \to K$, we have, for $k \in K$, a
linear order on $(gf)^{-1}(k)$ obtained by declaring $i_1 \le i_2$ if 
\begin{enumerate}
	\item either $f(i_1) = f(i_2)$ and $i_1 \le i_2$ with respect to the linear order on the fiber of $f$,
	\item or $f(i_1) \ne f(i_2)$ and $f(i_1) \le f(i_2)$ with respect to the linear order on the
		fiber of $g$.
\end{enumerate}
The sign of $i \in (gf)^{-1}(k)$ is obtained by setting $\varepsilon_{gf}(i) = \varepsilon_f(i) +
\varepsilon_g(f(i))$.
nodes.statement_short: Objects finite ordinals; morphisms are maps with signed linear orders on fibers, composed lexicographically.

nodes.name: $\Delta\mathfrak{W}$ is a crossed simplicial group
nodes.statement: The category ${\Delta {\mathfrak W}}$ is a crossed simplicial group with \[ \mathfrak{G}_n = \operatorname{Aut}\nolimits_{{\Delta {\mathfrak W}}}([n]) \cong W_{n+1} \] where $W_{n+1}$ denotes the signed permutation group of $\{0,1,\dots,n\}$ also known as the wreath product $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\wreath S_{n+1}$.
conclusions: The category ${\Delta {\mathfrak W}}$ is a crossed simplicial group

nodes.name: Proof of $\Delta\mathfrak{W}$ is a crossed simplicial group
nodes.statement: We have to verify the unique factorization property which is a direct consequence of the definition of ${\Delta {\mathfrak W}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Unique factorization follows directly from the definition of $\Delta\mathfrak{W}$.

nodes.name: Weyl crossed simplicial group
nodes.statement:
Following Krasauskas, we call ${\Delta {\mathfrak W}}$ the {\em Weyl crossed simplicial group}, since the group $W_{n}$
is the Weyl group of the root system $B_n$ (or $C_n$).

nodes.name: Classification of crossed simplicial groups
nodes.statement: Let ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ be a crossed simplicial group. \begin{enumerate} \item There is a canonical functor $\pi: {\Delta \mathfrak{G}} \to {\Delta {\mathfrak W}}$. \item For every $n \ge 0$, we have an induced short exact sequence of groups \[ 1 \longrightarrow \mathfrak{G}_n' \longrightarrow \mathfrak{G}_n \longrightarrow \mathfrak{G}_n'' \longrightarrow 1 \] where $\mathfrak{G}_n'$ and $\mathfrak{G}_n''$ denote kernel and image, respectively, of the induced homomorphism $\pi_n: \mathfrak{G}_n \to W_{n+1}$. The short exact sequences assemble to a sequence of functors \[ {\Delta \mathfrak{G}}' \longrightarrow {\Delta \mathfrak{G}} \longrightarrow {\Delta \mathfrak{G}}'' \] where ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}'$ is a simplicial group (Example \ref{exa:deviation}) and ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}'' \subset {\Delta {\mathfrak W}}$ is a crossed simplicial subgroup of ${\Delta {\mathfrak W}}$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Every crossed simplicial group maps to the Weyl crossed simplicial group with simplicial-group kernel and image a crossed simplicial subgroup.
assumptions: Let ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ be a crossed simplicial group.
conclusions: There is a canonical functor $\pi: {\Delta \mathfrak{G}} \to {\Delta {\mathfrak W}}$.
we have an induced short exact sequence of groups
nodes.label: thm:classification

nodes.name: Proof of Classification of crossed simplicial groups
nodes.statement: Consider the functor \[ \lambda: {\Delta \mathfrak{G}} \longrightarrow {\mathcal Set}, \; [n] \mapsto \operatorname{Hom}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}([0], [n])/\mathfrak{G}_0 \] from Proposition \ref{prop:forget}. We claim that $\lambda$ admits a canonical factorization over the forgetful functor ${\Delta {\mathfrak W}} \to {\mathcal Set}$. Note that, via $\lambda$, the group $\mathfrak{G}_n$ acts canonically on the set $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta}([0],[n]) = \{0,1,\dots,n\}$ of vertices of the combinatorial $n$-simplex. A vertex $i \in \{0,1,\dots,n\}$ can be canonically identified with the corresponding degeneracy map \[ s_i: [n+1] \longrightarrow [n],\; j \mapsto \begin{cases} j & \text{for $j \le i$,}\\ j-1 & \text{for $j > i$.} \end{cases} \] Explicitly, given $g \in \mathfrak{G}_n$ and $i \in \{0,1,\dots,n\}$, we have a commutative square \[ \xymatrix{ [n+1] \ar[d]_{s_j^*g} \ar[r]^{s_i} & [n] \ar[d]^g\\ [n+1] \ar[r]^{s_j} & [n] } \] where $j = \lambda(g)(i)$. Clearly, the map $\lambda(s_j^*g)$ induces a map from the fiber $s_i^{-1}(i) = \{i,i+1\}$ to the fiber $s_j^{-1}(j) = \{j,j+1\}$ which is either order preserving or order reversing. Therefore, we can lift $\lambda(g) \in S_{n+1}$ to a signed permutation \[ \widetilde{\lambda}(g) = (\varepsilon_0, \varepsilon_1, \dots, \varepsilon_n ; \lambda(g)) \in \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} \wreath S_{n+1} \] where \[ \varepsilon_i = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if $\lambda(s_j^*g): \{i,i+1\} \to \{j,j+1\}$ is order preserving,}\\ 1 & \text{if $\lambda(s_j^*g): \{i,i+1\} \to \{j,j+1\}$ is order reversing.} \end{cases} \] Using the unique factorization property in ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$, it is straightforward to verify that the association $g \mapsto \widetilde{\lambda}(g)$ extends to provide a functor \[ \widetilde{\lambda}: {\Delta \mathfrak{G}} \longrightarrow {\Delta {\mathfrak W}} \] commuting with the forgetful functors to ${\mathcal Set}$, which proves (1). The remaining statements are easy to verify, the only nonobvious point being that ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}'$ is in fact noncrossed simplicial. But this follows from the construction of $\widetilde{\lambda}$: For $g \in \mathfrak{G}_n$, the condition $\lambda(g) = \operatorname{id} \in S_{n+1}$ implies that $g^*$ fixes all face maps $[n-1] \to [n]$. The condition that all signs $\varepsilon_i$ of the lift $\widetilde{\lambda(g)}$ are $0$ implies that $g^*$ fixes all degeneracy maps $[n+1] \to [n]$. But this implies that ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}''$ is a simplicial group (cf. Example \ref{exa:deviation}).
nodes.statement_short: Lift the action of $\mathfrak{G}_n$ on vertices to signed permutations via degeneracy maps, giving the functor to $\Delta\mathfrak{W}$; the kernel fixes faces and degeneracies.

nodes.name: Forgetful functor
nodes.statement:
Consider the functor
		\[
			\lambda: {\Delta \mathfrak{G}} \longrightarrow {\mathcal Set}, \; [n] \mapsto \operatorname{Hom}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}([0], [n])/\mathfrak{G}_0
		\]
	from Proposition \ref{prop:forget}.
nodes.statement_short: Recall the functor $\lambda$ of Proposition 1.5.

nodes.name: Factorization claim
nodes.statement:
We claim that $\lambda$ admits a canonical factorization over the forgetful functor ${\Delta {\mathfrak W}} \to {\mathcal Set}$. 
	Note that, via $\lambda$, the group $\mathfrak{G}_n$ acts canonically on the set
	$\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta}([0],[n]) = \{0,1,\dots,n\}$ of vertices of the combinatorial $n$-simplex. 
	A vertex $i \in \{0,1,\dots,n\}$ can be canonically identified with the corresponding degeneracy map
	\[
		s_i: [n+1] \longrightarrow [n],\; j \mapsto \begin{cases} j & \text{for $j \le i$,}\\
			j-1 & \text{for $j > i$.} \end{cases}
	\] 
	Explicitly, given $g \in \mathfrak{G}_n$ and $i \in \{0,1,\dots,n\}$, we have a commutative square
	\[
		\xymatrix{
			[n+1] \ar[d]_{s_j^*g} \ar[r]^{s_i} & [n] \ar[d]^g\\
			[n+1] \ar[r]^{s_j} & [n]
		}
	\]
	where $j = \lambda(g)(i)$. Clearly, the map $\lambda(s_j^*g)$ induces a map from the fiber
	$s_i^{-1}(i) = \{i,i+1\}$ to the fiber $s_j^{-1}(j) = \{j,j+1\}$ which is either order
	preserving or order reversing. Therefore, we can lift $\lambda(g) \in S_{n+1}$ to a signed permutation 
	\[
		\widetilde{\lambda}(g) = (\varepsilon_0, \varepsilon_1, \dots, \varepsilon_n ;
		\lambda(g)) \in \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} \wreath S_{n+1}
	\]
	where 
	\[
		\varepsilon_i = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if $\lambda(s_j^*g): \{i,i+1\} \to \{j,j+1\}$ is order preserving,}\\
						1 & \text{if $\lambda(s_j^*g): \{i,i+1\} \to \{j,j+1\}$ is order reversing.}
				\end{cases}
	\]
	Using the unique factorization property in ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$, it is straightforward to verify 
	that the association $g \mapsto \widetilde{\lambda}(g)$ extends to provide a functor
	\[
		\widetilde{\lambda}: {\Delta \mathfrak{G}} \longrightarrow {\Delta {\mathfrak W}}
	\]
	commuting with the forgetful functors to ${\mathcal Set}$, which proves (1).
nodes.statement_short: Claim: $\lambda$ factors through $\Delta\mathfrak{W}$.

nodes.name: $\mathfrak{G}_n$ acts on the vertex set.
nodes.statement:
Note that, via $\lambda$, the group $\mathfrak{G}_n$ acts canonically on the set
	$\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta}([0],[n]) = \{0,1,\dots,n\}$ of vertices of the combinatorial $n$-simplex.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathfrak{G}_n$ acts on the vertex set.

nodes.name: Identify vertices with degeneracy maps.
nodes.statement:
A vertex $i \in \{0,1,\dots,n\}$ can be canonically identified with the corresponding degeneracy map
	\[
		s_i: [n+1] \longrightarrow [n],\; j \mapsto \begin{cases} j & \text{for $j \le i$,}\\
			j-1 & \text{for $j > i$.} \end{cases}
	\]
nodes.statement_short: Identify vertices with degeneracy maps.

nodes.name: Each $g$ maps fibers $\{i,i+1\}$ monotonically or anti-monotonically.
nodes.statement:
Explicitly, given $g \in \mathfrak{G}_n$ and $i \in \{0,1,\dots,n\}$, we have a commutative square
	\[
		\xymatrix{
			[n+1] \ar[d]_{s_j^*g} \ar[r]^{s_i} & [n] \ar[d]^g\\
			[n+1] \ar[r]^{s_j} & [n]
		}
	\]
	where $j = \lambda(g)(i)$. Clearly, the map $\lambda(s_j^*g)$ induces a map from the fiber
	$s_i^{-1}(i) = \{i,i+1\}$ to the fiber $s_j^{-1}(j) = \{j,j+1\}$ which is either order
	preserving or order reversing.
nodes.statement_short: Each $g$ maps fibers $\{i,i+1\}$ monotonically or anti-monotonically.

nodes.name: Define the signed lift $\widetilde\lambda(g)$.
nodes.statement_short: Define the signed lift $\widetilde\lambda(g)$.

nodes.name: Unique factorization gives the functor to $\Delta\mathfrak{W}$, pro...
nodes.statement:
Using the unique factorization property in ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$, it is straightforward to verify 
	that the association $g \mapsto \widetilde{\lambda}(g)$ extends to provide a functor
	\[
		\widetilde{\lambda}: {\Delta \mathfrak{G}} \longrightarrow {\Delta {\mathfrak W}}
	\]
	commuting with the forgetful functors to ${\mathcal Set}$, which proves (1).
nodes.statement_short: Unique factorization gives the functor to $\Delta\mathfrak{W}$, proving (1).

nodes.name: Kernel is simplicial
nodes.statement:
The remaining statements
	are easy to verify, the only nonobvious point being that ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}'$ is in fact noncrossed
	simplicial. But this follows from the construction of $\widetilde{\lambda}$: For $g \in
	\mathfrak{G}_n$, the condition $\lambda(g) = \operatorname{id} \in S_{n+1}$ implies that $g^*$ fixes all face maps
	$[n-1] \to [n]$.
nodes.statement_short: Trivial image in $S_{n+1}$ means $g^*$ fixes all face maps.

nodes.name: Trivial signs fix degeneracies, so the kernel is a simplicial group.
nodes.statement:
The condition that all signs $\varepsilon_i$ of the lift
	$\widetilde{\lambda(g)}$ are $0$ implies that $g^*$ fixes all degeneracy maps $[n+1] \to
	[n]$. But this implies that ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}''$ is a simplicial group (cf. Example \ref{exa:deviation}).
nodes.statement_short: Trivial signs fix degeneracies, so the kernel is a simplicial group.

nodes.name: Reduction of the classification to subgroups of $\Delta\mathfrak{W}$
nodes.statement:
According to Theorem \ref{thm:classification}, the classification of crossed simplicial groups up
to extensions by simplicial groups therefore reduces to the classification of crossed simplicial
subgroups of the Weyl crossed simplicial group ${\Delta {\mathfrak W}}$.
conclusions: therefore reduces to the classification of crossed simplicial

nodes.name: Seven fundamental crossed simplicial groups
nodes.statement:
There are precisely $7$ such subgroups called
{\em fundamental crossed simplicial groups}.

nodes.name: Type of a crossed simplicial group
nodes.statement: Therefore, every crossed simplicial group has a {\em type} given by its image in ${\Delta {\mathfrak W}}$.

nodes.name: Growth rate
nodes.statement:
Note that the
$7$ subgroups of ${\Delta {\mathfrak W}}$ can be further distinguished according to their {\em growth rate}:
\begin{enumerate}
	\item {\em Constant:} For the trivial and reflexive groups, the cardinality of $\mathfrak{G}_n$ is constant.

	\item {\em Tame:} For the cyclic and dihedral groups, the size of $\mathfrak{G}_n$ grows 
 		linearly with $n$.

	\item {\em Wild:} For the remaining subgroups, the size of $\mathfrak{G}_n$ grows exponentially.  
\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Terminal morphism $\omega_n$
nodes.statement: Let $\omega_n: [n]\to [0]$ be the unique morphism from $[n]$ to $[0]$ in $\Delta$.
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions

nodes.name: $\omega_n^*$ is a homomorphism
nodes.statement:
The first equality in
Proposition \ref{prop:skeleton}(c)
  together with
the uniqueness of $\omega_n$ implies that the pullback map
\[
	\omega_n^*: \mathfrak{G}_0 \longrightarrow \mathfrak{G}_n
\]
is a group homomorphism.
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions

nodes.name: Semiconstant crossed simplicial group
nodes.statement: A crossed simplicial group ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ is called {\em semiconstant} if, for every $n \ge 0$, the homomorphism $ \omega_n^*: \mathfrak{G}_0 \longrightarrow \mathfrak{G}_n, $ is an isomorphism.
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions

nodes.name: Semiconstant groups are constant simplicial groups
nodes.statement:
Note that this condition implies that, for every map $\phi: [m] \to [n]$ in $\Delta$,
the corresponging map $\phi^*: \mathfrak{G}_n \to \mathfrak{G}_m$ is a group isomorphism. We may use $\omega_n^*$
to identify $\mathfrak{G}_n$ with $\mathfrak{G}_0$. Via this identification we have, for every $g \in \mathfrak{G}_0$ and
every morphism $\phi: [m] \to [n]$ in $\Delta$, a commutative square
\begin{equation} \xymatrix{ [m] \ar[d]_{\phi^*g = g}\ar[r]^{g^*\phi} & [n]\ar[d]^g\\
		[m] \ar[r]^{\phi} & [n]}
\end{equation}
in ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$. Therefore, the simplicial set $\mathfrak{G}_{\bullet}$ corresponding to a semiconstant crossed
simplicial group is a constant simplicial group. However, the action $\phi \mapsto g^*\phi$ may 
be nontrivial which is an additional datum.
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions

nodes.name: Commutative square for semiconstant groups
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ [m] \ar[d]_{\phi^*g = g}\ar[r]^{g^*\phi} & [n]\ar[d]^g\\ [m] \ar[r]^{\phi} & [n]}
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions
nodes.label: eq:semiconstant

nodes.name: Semiconstant subgroup generated by $\mathfrak{G}_0$
nodes.statement: Any crossed simplicial group ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ contains the semiconstant crossed simplicial group $\Delta \{\mathfrak{G}_0\}$ generated by $\mathfrak{G}_0$: we restrict ourselves to those automorphisms of $[n]$ which are pullbacks of automorphisms of $[0]$ along $\omega_n$.
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions
nodes.label: ex:semiconst-emb

nodes.name: Strict action of a group on a category
nodes.statement:
A (strict) action of a group $G$ on a small
category ${\EuScript C}$, is defined to be a homomorphism $G \to \operatorname{Aut}\nolimits_{{\EuScript Cat}}({\EuScript C})$ where ${\EuScript Cat}$ denotes the
category of small categories.
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions

nodes.name: Semidirect product $G\ltimes\mathcal{C}$
nodes.statement: Let ${\EuScript C}$ be a category equipped with an action of a group $G$. We define a category $G \ltimes {\EuScript C}$ called the {\em semidirect product} of $G$ and ${\EuScript C}$. The objects of $G \ltimes {\EuScript C}$ are the objects of ${\EuScript C}$, a morphism from $x$ to $y$ is given by a pair $(g, \phi)$ where $g \in G$ and $\phi: g.x \to y$ is a morphism in ${\EuScript C}$. The composition of morphisms $(g, \phi): x \to y$ and $(g', \phi'): y \to z$ is the morphism $(g'g, \phi' \circ g'.\phi)$
nodes.statement_short: Objects of $\mathcal{C}$; morphisms $x\to y$ are pairs $(g,\phi:g.x\to y)$.
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions
nodes.label: defi:semidirect

nodes.name: Grothendieck construction
nodes.statement: The action of $G$ on ${\EuScript C}$ can be interpreted as a functor ${\mathcal B} G \to {\EuScript Cat}$ where ${\mathcal B} G$ denotes the groupoid with one object and automorphism group $G$. In this context, the semidirect product $G \ltimes {\EuScript C}$ equipped with its natural functor to ${\mathcal B} G$ is known as the Grothendieck construction.
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions

nodes.name: Semiconstant groups are semidirect products
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a group acting on $\Delta$. Then the corresponding semidirect product $G \ltimes \Delta$ is a semiconstant crossed simplicial group. Vice versa, any semiconstant crossed simplicial group is isomorphic to a semidirect product $\mathfrak{G}_0 \ltimes \Delta$.
nodes.statement_short: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups are exactly semidirect products $G\ltimes\Delta$.
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions
assumptions: Let $G$ be a group acting on $\Delta$.
conclusions: is a semiconstant crossed simplicial group.
nodes.label: prop:semi

nodes.name: Proof of Semiconstant groups are semidirect products
nodes.statement: The semidirect product $G \ltimes \Delta$ has the unique factorization property: $(g, \phi) = (1, \phi) \circ (g, \operatorname{id})$ making it a semiconstant crossed simplicial group. Given a semiconstant crossed simplicial group ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$, it follows from \eqref{eq:semiconstant} that $\mathfrak{G}_0$ acts on $\Delta$. It immediately follows from the definition that we may identify ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ with $\mathfrak{G}_0 \ltimes \Delta$.
nodes.statement_short: Check unique factorization for $G\ltimes\Delta$; conversely the square for semiconstant groups gives a $\mathfrak{G}_0$-action on $\Delta$.
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions

nodes.name: $G\ltimes\Delta$ has unique factorization.
nodes.statement:
The semidirect product $G \ltimes \Delta$ has the unique factorization property:
	$(g, \phi) = (1, \phi) \circ (g, \operatorname{id})$ making it a semiconstant crossed simplicial group.
nodes.statement_short: $G\ltimes\Delta$ has unique factorization.
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions

nodes.name: A semiconstant group gives a $\mathfrak{G}_0$-action and is the sem...
nodes.statement:
Given a semiconstant crossed simplicial group ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$, it follows from
	\eqref{eq:semiconstant} that $\mathfrak{G}_0$ acts on $\Delta$. It immediately follows from the
	definition that we may identify ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ with $\mathfrak{G}_0 \ltimes \Delta$.
nodes.statement_short: A semiconstant group gives a $\mathfrak{G}_0$-action and is the semidirect product.
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions

nodes.name: Opposite involution $\daleth$
nodes.statement:
There is an involution $\daleth$ on $\Delta$ which is the identity on objects and maps a morphism 
$\phi:[m] \to [n]$ to the {\em opposite morphism} $\phi^{{\operatorname{op}}}:[m] \to [n]$ defined by 
$\phi(i) = n+1 - \phi(m+1-i)$. If we replace $\Delta$ by the equivalent larger category
$\mathbf\Delta$ of all nonempty finite ordinals, then $\daleth$ can be defined more naturally as
the functor ${\mathbf\Delta} \to{\mathbf\Delta}$ sending each ordinal $(I, \leq)$ to the opposite
ordinal $(I, \geq)$.
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions

nodes.name: Automorphisms of $\Delta$
nodes.statement: We have $\operatorname{Aut}\nolimits_{{\EuScript Cat}}(\Delta) \cong \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ with generator given by $\daleth$. In particular, any action of a group $G$ on $\Delta$ factors via a homomorphism $G \to \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ over the action of $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ on $\Delta$ given by $\daleth$.
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions
conclusions: We have $\operatorname{Aut}\nolimits_{{\EuScript Cat}}(\Delta) \cong \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ with generator given by $\daleth$.

nodes.name: Proof of Automorphisms of $\Delta$
nodes.statement: Well known.
nodes.statement_short: Well known (no argument given).
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions

nodes.name: Semiconstant groups as extensions
nodes.statement: As a corollary, we obtain that any semidirect product $G \ltimes \Delta$ admits a canonical functor to $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} \ltimes \Delta$. Interpreting this in the general context of crossed simplicial groups says that for a semiconstant crossed simplicial group ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$, the canonical functor into the Weyl crossed simplicial group of Theorem \ref{thm:classification} factors through the semiconstant crossed simplicial group $\Delta \{\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\}$. Thus, in terms of the classification of crossed simplicial groups, semiconstant crossed simplicial groups are extensions of $\Delta \{\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\}$ by constant simplicial groups.
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions

nodes.name: Groupoid $\mathcal{B}\mathbb{Z}/2$
nodes.statement:
Let ${\EuScript C}$ be a category and let ${\mathcal B}\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ denote the groupoid with one object and automorphism group
$\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions

nodes.name: Parity on a category
nodes.statement:
We define a {\em parity} on ${\EuScript C}$ to be a functor ${\EuScript C} \to {\mathcal B}\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$. Explicitly,
we are given a partition $\operatorname{Hom}(x,y) = \operatorname{Hom}(x,y)_0 \amalg \operatorname{Hom}(x,y)_1$ of every morphism set into
{\em even} and {\em odd} morphisms such that the composite of morphisms of the same parity is even
while the composite of morphisms of opposite parity is odd.
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions

nodes.name: Categories with parity
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate} \item A {\em parity} on a group $G$ is defined to be a homomorphism $G \to \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$. We obtain a category with parity by passing to groupoids ${\mathcal B} G \to {\mathcal B}\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$. \item Let ${\EuScript D}$ be a category equipped with an involutive functor $\tau: {\EuScript D} \to {\EuScript D}$. We may interpret $\tau$ as an action of $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ on ${\EuScript D}$. The corresponding semidirect product $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} \ltimes {\EuScript D} \to {\mathcal B}\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ is a category with parity. \end{enumerate}
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions

nodes.name: Semidirect products with $\mathbb{Z}/2$
nodes.statement: We give some examples of categories with parities arising as semidirect products with $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$. \begin{enumerate} \item Consider the category ${\EuScript Cat}$ of small categories. The involution $\tau: {\EuScript C} \mapsto {\EuScript C}^{{\operatorname{op}}}$ gives rise to a semidirect product $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} \ltimes {\EuScript Cat}$. We can consider enriched variants of this construction. For example, given a field $\mathbf{k}$, we obtain a semidirect product $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} \ltimes {\EuScript Cat}_{\mathbf{k}}$ where ${\EuScript Cat}_{\mathbf{k}}$ denotes the category of small $\mathbf{k}$-linear categories (categories enriched over $\operatorname{Vect}_{\mathbf{k}}$). \item As we have seen above, the simplex category $\Delta$ has a natural involution $\daleth$ and we obtain a corresponding semidirect product $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} \ltimes \Delta$. \item Let ${\EuScript C}$ be any category. The involution $\daleth$ of $\Delta$ induces an involution on the category ${\EuScript C}_{\Delta}$ of simplicial objects in ${\EuScript C}$. We obtain a semidirect product $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} \ltimes {\EuScript C}_{\Delta}$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions
nodes.label: exas:semi

nodes.name: Free category / nerve adjunction
nodes.statement:
We have an adjunction 
\[
		\operatorname{FC}: {\mathcal Set}_{\Delta} \longleftrightarrow {\EuScript Cat}: \operatorname{N}
\]
where $\operatorname{FC}$ associates to a simplicial set $K$ the free category $\operatorname{FC}(K)$ generated by $K$ and $\operatorname{N}$ takes a
small category ${\EuScript C}$ to its nerve $\operatorname{N}({\EuScript C})$.
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions

nodes.name: Proof of Adjunction of categories with parity
nodes.statement:
Note that this adjunction is compatible with the
involutions $\daleth$ and $\tau$ so that we have the following consequence.
nodes.statement_short: Compatibility of the adjunction with the involutions $\daleth$ and $\tau$.
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions

nodes.name: Adjunction of categories with parity
nodes.statement: We have an adjunction \[ \xymatrix@C=2ex{ \operatorname{FC}: \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} \ltimes {\mathcal Set}_{\Delta} \ar[dr]\ar@{<->}[rr]& &\ar[dl] \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} \ltimes {\EuScript Cat}: \operatorname{N}\\ & {\mathcal B} \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} & } \] of categories with parity.
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions

nodes.name: Twisted action
nodes.statement:
Given a group $G$ and a category ${\EuScript D}$, both equipped with parity, we define a {\em twisted 
action} of $G$ on an object $x$ of ${\EuScript D}$ to be a parity preserving homomorphism $G \to
\operatorname{Aut}\nolimits_{{\EuScript D}}(x,x)$ or, in other words, a functor
\[
	\xymatrix@C=1ex{ {\mathcal B} G \ar[rr]\ar[dr] & & {\EuScript D}\ar[dl]\\
	& {\mathcal B}\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} & }
\]
over ${\mathcal B}\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions

nodes.name: Twisted group actions on linear categories and simplicial sets
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate} \item From Example \ref{exas:semi}(1), we obtain the concept of a twisted group actions on a $\mathbf{k}$-linear category. Explicitly, this means that even group elements act as covariant functors while odd group elements act via contravariant functors. As a special case, given by a $\mathbf{k}$-linear category with one object, we obtain the concept of a twisted group action on an associative $\mathbf{k}$-algebra. \item Example \ref{exas:semi}(3) provides us with the concept of a twisted group action on a simplicial set (or more generally simplicial object). Here, even group elements act in an the usual orientation preserving way: all face and degeneracy relations are respected. Odd group elements act in an orientation reversing way so that all face and degeneracy relations are reversed according to the involution $\daleth: \Delta \to \Delta$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions

nodes.name: Semiconstant objects as twisted actions
nodes.statement: Let ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ be a semiconstant crossed simplicial group. Then, for any category ${\EuScript C}$, we have a natural equivalence of categories \[ {\EuScript C}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}} \overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow} \mathfrak{G}_0-{\EuScript C}_{\Delta}, \; K \mapsto K_{| \Delta} \] where \[ \mathfrak{G}_0-{\EuScript C}_{\Delta} = \operatorname{Fun}_{{\mathcal B}\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}}({\mathcal B} \mathfrak{G}_0, \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} \ltimes {\EuScript C}_{\Delta}) \] denotes the category of simplicial objects in ${\EuScript C}$ equipped with a twisted group action of $\mathfrak{G}_0 \to \operatorname{Aut}\nolimits(\Delta) \cong \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.statement_short: For semiconstant $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$, $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$-objects are simplicial objects with a twisted $\mathfrak{G}_0$-action.
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions
assumptions: Let ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ be a semiconstant crossed simplicial group.
conclusions: we have a natural equivalence of categories
nodes.label: prop:main

nodes.name: Proof of Semiconstant objects as twisted actions
nodes.statement: This follows immediately from unravelling the definitions.
nodes.statement_short: Unravel the definitions.
nodes.section: Semiconstant crossed simplicial groups and twisted group actions

nodes.name: Cyclic category
nodes.statement: The {\bf cyclic category} $\Lambda$ has objects $\langle n \rangle$, $n \ge 0$, while the set of morphisms from $\langle m \rangle$ to $\langle n \rangle$ can be described as follows. Let $C_n$ denote the topological space given by the unit circle in $\mathbb{C}$ equipped with the subset of marked points $\{0, 1, \dots, n\}$, embedded via the map $k \mapsto \exp(2\pi i k /(n+1))$. A morphism $f: \langle n \rangle \to \langle m \rangle$ in $\Lambda$ is a homotopy class of monotone maps $C_m \to C_n$ of degree $1$ such that $f(\{0,1,\dots,m\}) \subset \{0,1,\dots,n\}$. The category $\Delta$ is contained in $\Lambda$ given by restricting to those morphisms $f: \langle n \rangle \to \langle m \rangle$ such that any homotopy inverse of $f$, relative to the marked points, maps the oriented arc between $m$ and $0$ on $C_m$ into the arc between $n$ and $0$ on $C_n$. The family of groups $\mathfrak{G}$ associated to $\Lambda$ via \eqref{eq:crossed} is the family of cyclic groups $\{\mathfrak{G}_n=\mathbb{Z}/(n+1)\}$.
nodes.label: ex:cyclic

nodes.name: Dihedral category
nodes.statement: The {\bf dihedral category} $\Xi$ has objects $\overline{\langle n \rangle}$, $n \ge 0$. Morphisms from $\overline{\langle m \rangle}$ to $\overline{\langle n \rangle}$ are homotopy classes of monotone maps $C_m \to C_n$ of degree $\pm 1$ such that $f(\{0,1,\dots,m\}) \subset \{0,1,\dots,n\}$. The category $\Xi$ naturally contains $\Lambda$ and hence also $\Delta$. The family of groups $\mathfrak{G}$ associated to $\Xi$ via \eqref{eq:crossed} is the family of dihedral groups \[ \mathfrak{G}_n = D_{n+1} = \langle \omega, \tau |\, \omega ^2=1, \tau^{n+1}=1, \omega\tau\omega^{-1} = \tau^{-1}\rangle \] with $|D_{n+1}| = 2(n+1)$.
nodes.label: ex:dihedral

nodes.name: Paracyclic category
nodes.statement: The {\bf paracyclic category} $\Lambda_{\infty}$ has objects $\widetilde{n}$, $n \ge 0$. Morphisms from $\widetilde{m}$ to $\widetilde{n}$ are maps $f: \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ which preserve the standard linear order and satisfy, for every $l \in \mathbb{Z}$, the condition $f(l + m+1) = f(l) + n + 1$. The category $\Delta$ can be found in $\Lambda_{\infty}$ by considering only morphisms $f:\widetilde{m} \to \widetilde{n}$ such that \[ f(\{0,1,\dots, m\}) \subset \{0,1,\dots,n\}. \] Construction \eqref{eq:crossed} yields the constant family of infinite cyclic groups $\{\mathfrak{G}_n=\mathbb{Z}\}$. While this category was introduced in \cite{fiedorowicz-loday}, we borrow the terminology {\em paracyclic} from \cite{getzler-jones}.

nodes.name: Paradihedral category
nodes.statement: The {\bf paradihedral category} $\Xi_\infty$ has objects $\widehat n$, $n\geq 0$. Morphisms from $\widehat m$ to $\widehat n$ are maps $f: \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ which either preserve or reverse the standard linear order and satisfy, for every $l \in \mathbb{Z}$, the condition \[ f(l +m+1) = \begin{cases} f(l) + n + 1, \text{ if $f$ preserves the order}, \\ f(l)-n-1,\text { if $f$ reverses the order}. \end{cases} \] Thus $\Xi_\infty\supset \Lambda_\infty\supset\Delta$. Construction \eqref{eq:crossed} yields the constant family of infinite dihedral groups \[ \mathfrak{G}_n = D_{\infty} = \langle \omega, \tau |\, \omega ^2=1, \omega\tau\omega^{-1} = \tau^{-1}\rangle. \]
nodes.label: ex:para-dihedral

nodes.name: Subdivision functor $\operatorname{sd}_N$
nodes.statement:
For $N\geq 1$, we define the functor
\[
\operatorname{sd}_N: \Delta\longrightarrow\Delta, \quad [n-1] \mapsto [Nn-1]
\]
which takes a monotone map $\phi:[m] \to [n]$ to the $N$-fold concatenation of $\phi$ with itself.

nodes.name: Edgewise subdivision
nodes.statement:
Given a simplicial set $X$, the 
{\em $N$-fold (edgewise) subdivision} of $X$ is
the simplicial set $\operatorname{sd}^*_N(X)$
obtained by precomposing $X:\Delta^{\operatorname{op}}\to{\mathcal Set}$ with $\operatorname{sd}_N$.

nodes.name: Geometric description of edgewise subdivision
nodes.statement:
Geometrically, $\operatorname{sd}^*_N(X)$ is obtained from $X$ by subdividing each simplex into several simplices
such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item Each edge is subdivided into $N$ intervals by introducing $N-1$ intermediate vertices. 

\item No other new vertices  inside simplices of dimension $\geq 2$ are introduced.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, the geometric realizations of $X$ and $\operatorname{sd}_N^*X$ are canonically homeomorphic.

nodes.name: $N$-subdivided categories $\Lambda_N,\Xi_N$
nodes.statement: The {\bf $N$-subdivided categories $\Lambda_N, \Xi_N$.} Given a crossed simplicial group $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$ with the associated simplicial set $\mathfrak{G}$, one can form the simplicial set $\operatorname{sd}_N^*\mathfrak{G}$ and ask whether it can be completed to a new crossed simplicial group $\Delta\operatorname{sd}_N^*\mathfrak{G}$. It was observed in \cite[Ex.7]{fiedorowicz-loday} that this is indeed so for $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$ equal to $\Lambda$ and $\Xi$. The corresponding crossed simplicial groups will be denoted $\Lambda_N, \Xi_N$. They can be defined explicitly as follows. (a) The {\bf $N$-cyclic category} $\Lambda_{N}$ has objects $\widetilde{n}_N$, $n \ge 0$. A morphism from $\widetilde{m}_N$ to $\widetilde{n}_N$ is an equivalence class of maps $f: \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ which preserve the standard linear order and satisfy, for every $l \in \mathbb{Z}$, the condition $f(l + m+1) = f(l) + n + 1$. A pair of maps $f,g$ are considered equivalent if there exists an integer $r$ such that $f - g = rN(n+1)$. The category $\Delta$ can be found in $\Lambda_{N}$ by considering only those morphisms $f:\widetilde{m}_N \to \widetilde{n}_N$ such that \[ f(\{0,1,\dots, m\}) \subset \{0,1,\dots,n\}. \] Thus $\mathfrak{G}_n= \{\mathbb{Z}/N(n+1)\mathbb{Z}\}$. A description of $\Lambda_N$ which is more in line with Example \ref{ex:cyclic} can be obtained as follows. Fix an $N$-fold cover $\widetilde{C} \to C$ of the unit circle in $\mathbb{C}$. Then a morphism in $\Lambda_N$ between $\widetilde{m}_N$ and $\widetilde{n}_N$ can be described as a homotopy class of monotone maps $C_m$ to $C_n$ of degree $1$, preserving the marked points, together with a lift to $\widetilde{C}$. (b) The {\bf $N$-dihedral category} $\Xi_N$ is obtained by modifying the definition of $\Lambda_N$, allowing $f$ to either preserve or reverse the standard linear order and imposing the condition on $f(l+m+1)$ as in Example \ref{ex:para-dihedral}. We have a topological description analogous to the one for the $N$-cyclic category.
nodes.label: ex:subdivided

nodes.name: Quaternionic category
nodes.statement:
The { f quaternionic category} $
abla$ has objects $\check n$, $n\geq 0$. To describe morphisms, we first introduce the {\em quaternionic groups} \[ Q_n \,\,=\,\, \langle w, 	au |\, w^2=	au^n , 	au^{2n}=w^4=1, w	au w^{-1} = 	au^{-1}angle, \quad |Q_n|=4n. \] Here $n\geq 1$ is an integer. Thus $Q_1=\mathbb{Z}/4$. Let $\mathbb{H}$ be the skew field of quaternions. For any $r$, we denote by $\mu_r \subset \mathbb{C}^* \subset \mathbb{H}^*$ the group of $r$th roots of 1. Then $Q_n$, $n\geq 2$, can be identified with the subgroup in $\mathbb{H}^*$ generated by $\mu_{2n}$ and $j$. In other words, $Q_n$ is, for $n\geq 2$, a finite subgroup in $SU_2$ of type $D$ in the standard ADE classification (and in that context is also sometimes referred to, confusingly, as the ``dihedral group"). Another traditional name for $Q_n$ is the {``dicyclic group"} \cite[\S 7.2]{coxeter}. We have the central extension  egin{equation} 1	o \mathbb{Z}/2\longrightarrow Q_n uildrel \pi_n \over \longrightarrow D_n	o 1, \quad \pi_n(\omega) = \omega \end{equation} For $n\geq 3$, $D_n$ embeds into the group of automorphisms of $\mu_n\simeq \mathbb{Z}/n$, while $Q_n\subset\mathbb{H}^*$ normalizes $\mu_n$, so $\pi_n$ is obtained by looking at the conjugation action of $Q_n$. The morphisms of $
abla$ are defined to be generated by the morphisms in $\Delta$ and by elements of the groups $\operatorname{Aut}
olimits_
abla(\check n):=Q_{n+1}$ subject to the relations spelled out in \cite{loday}, Prop. 6.3.4(e) (proof). Thus, for $
abla$ we have \[ \mathfrak{G}_n = Q_{n+1}, \quad |\mathfrak{G}_n|= 4(n+1). \]
nodes.label: ex:quaternionic

nodes.name: Central extension of $D_n$ by $\mathbb{Z}/2$
nodes.statement: 1\to \mathbb{Z}/2\longrightarrow Q_n\buildrel \pi_n \over \longrightarrow D_n\to 1, \quad \pi_n(\omega) = \omega
nodes.label: eq:p_n

nodes.name: $N$-quaternionic category
nodes.statement:
The { f $N$-quaternionic category} $
abla_N$ is the crossed simplicial group obtained from $
abla$ by $N$-fold subdivision, similarly to $\Lambda_N$ and $\Xi_N$. In other words, the simplicial set associated to $
abla_N$ is $(Q_{N(n+1)})_{n\geq 0} = \operatorname{sd}_N^* igl( (Q_{n+1})_{n\geq 0} igr)$, see \cite{fiedorowicz-loday}, Ex. 7.
nodes.label: ex:N-quat

nodes.name: Planar crossed simplicial groups
nodes.statement: The crossed simplicial groups from Examples \ref{ex:cyclic}-\ref{ex:N-quat} will be called the {\em planar crossed simplicial groups}.

nodes.name: $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$-object
nodes.statement:
Let $\Delta \mathfrak{G}$ be a crossed simplicial group.  A  functor $X: (\Delta \mathfrak{G})^{{\operatorname{op}}} \to {\EuScript C}$
with values in a category ${\EuScript C}$ will be called a ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-{\em object} of ${\EuScript C}$.

nodes.name: Cyclic, dihedral, paracyclic objects
nodes.statement:
In the case when $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$ is one of the planar crossed simplicial
groups $\Lambda$,$\Xi$, $\Lambda_\infty$, etc, we will speak about {\em cyclic, dihedral,
paracyclic, etc,} objects in ${\EuScript C}$.

nodes.name: $\mathfrak{G}$ is a $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$-object
nodes.statement:
For example, the simplicial set $\mathfrak{G}$ extends naturally to a ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-object, as it follows from
Example \ref{ex:extreme}.

nodes.name: Paracyclic objects
nodes.statement: A paracyclic object $X: (\Lambda_{\infty})^{{\operatorname{op}}} \to {\EuScript C}$ can be described as a simplicial object $i^* X$ equipped with automorphisms $t_n: X_n\to X_n$, $n \ge 0$, satisfying the relations \begin{align*} \partial_i t_n & = \begin{cases} \partial_n & \text{for $i = 0$,}\\ t_{n-1}\partial_{i-1} & \text{for $1 \le i \le n$,} \end{cases} & s_i t_n & = \begin{cases} t_{n+1}^2 s_n & \text{for $i = 0$,}\\ t_{n+1}s_{i-1} & \text{for $1 \le i \le n$.} \end{cases} \end{align*} An $N$-cyclic object admits an identical description with the additional condition that the automorphism $t_n$, $n \ge 0$, has order $N(n+1)$. In particular, for $N=1$ we obtain an explicit description of cyclic objects.

nodes.name: Identity component $G_e$
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a topological group. We denote by $G_e\subset G$ the connected component of the identity.

nodes.name: Group of components $P=\pi_0(G)$
nodes.statement: The possibly nonabelian group $P=\pi_0(G)$.

nodes.name: Abelian group $A=\pi_1(G_e,e)$
nodes.statement: The abelian group $A=\pi_1(G_e, e)$ equipped with a natural $P$-action induced by conjugation in $G$.

nodes.name: Cohomology class $\gamma_G$
nodes.statement:
The cohomology class $\gamma=\gamma_G\in H^3(P,A)$ defined as follows. For every connected
component $a\in P=\pi_0(G)$, we choose a representative $g_a\in G$. For every pair $a,b\in P$,
we choose a path $\xi_{a,b}$ joining $g_ag_b$ and $g_{ab}$. We denote by $\xi_{a,b}^{-1}$ the same path
run in the opposite direction. Then, for every triple $a,b,c\in P$, we have a loop
in the component $abc$:
\[
\xymatrix{
g_a g_b g_c \ar[r]^{\xi_{a,b}\cdot g_c}& g_{ab}g_c
\ar[d]^{\xi_{ab, c}}
\\
g_a g_{bc}\ar[u]^{g_a\cdot \xi_{b,c}^{-1}}&\ar[l]^{\xi_{a,bc}^{-1}} g_{abc}
}
\]
By multiplying this loop pointwise on the left with $g_{abc}^{-1}$, we obtain a loop $L(a,b,c)$ in
$G_e$ based at $e$. We denote by $\gamma(a,b,c) \in A$ the class of $L(a,b,c)$. 
The collection $\{ \gamma(a,b,c) \}$ forms a 3-cocycle of $P$ with coefficients in $A$ 
whose cohomology class is independent on the choices.
nodes.statement_short: The 3-cocycle of $P$ with values in $A$ built from choices of representatives and connecting paths.

nodes.name: Connective covering
nodes.statement: A morphism $p:\widetilde G\to G$ of topological groups is called a {\em connective covering}, if $p$ is a covering of its image, and $p^{-1}(G_e)$ is connected, that is, coincides with $\widetilde G_e$. A {\em proper covering} is a surjective connective covering.
differentia: $p$ is a covering of its image

nodes.name: Connectivity via injectivity on $\pi_0$
nodes.statement:
Note that the condition $p^{-1}(G_e)=\widetilde G_e$ is equivalent to saying that the induced homomorphism
$p_*:\pi_0(\widetilde G)\to\pi_0(G)$ is injective.

nodes.name: Category of proper coverings $\operatorname{Con}(G)$
nodes.statement:
We denote by $\operatorname{Con}(G)$ the category of proper coverings of $G$, with morphisms being morphisms
of topological groups commuting with the projections to $G$.

nodes.name: Subgroups $\widetilde P,\widetilde A$ of a covering
Subgroups $\widetilde P\subset P$, $\widetilde A\subset A$
nodes.statement: \begin{gathered} \widetilde P \,\,=\,\,\pi_0(\widetilde G)\,\, \subset\,\, P\,\,=\,\,\pi_0(G), \\ \widetilde A \,\,=\,\, \pi_1(\widetilde G_e,e)\,\, \subset\,\, A\,\,=\,\,\pi_1(G_e,e), \end{gathered}
nodes.label: eq:tilde-P-A

nodes.name: Classification of connective coverings
nodes.statement: \begin{itemize} \item[(a)] Suppose we are given subgroups $\widetilde P\subset P$, $\widetilde A\subset A$ so that $\widetilde A$ is $P$-invariant. For the existence of a connective covering $\widetilde G$ realizing $\widetilde P$ and $\widetilde A$ as in \eqref{eq:tilde-P-A}, it is necessary and sufficient that the image of $\gamma_G$ in $H^3(\widetilde P, A/\widetilde A)$ be $0$. \item[(b)] In particular, $G$ has a ``universal covering" (a proper covering $\widetilde G$ with $\widetilde G_e$ simply connected), if and only if $\gamma_G=0$. \item[(c)] If $f: G_1\to G_2$ is a morphism of topological groups which is a homotopy equivalence of topological spaces, then pullback under $f$ gives an equivalence of categories \[ f^*: \operatorname{Con}(G_2)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Con}(G_1). \] \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Connective coverings with given $(\widetilde P,\widetilde A)$ exist iff the obstruction class vanishes; homotopy equivalences induce equivalences of covering categories.
assumptions: Suppose we are given subgroups $\widetilde P\subset P$, $\widetilde A\subset A$ so that $\widetilde A$
conclusions: it is necessary and sufficient that the image of $\gamma_G$ in $H^3(\widetilde P, A/\widetilde A)$
then pullback under $f$ gives an equivalence of categories
nodes.label: prop:summary-covers

nodes.name: 2-group
nodes.statement:
By definition, a 2-group
is an essentially small monoidal category $({\bf G}, \otimes, {\bf 1})$ in which each object is invertible
(up to isomorphism) with respect to $\otimes$ and each morphism is invertible with respect to composition.

nodes.name: Crossed module
nodes.statement:
{\bf Crossed modules,}
i.e.,  data consisting of a morphism of groups
\[
\bigl\{ K^{-1} \buildrel\partial \over\longrightarrow K^0\bigr\}
\]
and an action $\epsilon: K^0\to \operatorname{Aut}\nolimits(K^{-1})$ satisfying the axioms
\[
\begin{gathered}
\epsilon(\partial(k_{-1}))(k'_{-1}) \,\,=\,\, k'_{-1} \cdot k_{-1} \cdot (k'_1)^{-1},\quad k_{-1}, k'_{-1} \in K^{-1},
\\
\partial(k_{-1})\cdot k_0 \cdot \partial(k_{-1})^{-1} \,\,=\,\, \partial (\epsilon(k_0)(k_{-1})),
\quad
k_0\in K^0, k_{-1}\in K^{-1}.
\end{gathered}
\]

nodes.name: Circle $S^1$ and $\operatorname{Homeo}(S^1)$
nodes.statement:
Let $S^1$ be the standard unit circle in $\mathbb{C}$, and  ${ \operatorname{Homeo}}(S^1)$ be the group of all self-homeomorphisms
 of $S^1$ with the standard (compact-open) topology.

nodes.name: Coverings of $O(2)$, $GL(2,\mathbb{R})$ and $\operatorname{Homeo}(S^1)$ agree
nodes.statement:
We have morphisms of topological groups
 \[
 O(2) \,\,\hookrightarrow \,\, GL(2,\mathbb{R}) \longrightarrow { \operatorname{Homeo}}(S^1)
 \]
 which are homotopy equivalences, Therefore, by Proposition \ref{prop:summary-covers}(c), the categories
 of connective coverings of these three groups are naturally identified.

nodes.name: Planar Lie group
nodes.statement: Connective coverings of $O(2)$ will be called {\em (thin) planar Lie groups}.

nodes.name: Thick planar Lie group
nodes.statement: Connective coverings of $GL(2, \mathbb{R})$ will be called {\em thick planar Lie groups}.

nodes.name: Notation $G^\diamond$
nodes.statement:
We will
 denote them by $G^\diamond$, where $G$ is a thin planar Lie group.

nodes.name: Planar homeomorphism group
nodes.statement: Connective coverings of ${ \operatorname{Homeo}}(S^1)$ will be called {\em planar homeomorphism groups}.

nodes.name: Notation $\operatorname{Homeo}^G(S^1)$
nodes.statement: We will denote them by ${ \operatorname{Homeo}}^G(S^1)$, where $G$ is as above.

nodes.name: Planar Lie groups and their crossed simplicial groups
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)] \item The group $SO(2)$ corresponds to the cyclic category $\Lambda$. \item The group $O(2)$ corresponds to the dihedral category $\Xi$. \item We denote by $\widetilde{SO}(2)\to SO(2)$ the universal covering of $SO(2)\simeq S^1$. It corresponds to the paracyclic category $\Lambda_\infty$. \item We denote \[ \widetilde O(2) = (\mathbb{Z}/2)\ltimes \mathbb{R} \longrightarrow O(2) = (\mathbb{Z}/2)\ltimes S^1 \] the proper covering of the semi-direct product induced from the universal covering $\mathbb{R}\to S^1$. It corresponds to the paradihedral category $\Xi_\infty$. \item Consider the group \[ P \,\,=\,\,\bigl\{ q\in\mathbb{H}^* \bigl| \,\, |q|=1, q S^1 q^{-1} \subset S^1 \bigr\}. \] Here $S^1$ is considered as the unit circle subgroup in $\mathbb{C}^*\subset\mathbb{H}^*$. In other words, $P$ is the normalizer of a maximal torus in $SU(2)$. Like $O(2)$, the group $P$ has $\pi_0=\mathbb{Z}/2$ and $P_e= S^1$, but the corresponding extension of $\mathbb{Z}/2$ by $S^1$ is different from the one provided by $O(2)$. Similarly to \eqref{eq:p_n}, looking at the conjugation action gives a central extension \[ 1\to \mathbb{Z}/2\longrightarrow P \buildrel \pi \over \longrightarrow O(2)\to 1 \] with $\pi$ a proper covering. This makes $P$ into a planar Lie group. It corresponds to the quaternionic category $\nabla$. \item Let $N\geq 1$. We denote the unique $N$-fold proper covering of $SO(2)$ by \[ 1\to \mathbb{Z}/N \longrightarrow \operatorname{Spin}_N(2)\buildrel \phi_N\over \longrightarrow SO(2) \to 1. \] As an abstract Lie group, $\operatorname{Spin}_N(2)$ is identified with $SO(2)$, and $\phi_N$ is the $N$th power homomorphism. The group $\operatorname{Spin}_N(2)$ corresponds to the $N$-cyclic category $\Lambda_N$. \item Let us represent elements of $O(2) = (\mathbb{Z}/2)\ltimes S^1$ as pairs $(\alpha, z)=\alpha\cdot z$ with $\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}/2$, $z\in S^1$, so that $\alpha z\alpha^{-1} = z^{-1}$. Then the map \[ f_N: O(2)\longrightarrow O(2), \quad (\alpha, z)\mapsto (\alpha, z^N). \] is a (continuous) homomorphism and, moreover, a proper covering with kernel $\mathbb{Z}/N$. We denote this covering \[ 1\to \mathbb{Z}/N \longrightarrow \operatorname{Pin}^+_N(2) \buildrel p_N^+ \over\longrightarrow O(2)\to 1 \] Thus $ \operatorname{Pin}^+_N(2)=O(2)$ as an abstract Lie group, and $p_N^+=f_N$. The planar Lie group $\operatorname{Pin}^+_N(2)$ corresponds to the $N$-dihedral category $\Xi_N$. \item If $N=2M$ is even, then the composition $P\buildrel \pi \over\to O(2) \buildrel f_M\over\to O(2)$ is a proper covering with kernel $\mathbb{Z}/N$. We denote this covering \[ 1\to \mathbb{Z}/N \longrightarrow \operatorname{Pin}^-_N(2) \buildrel p_N^- \over\longrightarrow O(2)\to 1 \] Thus $ \operatorname{Pin}^-_N(2)=Q_\infty$ as an abstract Lie group, and $p_N^-=f_M\pi$. The planar Lie group $\operatorname{Pin}^-_{N}(2)$ corresponds to the $M$-quaternionic category $\nabla_M$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: ex:planar

nodes.name: Classification of planar Lie groups
nodes.statement: The groups from Examples \ref{ex:planar} exhaust all planar Lie groups up to isomorphism. \qed
conclusions: exhaust all planar Lie groups up to isomorphism.

nodes.name: Proof of Classification of planar Lie groups
nodes.statement: The question reduces to classification of proper coverings of $O(2)$ for which see, e.g., \cite[\S 8]{taylor}. \qed
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the classification of proper coverings of $O(2)$ (Taylor).

nodes.name: Realizations of planar crossed simplicial groups
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate} \item[(a)] Let $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$ be any crossed simplicial group. Then the geometric realization $|\mathfrak{G}|$ of the simplicial set $\mathfrak{G}$ has a natural group structure, making it a topological group. Further, the geometric realization $|\operatorname{N} (\Delta\mathfrak{G})|$ of the nerve of $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$ is homotopy equivalent to the classifying space $B |\mathfrak{G}|$. \item[(b)] Let $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$ be a planar crossed simplicial group. Then: \begin{enumerate} \item[(b1)] $|\mathfrak{G}|=G$ is the planar Lie group corresponding to $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$ in Table \ref{table:corr}. In particular, there is a covering $p: G\to O(2)$. \item[(b2)] The group $\mathfrak{G}_n$ is identified with the subgroup $p^{-1}(D_{n+1})$, where $D_{n+1}$ is embedded into $O(2)=(\mathbb{Z}/2)\ltimes S^1$ as $(\mathbb{Z}/2)\ltimes\mu_{n+1}$. \end{enumerate} \item[(c)] Let $X:\Delta\mathfrak{G}^{\operatorname{op}}\to{\mathcal Set}$ be any $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$-set. Then $|i^*X|$, the geometric realization of $X$ considered as a simplicial set, has a natural $G$-action. \item[(d)] The homotopy category of $G$-spaces can be identified with the localization of the category $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta\mathfrak{G}^{\operatorname{op}}, {\mathcal Set})$ along morphisms which give homotopy equivalences of the induced simplicial sets. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $|\mathfrak{G}|$ is a topological group with $|N\Delta\mathfrak{G}|\simeq B|\mathfrak{G}|$; for planar $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$ it is the planar Lie group, and $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$-sets model $G$-spaces.
assumptions: Let $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$ be any crossed simplicial group.
Let $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$ be a planar crossed simplicial group.
conclusions: has a natural group structure, making it a topological group.
is homotopy equivalent to the classifying space $B |\mathfrak{G}|$.
planar Lie group corresponding to $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$ in Table \ref{table:corr}.
nodes.label: thm:crossed-groups

nodes.name: Proof of Realizations of planar crossed simplicial groups
nodes.statement: (a) was shown by Fiedorowicz and Loday \cite{fiedorowicz-loday}. The identification of $|\mathfrak{G}|$ in the examples of (b) is also immediate from their considerations. The remaining parts are well known \cite{DHK} \cite[Ch.7]{loday} in the cyclic and paracyclic cases $\Delta \mathfrak{G}=\Lambda, \Lambda_\infty$, and were extended by Dunn \cite{dunn} to the dihedral and quaternionic cases. The $N$-subdivided cases can be deduced from these using the fact that $\operatorname{sd}_N^*$ does not change the geometric realization. The paradihedral case can be deduced from the paracyclic one by identifying $\Xi_\infty$ with the semi-direct product of $\mathbb{Z}/2$ and $\Lambda_\infty$. We leave the remaining details to the reader.
nodes.statement_short: Collects results of Fiedorowicz-Loday, Dwyer-Hopkins-Kan, Loday and Dunn; subdivided and paradihedral cases reduce to these.

nodes.name: Part (a) and the identification in (b) from Fiedorowicz-Loday.
nodes.statement:
(a)  was shown by Fiedorowicz and Loday \cite{fiedorowicz-loday}.  The identification of
   $|\mathfrak{G}|$ in the examples of (b) is also immediate from their considerations.
nodes.statement_short: Part (a) and the identification in (b) from Fiedorowicz-Loday.

nodes.name: Cyclic, paracyclic, dihedral, quaternionic cases are known.
nodes.statement:
The remaining parts
   are well known \cite{DHK} \cite[Ch.7]{loday} in the cyclic and paracyclic cases
    $\Delta \mathfrak{G}=\Lambda,
   \Lambda_\infty$,
   and were extended by Dunn \cite{dunn} to the dihedral and quaternionic cases.
nodes.statement_short: Cyclic, paracyclic, dihedral, quaternionic cases are known.

nodes.name: Subdivision does not change the realization.
nodes.statement:
The   $N$-subdivided  cases can be deduced from these using the fact that $\operatorname{sd}_N^*$
   does not change the geometric realization.
nodes.statement_short: Subdivision does not change the realization.

nodes.name: Paradihedral case as a semidirect product with $\mathbb{Z}/2$.
nodes.statement:
The paradihedral case can be
   deduced from the paracyclic one by identifying $\Xi_\infty$ with the semi-direct product of
   $\mathbb{Z}/2$ and $\Lambda_\infty$. We leave the remaining details to the reader.
nodes.statement_short: Paradihedral case as a semidirect product with $\mathbb{Z}/2$.

nodes.name: Canonical parity of $\mathfrak{G}_0$
nodes.statement:
By Proposition \ref{prop:semi}, the group $\mathfrak{G}_0$ acts on $\Delta$ and is
hence equipped with a {\em canonical parity} $\mathfrak{G}_0 \to \operatorname{Aut}\nolimits(\Delta) \cong \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$.

nodes.name: Canonical parity for planar groups
nodes.statement: Let ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ be a planar crossed simplicial group with the corresponding planar Lie group $p: G \to O(2)$. Then: \begin{enumerate} \item[(a)] Let $O(1)=\mathbb{Z}/2$ be embedded into $O(2)$ in the standard way. Then $\mathfrak{G}_0$ is identified, as a group with parity, with the preimage of $O(1)$ in $G$, so we have the Cartesian square \[ \xymatrix{ \mathfrak{G}_0\ar[r]^\epsilon \ar[d]^{\hskip -.7cm \rho} & G\ar[d]^p\\ \mathbb{Z}/2=O(1) \ar[r]& O(2). } \] \item[(b)] Explicitly, the canonical parities of $\mathfrak{G}_0 = \mathbb{Z}, (\mathbb{Z}/2)\ltimes \mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{Z}/N, D_N, Q_N$ are given as follows: the groups $\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}/N$ are equipped with the trivial homomorphism to $\mathbb{Z}/2$, and the group $D_N$ and $Q_N$ with homomorphisms \[ \begin{gathered} \rho_D: D_N\longrightarrow \mathbb{Z}/2, \quad \rho_D(\omega)=\overline 1, \,\,\rho_D(\tau)=\overline 0, \\ \rho_Q: Q_N\longrightarrow \mathbb{Z}/2, \quad \rho_Q(w)=\overline 1, \,\,\rho_Q(\tau)=\overline 0, \end{gathered} \] and $(\mathbb{Z}/2)\ltimes\mathbb{Z}$ with the projection to $\mathbb{Z}/2$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: For planar $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$, $\mathfrak{G}_0$ is the preimage of $O(1)$ in $G$, with explicit parities.
assumptions: Let ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ be a planar crossed simplicial group with the corresponding planar Lie group $p: G \to O(2)$.
nodes.label: prop:orient-G-0

nodes.name: Proof of Canonical parity for planar groups
nodes.statement: We recall that $G$ is identified with $|\mathfrak{G}|$ by Theorem \ref{thm:crossed-groups}(b1). A homomorphism $\epsilon: \mathfrak{G}_0\to |\mathfrak{G}|$ is obtained from the compatible system of homomorphisms $\omega_n^*: \mathfrak{G}_0\to \mathfrak{G}_n$. The verification that $\epsilon$ is an embedding with the required properties, is obtained using case by case analysis.
nodes.statement_short: Embed $\mathfrak{G}_0$ into $|\mathfrak{G}|$ via the maps $\omega_n^*$ and check case by case.

nodes.name: Recall $G=|\mathfrak{G}|$.
nodes.statement:
We recall that $G$ is identified with $|\mathfrak{G}|$ by Theorem 
\ref{thm:crossed-groups}(b1).
nodes.statement_short: Recall $G=|\mathfrak{G}|$.

nodes.name: Define $\epsilon$ from the $\omega_n^*$.
nodes.statement:
A homomorphism $\epsilon: \mathfrak{G}_0\to |\mathfrak{G}|$
is obtained from the compatible system of homomorphisms $\omega_n^*: \mathfrak{G}_0\to \mathfrak{G}_n$.
nodes.statement_short: Define $\epsilon$ from the $\omega_n^*$.

nodes.name: Verify properties case by case.
nodes.statement:
The verification that $\epsilon$ is an embedding with the required properties, is obtained using case
by case analysis.
nodes.statement_short: Verify properties case by case.

nodes.name: $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$-simplex
nodes.statement:
Let ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ be any crossed simplicial group, and let $n\geq 0$. We call the representable ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-set
\[
{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}^n := \operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}(-, [n]): {\Delta \mathfrak{G}}^{\operatorname{op}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal Set}
\]
the $n$-dimensional {\em ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-simplex}.

nodes.name: Cosimplicial categories with twisted action
nodes.statement: For any crossed simplicial group ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$, we have a natural functor \[ {\Delta \mathfrak{G}} \longrightarrow \mathfrak{G}_0-{\EuScript Cat},\; [n] \mapsto \operatorname{FC}({\Delta \mathfrak{G}}^n|_{\Delta}) \] where \[ \mathfrak{G}_0-{\EuScript Cat} = \operatorname{Fun}_{{\mathcal B}\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}}({\mathcal B} \mathfrak{G}_0, \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} \ltimes {\EuScript Cat}) \] denotes the category of small categories equipped with a twisted action of $\mathfrak{G}_0$.
assumptions: For any crossed simplicial group ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$
nodes.label: prop:cosimplex

nodes.name: Proof of Cosimplicial categories with twisted action
nodes.statement: Denoting $\operatorname{Res}$ the restriction from ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ to $\Delta\{\mathfrak{G}_0\}$, we obtain a sequence of functors \[ {\Delta \mathfrak{G}} \overset{\text{Yoneda}}{\longrightarrow} {\mathcal Set}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}} \overset{\operatorname{Res^*}}{\longrightarrow} {\mathcal Set}_{\Delta \{ \mathfrak{G}_0 \}} \overset{\ref{prop:main}}{\longrightarrow} \mathfrak{G}_0-{\mathcal Set}_{\Delta} \overset{\operatorname{FC}}{\longrightarrow} \mathfrak{G}_0-{\EuScript Cat} \] whose composite is the desired functor.
nodes.statement_short: Compose Yoneda, restriction to $\Delta\{\mathfrak{G}_0\}$, Proposition 1.19 and the free category functor.

nodes.name: $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$-nerve
nodes.statement: Let ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ be any crossed simplicial group. Equip $\mathfrak{G}_0$ with its canonical parity. Then to each small category ${\EuScript C}$ with a twisted $\mathfrak{G}_0$-action, there is an associated ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-set $\operatorname{N}^{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}({\EuScript C})$ called the {\em ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-nerve} of ${\EuScript C}$ such that \[ \operatorname{N}^{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}({\EuScript C})_n = \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak{G}_0-{\EuScript Cat}}(\operatorname{FC}({\Delta \mathfrak{G}}^n_{|\Delta}), {\EuScript C}). \]
nodes.statement_short: A category with twisted $\mathfrak{G}_0$-action has a $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$-nerve whose $n$-simplices are twisted functors from $\operatorname{FC}(\Delta\mathfrak{G}^n)$.
assumptions: Let ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ be any crossed simplicial group.

nodes.name: Cyclic nerve
nodes.statement:
Let ${\EuScript C}$ be a small category. Its {\em cyclic nerve} is the simplicial set $\operatorname{NC}_\bullet{\EuScript C}$
  with $\operatorname{NC}_n{\EuScript C}$ being the set of diagrams
  \begin{equation} x_0\buildrel a_0\over  \longrightarrow x_1\buildrel a_1\over \longrightarrow \cdots\buildrel a_{n-1}\over \longrightarrow x_n
  \buildrel a_n\over \longrightarrow x_0. 
  \end{equation}

nodes.name: Simplices of the cyclic nerve
nodes.statement: x_0\buildrel a_0\over \longrightarrow x_1\buildrel a_1\over \longrightarrow \cdots\buildrel a_{n-1}\over \longrightarrow x_n \buildrel a_n\over \longrightarrow x_0.
nodes.label: eq:NC

nodes.name: Cyclic nerve is a cyclic set
nodes.statement: As i well-known, the cyclic rotation of such diagrams makes $\operatorname{NC}_\bullet{\EuScript C}$ into a cyclic set.

nodes.name: Dihedral structure on the cyclic nerve
nodes.statement:
Let $({\EuScript C},*)$ be a small category with  involution,
  which we write  as an isomorphism $*: {\EuScript C}\to{\EuScript C}^{\operatorname{op}}$, $**=\operatorname{Id}$.  Then $\operatorname{NC}_\bullet{\EuScript C}$ becomes a
  dihedral set, with the generator $\omega_n \in D_{n+1} = \operatorname{Aut}\nolimits \overline {\langle n \rangle}$ sending a diagram
  \eqref{eq:NC} into
  \[
 x_1^*\buildrel a_0^*\over\longrightarrow  x_0^*\buildrel a_n^*\over \longrightarrow x_{n}^*\buildrel a_{n-1}^*\over  \longrightarrow x_{n-1}^*
  \buildrel a_{n-2}^*\over \longrightarrow\cdots \buildrel a_2^*\over \longrightarrow x_2^* \buildrel a_1^*\over\longrightarrow x_1^*. 
  \]
assumptions: Let $({\EuScript C},*)$ be a small category with  involution

nodes.name: Twisted cyclic nerve
nodes.statement:
Let ${\EuScript C}$ be a category equipped with a (covariant) automorphism
  $F$. We have then the {\em twisted cyclic nerve} $\operatorname{NC}^F_\bullet{\EuScript C}$, see \cite{HSS1}. This is a simplicial set
  whose $n$-simplices are diagrams
 \begin{equation} x_0\buildrel a_0\over  \longrightarrow x_1\buildrel a_1\over \longrightarrow \cdots 
  \buildrel a_{n-1}\over \longrightarrow x_n
  \buildrel a_n\over \longrightarrow F(x_0). 
  \end{equation}

nodes.name: Simplices of the twisted cyclic nerve
nodes.statement: x_0\buildrel a_0\over \longrightarrow x_1\buildrel a_1\over \longrightarrow \cdots \buildrel a_{n-1}\over \longrightarrow x_n \buildrel a_n\over \longrightarrow F(x_0).
nodes.label: eq:NC^F

nodes.name: Twisted rotation $\tau_n$
Twisted cyclic rotation
nodes.statement: F^{-1}(x_n) \buildrel F^{-1}(a_n)\over\longrightarrow x_0 \buildrel a_0\over \longrightarrow x_1\buildrel a_1\over \longrightarrow \cdots \buildrel a_{n-2}\over\longrightarrow x_{n-1} \buildrel a_{n-1}\over \longrightarrow x_n = F(F^{-1}(x_n)).
nodes.label: eq:tau-twisted

nodes.name: Twisted cyclic nerve is paracyclic
nodes.statement:
One sees directly that the $\tau_n$ make $\operatorname{NC}^F_\bullet {\EuScript C}$ into a paracyclic set. 
   If $F^N=\operatorname{Id} $ for some $N$, then  
   $\tau_n^{N(n+1)}=\operatorname{Id}$ as well, and so $\operatorname{NC}^F_\bullet {\EuScript C}$ is an  $N$-cyclic set.
assumptions: If $F^N=\operatorname{Id} $ for some $N$

conclusions: One sees directly that the $\tau_n$ make $\operatorname{NC}^F_\bullet {\EuScript C}$ into a paracyclic set.

nodes.name: Twisted loop space
nodes.statement:
The twisted cyclic nerve is the categorical analog of the {\em twisted loop space} $L^F X$
   associated to a topological space $X$ together with a homeomorphism $F: X\to X$. 
   Explicitly, $L^F X$ consists of continuous maps $\gamma: \mathbb{R}\to X$ such that $\gamma(t+1)= F(\gamma(t))$.

nodes.name: Quaternionic structure on the twisted cyclic nerve
nodes.statement:
More precisely, let ${\EuScript C}$ be a category and $J: {\EuScript C}\to {\EuScript C}$ be a contravariant functor such that $J^4=\operatorname{Id}$. 
  Consider the 2-cyclic set $\operatorname{NC}^{J^2}_\bullet{\EuScript C}$. Define $w=w_n: \operatorname{NC}^{J^2}_n{\EuScript C}\to \operatorname{NC}^{J^2}_n{\EuScript C}$
  by
  \[
  \begin{gathered}
  w_n \bigl\{   x_0\buildrel a_0\over  \longrightarrow x_1\buildrel a_1\over \longrightarrow \cdots 
  \buildrel a_{n-1}\over \longrightarrow x_n
  \buildrel a_n\over \longrightarrow J^2 x_0\bigr\} = 
  \\
  \bigl\{ J^{-1}x_1 \buildrel J^{-1}(a_0)\over\longrightarrow
  J^{-1}(x_0)\buildrel J(a_n)\over\longrightarrow J(x_n)
  \buildrel J(a_{n-1}) \over\longrightarrow 
  J(x_{n-1})\buildrel J(a_{n-2})\over\longrightarrow\cdots
  \buildrel J(a_1)\over
  \longrightarrow J(x_1)= J^2(J^{-1}x_1)   \bigr\} .
    \end{gathered}
  \]
  (Note that the source of $J(a_n)$ is $J(J^2x_0) = J^{-1}x_0$.)
   Then $w_n$ together with $\tau_n$ defined as in \eqref{eq:tau-twisted}, define an action of
  $Q_{n+1}$ on $\operatorname{NC}^{J^2}_n{\EuScript C}$. One verifies that in this way $\operatorname{NC}^{J^2}_\bullet{\EuScript C}$
 becomes a quaternionic set.
assumptions: be a contravariant functor such that $J^4=\operatorname{Id}$.

nodes.name: $N$-dihedral structure on the twisted cyclic nerve
nodes.statement:
Let ${\EuScript C}$ be a category with a twisted action of $D_N$, i.e.,
 with a contravariant functor $\Omega: {\EuScript C}\to {\EuScript C}$ and a covariant functor $T: {\EuScript C}\to{\EuScript C}$ satisfying the relations
 of $D_N$. In particular, $T^N=\operatorname{Id}$,  so we have an $N$-cyclic set $\operatorname{NC}^T_\bullet{\EuScript C}$. 
 For a given $n$, the set $\operatorname{NC}_n^T{\EuScript C}$ is acted upon by the transformation $\tau_n$ as in
 \eqref{eq:tau-twisted} and $\omega_n$ which takes an $n$-simplex 
 \[
  x_0\buildrel a_0\over  \longrightarrow x_1\buildrel a_1\over \longrightarrow \cdots 
  \buildrel a_{n-1}\over \longrightarrow x_n
  \buildrel a_n\over \longrightarrow T(x_0) 
 \]
 into 
 \[
 \Omega (x_1) \buildrel \Omega(a_0)\over\longrightarrow \Omega (x_0) 
 \buildrel T\Omega (a_n)\over\longrightarrow T\Omega(x_n) 
 \buildrel T\Omega (a_{n-1})\over\longrightarrow T\Omega(x_{n-1}) 
 \buildrel T\Omega (a_{n-1})\over\longrightarrow \cdots
 \buildrel T\Omega (a_1)\over\longrightarrow T\Omega(x_1).
  \]
  Note that by the  dihedral relations
  we can write the source of $\Omega(a_n)$ as $\Omega T x_0 = T^{-1}\Omega x_0$, so
  $T\Omega (a_n): \Omega x_0\to T\Omega x_n$.
  The maps $\tau_n$ and $\omega_n$ satisfy the relations of $D_{N(n+1)}$
  and one checks directly that in this way $\operatorname{NC}^T_\bullet{\EuScript C}$ becomes an $N$-dihedral
  set.
assumptions: Let ${\EuScript C}$ be a category with a twisted action of $D_N$

nodes.name: $N$-quaternionic structure on the twisted cyclic nerve
nodes.statement:
Let ${\EuScript C}$ be a category with a twisted action of $Q_N$, i.e.,
 with a contravariant functor $W: {\EuScript C}\to {\EuScript C}$ and a covariant functor $T:{\EuScript C}\to{\EuScript C}$,
    satisfying the relations
 of $Q_N$. Then $T^{2N}=\operatorname{Id}$,  so we have
 the $2N$-cyclic set $\operatorname{NC}^{T}_\bullet{\EuScript C}$. We define the action of $Q_{N(n+1)}$
 on $\operatorname{NC}^{T}_n{\EuScript C}$ by transformations $\tau_n$, defined  as in \eqref{eq:tau-twisted},
 and $w_n$ which takes a simplex
 \[
  x_0\buildrel a_0\over  \longrightarrow x_1\buildrel a_1\over \longrightarrow \cdots 
  \buildrel a_{n-1}\over \longrightarrow x_n
  \buildrel a_n\over \longrightarrow T(x_0) 
 \]
 into  
 \[
 W(x_1)\buildrel W(a_0))\over\longrightarrow W(x_0) \buildrel TW(a_n)\over\longrightarrow TW (x_n)\buildrel TW(a_{n-1})\over\longrightarrow
 TW(x_{n-1})\longrightarrow\cdots \buildrel TW(a_1)\over\longrightarrow TW( x_1). 
 \]
As before, the identity $WTW^{-1}=T^{-1}$ implies  that $TW(a_n)$ acts from $W(x_0)$ to $TW(x_n)$. 
The relations of the quaternionic group $Q_{N(n+1)}$ and the compatibility of the actions of the $Q_{N(n+1)}$, $n\geq 0$
and of $\Delta$ are verified directly.
assumptions: Let ${\EuScript C}$ be a category with a twisted action of $Q_N$

nodes.name: $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$-structure on the Hochschild complex
nodes.statement: Let ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ be a planar crossed simplicial group. Let $A$ be a unital associative algebra with a twisted action of $\mathfrak{G}_0$. Then the collection of vector spaces \[ C_\bullet(A) = \bigl\{ C_n(A) = A^{\otimes (n+1)}\bigr\}_{n\geq 0}, \] given by the terms of the Hochschild complex of $A$, naturally forms a $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$-vector space. In particular, the group $\mathfrak{G}_n$ acts on $C_n(A)$.
nodes.statement_short: For planar $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$ and an algebra with twisted $\mathfrak{G}_0$-action, the Hochschild terms $A^{\otimes(n+1)}$ form a $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$-vector space.
assumptions: Let ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ be a planar crossed simplicial group.

nodes.name: Proof of $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$-structure on the Hochschild complex
nodes.statement: The cosimplicial structure is obtained by letting face maps act by insertion of $1$ and degeneracy maps act by multiplication in $A$. Let us construct an action of $\mathfrak{G}_n$ on $A^{\otimes (n+1)}$. Consider the wreath product \[ S_{n+1}\wr \mathfrak{G}_0 := S_{n+1}\ltimes \mathfrak{G}_0^{n+1}, \] where the action of $S_{n+1}$ on $\mathfrak{G}_0^{n+1}$ is by permuting the Cartesian factors. Note that we have a projection map $S_{n+1}\wr\mathfrak{G}_0 \to S_{n+1}$. We now claim that the homomorphism $\lambda_n: \mathfrak{G}_n\to S_{n+1}$ from Proposition \ref{prop:forget} has a natural lifting to a homomorphism \[ L_n: \mathfrak{G}_n \longrightarrow S_{n+1}\wr \mathfrak{G}_0. \] Indeed, by the canonical factorization \[ \operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}([0], [n]) = \mathfrak{G}_0 \times\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([0], [n]), \] and $\mathfrak{G}_n$ acts on this set on the left by composition of morphisms in ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$. We see, first, that the action of any $g\in\mathfrak{G}_n$ takes any fiber of the projection to $\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([0], [n])$ to another fiber. The induced permutation of these fibers is precisely $\lambda_n(g)\in S_{n+1}$. Second, if we identify each fiber with $\mathfrak{G}_0$, then the identification of one fiber with another is given by the left multiplication with some element of $\mathfrak{G}_0$, These elements, together with $\lambda_n(g)$, give the desired $L_n(g)\in S_{n+1}\wr \mathfrak{G}_0$. Since $\mathfrak{G}_0$ acts on $A$ as a vector space, we have the natural action of $S_{n+1}\wr\mathfrak{G}_0$ on $A^{\otimes(n+1)}$ which combines the permutations of the tensor factors and action of $\mathfrak{G}_0$ on each factor. We pull this action back along $L_n$ to get a $\mathfrak{G}_n$-action on $A^{\otimes(n+1)}$. The compatibility of these actions with the simplicial structure is verified straightforwardly.
nodes.statement_short: Lift $\lambda_n$ to $L_n:\mathfrak{G}_n\to S_{n+1}\wr\mathfrak{G}_0$ using canonical factorization of $\operatorname{Hom}([0],[n])$, then pull back the wreath product action on $A^{\otimes(n+1)}$.

nodes.statement:
We now claim that the
homomorphism $\lambda_n: \mathfrak{G}_n\to S_{n+1}$ from Proposition \ref{prop:forget} has a natural lifting
to a homomorphism
\[
L_n: \mathfrak{G}_n \longrightarrow S_{n+1}\wr \mathfrak{G}_0. 
\]
Indeed, by the canonical factorization
\[
\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}([0], [n]) = \mathfrak{G}_0 \times\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([0], [n]),
\]
and $\mathfrak{G}_n$ acts on this set on the left by composition of morphisms in ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$.  We see, first,
that the action of any $g\in\mathfrak{G}_n$ takes any fiber of the projection to $\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([0], [n])$ to
another fiber. The induced permutation of these fibers is precisely $\lambda_n(g)\in S_{n+1}$.
Second, if we identify each fiber with $\mathfrak{G}_0$, then the identification of one fiber with another
is given by the left multiplication with some element of $\mathfrak{G}_0$, These elements, together with
$\lambda_n(g)$, give the desired $L_n(g)\in S_{n+1}\wr \mathfrak{G}_0$.

Indeed, by the canonical factorization
\[

\]
and $\mathfrak{G}_n$ acts on this set on the left by composition of morphisms in ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$.

We see, first,
that the action of any $g\in\mathfrak{G}_n$ takes any fiber of the projection to $\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([0], [n])$ to
another fiber. The induced permutation of these fibers is precisely $\lambda_n(g)\in S_{n+1}$.

nodes.statement:
Second, if we identify each fiber with $\mathfrak{G}_0$, then the identification of one fiber with another

nodes.name: Pull back the wreath product action along $L_n$.
nodes.statement:
Since $\mathfrak{G}_0$ acts on $A$ as a vector space, we have the natural action of $S_{n+1}\wr\mathfrak{G}_0$ on

The compatibility of these actions with the simplicial structure is verified straightforwardly.
