a partially ordered set $(S,\leq)$ and an  morphism of partially ordered set $F: S\to S$.

nodes.name: Partial paracyclic order
nodes.statement: A {\em partial paracyclic order} on a set $J$ is a datum of: \begin{enumerate} \item a $\mathbb{Z}$-ordered set $(\widetilde J, F)$ such that $F$ is a fixed point-free bijection. We denote by $F^{\mathbb{Z}}$ the group of automorphisms of $S$ generated by $F$. \item A bijection $\widetilde J/F^{\mathbb{Z}}\to J$. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Paracyclic order on lattices
nodes.statement: (Cf. \cite{HSS1}, Ex. 3.1.5) Let $\mathbf{k}$ be a discrete valued field with the ring of integers $\mathfrak o$ and uniformizing element $\varpi$. Then the set $B=GL(n, \mathbf{k})/GL(n, \mathfrak{o})$ is identified with the set of $\mathfrak o$-lattices $L\subset \mathbf{k}^n$, so it is partially ordered by inclusion of lattices. The automorphism $F$ given by multiplication of (matrices or lattices) by the scalar matrix $\varpi$, makes $B$ into a $\mathbb{Z}$-ordered set. The quotient \[ B/\varpi^{\mathbb{Z}} \,\,=\,\, PGL(n, \mathbf{k})/PGL(n, \mathfrak{o}) \] has therefore a canonical (partial) paracyclic order.

nodes.name: Point paracyclic set
nodes.statement:
We denote by $\operatorname{pt}\nolimits$ the set $\{0\}$ equipped with the paracyclic order given by the trivial
$\mathbb{Z}$-torsor.

nodes.name: Paracyclic dual $J^\vee$
nodes.statement:
Given a finite nonempty paracyclically ordered set $(J, \widetilde{J})$, 
consider the set $\widetilde{J^{\vee}} := \operatorname{Hom}_{\bf \Lambda_{\infty}}(J, \operatorname{pt}\nolimits)$ and define $J^{\vee}$
to be the orbit set under the translation action of $\mathbb{Z}$ on $\operatorname{pt}\nolimits$. We can equip
$\widetilde{J^{\vee}}$ with the $\mathbb{Z}$-action given by pulling back the translation action on $J$.

nodes.name: Paracyclic dual is paracyclically ordered
nodes.statement:
It is straightforward to verify that $\widetilde{J^{\vee}}$ is a $\mathbb{Z}$-torsor and the projection map
$\widetilde{J^{\vee}} \to J^{\vee}$ defines a paracyclic order on $J^{\vee}$.

nodes.name: Interstices for paracyclic orders
nodes.statement: Let $J \subset S^1$ and consider the paracyclic order $\pi^{-1}(J) \to J$ on $J$ induced from the universal cover map $\pi: \mathbb{R} \to S^1$ (corresponding to the base point $1\in S^1$. Then we can identify $\operatorname{Hom}_{\bf \Lambda_{\infty}}(J, \operatorname{pt}\nolimits)$ with homotopy classes of monotone maps $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ which \begin{enumerate} \item map the subset $\widetilde{J} \subset \mathbb{R}$ to the subset $\mathbb{Z} \subset \mathbb{R}$, \item are equivariant with respect to translation by $|J|$ on $\widetilde{J}$ and translation by $1$ on $\mathbb{Z}$. \end{enumerate} Any such homotopy class is uniquely determined by specifying the interstice $[\widetilde{j},\widetilde{j}+1]$ of $\widetilde{J} \subset \mathbb{R}$ which maps onto the interstice $[0,1]$ of $\mathbb{Z} \subset \mathbb{R}$. Thus the set $\widetilde{J^{\vee}}$ can be naturally identified with the set of interstices of $\widetilde{J} \subset \mathbb{R}$. The quotient $J^{\vee}$ can therefore be canonically identified with the set of interstices of $J \subset S^1$.

nodes.name: Paracyclic interstice duality
nodes.statement: The interstice construction $J \mapsto J^{\vee}$ extends to a functor \[ ({\bf \Lambda_{\infty}})^{{\operatorname{op}}} \longrightarrow {\bf \Lambda_{\infty}} \] which is an equivalence of categories. \qed
conclusions: which is an equivalence of categories.

nodes.name: Thick group $\mathbb{G}$
nodes.statement:
Let $p:G\to O(2)$ be a planar Lie group, and $\mathbbm{p}: \mathbb{G}=G^\diamond \to GL(2, \mathbb{R})$
the connective covering extending $p$.

nodes.name: Kernel $K$
nodes.statement: We denote $K=\operatorname{Ker}\nolimits(p)=\operatorname{Ker}\nolimits(\mathbbm{p})$.

nodes.name: $K$ is abelian
nodes.statement:
As the kernel of a connective
covering, the group $K$ is abelian.

nodes.name: Orientation preserving $\mathbb{G}$
nodes.statement:
We say that $\mathbb{G}$ {\em preserves
orientation} if $\mathbbm{p}(\mathbb{G})\subset GL^+(2,\mathbb{R})$.

nodes.name: Exact sequences for $K$
Short exact sequences for $K$
nodes.statement: \begin{gathered} 0\to K\longrightarrow \mathbb{G} \longrightarrow GL^+(2,\mathbb{R})\to 1, \\ 0\to K\longrightarrow \mathbb{G} \longrightarrow GL(2,\mathbb{R})\to 1. \end{gathered}
nodes.label: eq:group-K

nodes.name: Conjugation action on $K$
nodes.statement:
In the first case, $K$ lies in the center of $\mathbb{G}$. In the second case, the action of $\mathbb{G}$ on $K$
by conjugation factors through an action of $\pi_0(GL(2,\mathbb{R}))= \{1, \tau\}$ given by an involution
$\tau:K\to K$.

nodes.name: Kernels of planar groups
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate} \item[(a)] Let ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ be the crossed simplicial group corresponding to $\mathbb{G}$. Then $K=\operatorname{Ker}\nolimits\{\rho: \mathfrak{G}_0\to \mathbb{Z}/2\}$. \item[(b)] The kernels corresponding to the various planar groups are given by:\\ \begin{tabular}{ p{1cm} || p{2cm}| p{2cm}| p{2cm}|p{2cm}|p{2cm}} $G$& $\operatorname{Spin}_N(2)$& $\widetilde{SO(2)}$ & $\operatorname{Pin}^+_N(2)$ & $\widetilde {O(2)}$& $\operatorname{Pin}^-_{2M}(2)$ \\ \hline $K$ & $\mathbb{Z}/N$ & $\mathbb{Z}$ & $\mathbb{Z}/N$ & $\mathbb{Z}$ & $\mathbb{Z}/2M$ \end{tabular}\\ If $G$ does not preserve orientation then $\tau$ acts on $K$ by $\tau(k)=-k$. \end{enumerate}
assumptions: Let ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ be the crossed simplicial group corresponding to $\mathbb{G}$.
nodes.label: prop:group-K

nodes.name: Proof of Kernels of planar groups
nodes.statement: Follows from Proposition \ref{prop:orient-G-0} (a) and (b) respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Follows from Proposition 1.34 (a),(b).

nodes.name: Surface
nodes.statement:
By a {\em surface} we will mean a  connected $C^\infty$-surface $S$ possibly with boundary
$\partial S$.

nodes.name: Frame bundle $\operatorname{Fr}_S$
nodes.statement:
Given a surface $S$, let $\operatorname{Fr}_S\to S$ be the principal $GL(2,\mathbb{R})$-bundle of frames in
the tangent bundle $T_S$.

nodes.name: Orientation torsor
nodes.statement:
The sheaf of connected components $\underline{\pi}_0(\operatorname{Fr}_S)$ is a
$\mathbb{Z}/2$-torsor over $S$ which we call the {\em orientation torsor} of $S$ and denote by ${\operatorname{or}}_S$.

nodes.name: Orientation cover
nodes.statement:
Thus
the total space of ${\operatorname{or}}_S$ is the orientation cover of $S$, denoted $\widetilde S$.

nodes.name: Local system $\underline K^{or}$
nodes.statement:
Suppose $\mathbb{G}$ does not preserve orientation. In this case, the $GL(2,\mathbb{R})$-action on $K$ from
\eqref {eq:group-K} together with the $GL(2,\mathbb{R})$-torsor $\operatorname{Fr}_S\to S$,  gives rise to a local
system of abelian groups $\underline K^{\operatorname{or}}$ on $S$, locally isomorphic to $\underline{K}$. If $S$
is orientable, then $\underline K^{\operatorname{or}} \cong \underline K$ is a constant sheaf.

nodes.name: $\mathbb{G}$-structured surface
nodes.statement: A $\mathbb{G}$-structured surface is a datum $(S,F)$, where $S$ is a surface, and $F\buildrel\rho\over\to \operatorname{Fr}_S$ is a reduction of structure groups along $\mathbbm{p}$.

nodes.name: Examples of $\mathbb{G}$-structures; framings and $N$-spin structures
nodes.statement: We give examples using the notation of Table \ref{table:corr}. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph{*})] \item For $G=O(2)$, we have $\mathbb{G}=GL(2,\mathbb{R})$, and a $\mathbb{G}$-structured surface is just a surface with no additional structure. \item For $G=SO(2)$, we have $\mathbb{G}=GL^+(2,\mathbb{R})$, and a $\mathbb{G}$-structure on $S$ is the same as an orientation of $S$. \item For $G=\operatorname{Spin}_N(2)$, the group $\mathbb{G}$ is the $N$-fold connected covering of $GL^+(2,\mathbb{R})$, and a $\mathbb{G}$-structure is known as an $N$-{\em spin structure}. The case $N=2$, being an instance of the spinor construction existing in any number of dimensions, has been studied more systematically, cf. \cite{johnson}. \item For the unversal covering $G=\widetilde{SO(2)}$ of $SO(2)$, the group $\mathbb{G}=\widetilde{GL^+(2,\mathbb{R})}$ is the universal covering of $GL(2,\mathbb{R})$. A $\widetilde{GL^+(2,\mathbb{R})}$-structure on a surface will be called a {\em framing}. Note that, in our definition, a framing on $S$ is a discrete datum: not an actual choice of a trivialization of $T_S$ but what amounts to an isotopy class of such trivializations. In fact, the same is true in all the other cases, and this is the reason for working with $\mathbb{G}$ instead of $G$. For instance, an $O(2)$-structure on $S$ is a Riemannian metric, while a $GL(2,\mathbb{R})$-structure is no extra structure at all. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Structured diffeomorphism
nodes.statement:
A {\em structured diffeomorphism} of $\mathbb{G}$-structured surfaces $(S,F)\to (S', F')$ is a pair
$(\phi,\widetilde \phi)$ where $\phi: S\to S'$ is a diffeomorphism, and $\widetilde\phi: F\to F'$
is a $\mathbb{G}$-equivariant diffeomorphism lifting $d\phi: \operatorname{Fr}_S\to\operatorname{Fr}_{S'}$.

nodes.name: Isomorphism of $\mathbb{G}$-structures
nodes.statement:
A structured diffeomorphism
$(S,F) \to (S,F')$ with $\phi=\operatorname{Id}\nolimits$ will be called an {\em isomorphism of $\mathbb{G}$-structures} on $S$.

nodes.name: Groupoid $\mathbb{G}\operatorname{Str}(S)$
nodes.statement: We denote by $\mathbb{G}\operatorname{Str}(S)$ the groupoid formed by $\mathbb{G}$-structures on $S$ and their isomorphisms.

nodes.name: Orientation-preserving structures induce orientations
nodes.statement: Suppose $\mathbb{G}$ preserves orientation. Then any $\mathbb{G}$-structure on $S$ gives rise to an orientation.
assumptions: Suppose $\mathbb{G}$ preserves orientation.

nodes.name: Groupoid $\mathbb{G}\operatorname{Str}^+(S)$
nodes.statement:
Given an oriented surface $S$, we denote by $\mathbb{G}\operatorname{Str}^+(S)$ the full subcategory in $\mathbb{G}\operatorname{Str}(S)$ formed
by those $\mathbb{G}$-structures which induce the given orientation.

nodes.name: Sheaf $\underline L$
nodes.statement:
For a Lie group $L$, let $\underline {L}$ be the sheaf of
groups on $S$ formed by local $C^\infty$-maps into $L$. Thus, the pointed set $H^1(S,\underline L)$ is the set of
isomorphism classes of principal $L$-bundles on $S$.

nodes.name: Classification of $\mathbb{G}$-structures by nonabelian cohomology
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate} \item[(a)] Suppose $\mathbb{G}$ preserves orientation, and let $S$ be an oriented surface. Then: \begin{enumerate} \item[(a1)] For any object $F\in\mathbb{G}\operatorname{Str}^+(S)$, the group $\operatorname{Aut}\nolimits(F)$ is identified with $K$. \item[(a2)] The set of isomorphism classes of objects of $\mathbb{G}\operatorname{Str}^+(S)$ is either empty or a torsor over $H^1(S,K)$. \end{enumerate} \item[(b)] Suppose $\mathbb{G}$ does not preserve orientation, and let $S$ be any surface. Then: \begin{enumerate} \item[(b1)] For any object $F\in\mathbb{G}\operatorname{Str}(S)$, the group $\operatorname{Aut}\nolimits(F)$ is identified with $H^0(S, \underline K^{\operatorname{or}})$. \item[(b2)] The set of isomorphism classes of objects of $\mathbb{G}\operatorname{Str}(S)$ is either empty, or is a torsor over $H^1(S,\underline K^{\operatorname{or}})$. \item[(b3)] The group $H^0(S, \underline K^{\operatorname{or}})$ is identified with $K$, if $S$ is orientable, and with the 2-torsion subgroup $K_2\subset K$, if $S$ is non-orientable. \end{enumerate} \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Automorphisms of a $\mathbb{G}$-structure form $K$ (or $H^0$ of the twisted local system) and isomorphism classes form a torsor over $H^1$.
assumptions: Suppose $\mathbb{G}$ preserves orientation, and let $S$ be an oriented surface.
Suppose $\mathbb{G}$ does not preserve orientation, and let $S$

nodes.label: prop:G-structures

nodes.name: Proof of Classification of $\mathbb{G}$-structures by nonabelian cohomology
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and \[ 0\to A\longrightarrow\Gamma'\buildrel\pi\over\longrightarrow \Gamma\to 1 \] be an extension of sheaves of groups on $X$ with abelian kernel $A$. Let $P$ be a sheaf of $\Gamma$-torsors on $X$, with associated class $[P]\in H^1(X, \Gamma)$. In this situation, the $\Gamma$-action on $A$ by conjugation gives rise to the twisted form $A^P$, a sheaf of abelian groups on $X$ locally isomorphic to $A$. Denote by $\operatorname{Lift}(P)$ the category formed by sheaves $P'$ of $\Gamma'$-torsors on $X$ together with a $\pi$-equivariant map $\pi_{P'}: P'\to P$. Morphisms in $\operatorname{Lift}(P)$ are isomorphisms of torsors commuting with the projection to $P$. In the described situation, we have: \begin{enumerate} \item[(i)] Each group $\operatorname{Aut}\nolimits_{\operatorname{Lift}(P)}(P')$ is identified with $H^0(X, A^P)$. \item[(ii)] The set of isomorphism classes of objects of $\operatorname{Lift}(P)$ is either empty or is a torsor over $H^1(X, A^P)$. \item[(iii)] If $A$ is central, then there is a natural coboundary map of pointed sets $\delta: H^1(X,\Gamma)\to H^2(X, A)$. In this case $\operatorname{Lift}(P)\neq\emptyset$ if and only if $\delta([P])=0$. \end{enumerate} Now, parts (a1-2) and (b1-2) follow by considering the extensions of sheaves on $S$ obtained from \eqref{eq:group-K} by passing to sheaves of $C^\infty$-sections. Part (b3) follows from Proposition \ref{prop:group-K}(b).
nodes.statement_short: General facts on lifting torsors along extensions with abelian kernel, applied to the extensions of sheaves from the sequences for $K$.

nodes.name: Recall nonabelian cohomology facts on lifts of torsors.
nodes.statement:
Let $X$ be a topological space
and
\[
0\to A\longrightarrow\Gamma'\buildrel\pi\over\longrightarrow \Gamma\to 1
\]
be an extension of sheaves of groups on $X$ with abelian kernel $A$. Let $P$ be a sheaf of $\Gamma$-torsors
on $X$, with associated class $[P]\in H^1(X, \Gamma)$.
 In this situation, the $\Gamma$-action on $A$ by conjugation gives rise to the twisted form
$A^P$, a sheaf of abelian groups on $X$ locally isomorphic to $A$. Denote by $\operatorname{Lift}(P)$ the category
formed by sheaves $P'$ of $\Gamma'$-torsors on $X$ together with a $\pi$-equivariant 
map $\pi_{P'}: P'\to P$. Morphisms in $\operatorname{Lift}(P)$ are isomorphisms of torsors
commuting with the projection to $P$. 
In the described situation, we have:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] Each group $\operatorname{Aut}\nolimits_{\operatorname{Lift}(P)}(P')$ is identified with $H^0(X, A^P)$.

\item[(ii)] The set of isomorphism classes of objects of $\operatorname{Lift}(P)$ is either empty or is
a torsor over $H^1(X, A^P)$.

\item[(iii)] If $A$ is central, then there is a natural coboundary map of pointed sets
$\delta: H^1(X,\Gamma)\to H^2(X, A)$.
In this case $\operatorname{Lift}(P)\neq\emptyset$ if and only if $\delta([P])=0$. 
\end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Recall nonabelian cohomology facts on lifts of torsors.

nodes.name: Apply to sheaves of sections of the sequences for $K$.
nodes.statement:
Now, parts (a1-2) and (b1-2) follow by considering the extensions of sheaves
on $S$ obtained from \eqref{eq:group-K} by passing to sheaves of $C^\infty$-sections. Part (b3) follows from
Proposition \ref{prop:group-K}(b).
nodes.statement_short: Apply to sheaves of sections of the sequences for $K$.

nodes.name: Existence of $N$-spin structures
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be an oriented surface and $G=\operatorname{Spin}_N(2)$. If $S$ is noncompact or has nonempty boundary then we have $H^2(S,K) = 0$ so that $\mathbb{G}\operatorname{Str}^+(S)$ is nonempty. If $S$ is compact without boundary, then $\mathbb{G}\operatorname{Str}^+(S)$ is nonempty for $N=2$. This follows by considering the inclusion of short exact sequences of sheaves of groups \begin{equation} \xymatrix{ 0\ar[r]& \underline{\mathbb{Z}/2}\ar[r]\ar[d]^{=}&\underline{S}^1\ar[d] \ar[r]^{z \mapsto z^2} & \underline{S}^1\ar[d]\ar[r] & 1 \\ 0\ar[r]& \underline{\mathbb{Z}/2}\ar[r]&\underline{\widetilde {GL^+(2,\mathbb{R})}_2}\ar[r] & \underline {GL^+(2,\mathbb{R})}\ar[r] & 1 } \end{equation} where $S^1=SO(2)$. Choosing a Riemannian metric on $S$, we reduce the structure group to $S^1$ and so realize $[\operatorname{Fr}_S]$ as coming from an element of $H^1(S, \underline{S}^1)$. The coboundary map $\delta_{S^1}: H^1(S, \underline S^1)\to H^2(S, \mathbb{Z}/2) \cong \mathbb{Z}/2$ is given by the degree modulo $2$. Since the tangent bundle of a surface of genus $g$ has degree $2g -2$, we have $\delta_{S^1}([\operatorname{Fr}_S]) = 0$.

nodes.name: Comparison of exact sequences of sheaves
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ 0\ar[r]& \underline{\mathbb{Z}/2}\ar[r]\ar[d]^{=}&\underline{S}^1\ar[d] \ar[r]^{z \mapsto z^2} & \underline{S}^1\ar[d]\ar[r] & 1 \\ 0\ar[r]& \underline{\mathbb{Z}/2}\ar[r]&\underline{\widetilde {GL^+(2,\mathbb{R})}_2}\ar[r] & \underline {GL^+(2,\mathbb{R})}\ar[r] & 1 }
nodes.label: eq;two-seq

nodes.name: $\mathbb{G}$-structured marked surface
nodes.statement: A {\em $\mathbb{G}$-structured marked surface} is a datum consisting of: \begin{enumerate} \item[(1)] A compact surface $S$ (possibly with boundary). We denote $S^\circ= S-\partial S$ the interior of $S$. \item[(2)] A finite subset $M\subset S$. \item[(3)] A $\mathbb{G}$-structure $F$ on $S-(M\cap S^\circ)$. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Structured diffeomorphism of marked surfaces
nodes.statement: Let $(S,M)$ and $(S', M')$ be two $\mathbb{G}$-structured marked surfaces, with $\mathbb{G}$-structured torsors $F$ and $F'$ respectively. A {\em structured diffeomorphism} $(S,M)\to(S', M')$ is a datum consisting of: \begin{enumerate} \item[(1)] A diffeomoprhism $\phi: S\to S'$ taking $M$ to $M'$. \item[(2)] A structured diffeomorphism $\widetilde\phi: S-(M\cap S^\circ)\to S'- (M'\cap S'{}^\circ)$ lifting the restriction of $\phi$. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Structured diffeomorphism groups
nodes.statement:
For a $\mathbb{G}$-structured marked surface
	 $(S,M)$, we denote by $\operatorname{Diff}^{\mathbb{G}}(S,M)$ the group of $\mathbb{G}$-structured self-diffeomorphisms of $(S,M)$,
	 and by   $\operatorname{Diff}^{\mathbb{G}}_{\operatorname{pure}}(S,M)$ the subgroup of structured self-diffeomorphisms preserving $M$ pointwise. 
	  We consider
	 these groups as subgroups in the group of diffeomorphisms of the structure torsor $F$ and
	 equip them with the subspace topology.

nodes.name: Ordinary diffeomorphism groups and forgetful maps
nodes.statement:
For $\mathbb{G}=GL(2,\mathbb{R})$, we get the ordinary (pure) diffeomorphism group of the  marked surface $(S,M)$,
which we denote $\operatorname{Diff}(S,M)$ and $\operatorname{Diff}_{\operatorname{pure}}(S,M)$. Forgetting the $\mathbb{G}$-structured data gives
morphisms of topological groups
\[
\begin{gathered}
	\pi: \operatorname{Diff}^{\mathbb{G}}(S,M) \longrightarrow\operatorname{Diff}(S,M), 
	\\
	\pi_{\operatorname{pure}}: \operatorname{Diff}_{\operatorname{pure}}^{\mathbb{G}}(S,M) \longrightarrow\operatorname{Diff}_{\operatorname{pure}}(S,M).  
\end{gathered}
\]

nodes.name: Structured diffeomorphisms form coverings
nodes.statement: The group $\operatorname{Ker}\nolimits(\pi)=\operatorname{Ker}\nolimits(\pi_{\operatorname{pure}})$ is a discrete abelian group, so that $\pi$ and $\pi_{\operatorname{pure}}$ are unramified coverings. Further, the groups $\operatorname{Im}(\pi)$ and $\operatorname{Im}(\pi_{\operatorname{pure}})$ are unions of connected components of $\operatorname{Diff}(S,M)$.
nodes.label: prop:str-non-str-diff

nodes.name: Proof of Structured diffeomorphisms form coverings
nodes.statement_short: Kernel is $\operatorname{Aut}(F)$, abelian by Prop. 3.4; image is a stabilizer of a discrete set, hence open and closed.

nodes.name: Kernel is $\operatorname{Aut}(F)$, abelian by Prop. 3.4.
nodes.statement_short: Kernel is $\operatorname{Aut}(F)$, abelian by Prop. 3.4.

nodes.name: Image is a stabilizer of a discrete set, hence open and closed.
nodes.statement:
Further, $\phi\in\operatorname{Diff}(S,M)$ lies
in $\operatorname{Im}(\pi)$ if and only if the $\mathbb{G}$-structure $\phi^*F$  on $S-(M\cap S^\circ)$  is isomorphic to $F$. So 
$\operatorname{Im}(\pi)$ is the stabilizer of the action of $\operatorname{Diff}(S,M)$ on the  set of
isomorphism classes of objects of $\mathbb{G}\operatorname{Str}(S-(M\cap S^\circ))$. This set was described in Proposition 
 \ref {prop:G-structures}  (a2)(b2), in particular, it is discrete. So $\operatorname{Im}(\pi)$ is open and
 closed, and similarly for $\operatorname{Im}(\pi_{\operatorname{pure}})$.
nodes.statement_short: Image is a stabilizer of a discrete set, hence open and closed.

nodes.name: Structured mapping class groups
nodes.statement: Let $(S,M)$ be a $\mathbb{G}$-structued marked surface. We define the $\mathbb{G}$-structured mapping class groups as \[ \operatorname{Mod}^{\mathbb{G}}(S,M) = \pi_0 \operatorname{Diff}^{\mathbb{G}}(S,M), \quad \operatorname{Mod}^{\mathbb{G}}_{\operatorname{pure}}(S,M) =\pi_0 \operatorname{Diff}_{\operatorname{pure}}^{\mathbb{G}}(S,M). \]

nodes.name: Schottky double
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be a compact $C^\infty$-surface with boundary $\partial S$, and $S^\circ = S-\partial S$. The {\em Schottky double} of $S$ is the compact oriented $C^\infty$ surface $S^\#$ without boundary obtained by compatifying $\widetilde{S^\circ}$, the orientation cover of $S^\circ$, by adding one copy of $\partial S$. Thus we have a 2-sheeted covering $\pi: S^\#\to S$, ramified along $\partial S$, and the deck involution $\sigma: S^\#\to S^\#$ of this covering, reversing the orientation and identical on $\partial S$. If $(S,M)$ is a marked surface, we equip $S^\#$ with the subset $M^\#=\pi^{-1}(M)$.

nodes.name: Classical surface
nodes.statement: \cite{seppala} A surface $S$ is called {\em classical}, if $S$ is orientable and $\partial S=\emptyset$, and {\em non-classical} otherwise.

nodes.name: Connectedness of the Schottky double
nodes.statement: Thus $S^\#$ is connected, if and only if $S$ is non-classical.
conclusions: $S^\#$ is connected, if and only if $S$ is non-classical.

nodes.name: Stable marked surface
nodes.statement: A marked surface $(S,M)$ is called {\em stable}, if: \begin{enumerate} \item[(1)] $M\neq\emptyset$ and moreover, $M$ meets each component of $\partial S$. \item[(2)] $\chi (S^\# - M^\#) < 0$. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Punctures
nodes.statement:
For a stable marked surface $(S,M)$ the points of $M$ lying in the interior of $S$, will be called
{\em punctures}.

nodes.name: Contractibility of components of $\operatorname{Diff}^{\mathbb{G}}(S,M)$
nodes.statement: If $(S,M)$ is a stable $\mathbb{G}$-structured marked surface, then each component of $\operatorname{Diff}^{\mathbb{G}}(S,M)$ is contractible.
assumptions: If $(S,M)$ is a stable $\mathbb{G}$-structured marked surface
nodes.label: prop:diff-contract

nodes.name: Proof of Contractibility of components of $\operatorname{Diff}^{\mathbb{G}}(S,M)$
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{prop:str-non-str-diff}, the statement reduces to the particular case of $\mathbb{G}=GL(2,\mathbb{R})$ where it translates to the contractibility of each component or, equivalently, of the identity component of $\operatorname{Diff}(S,M)$. This statement is shown in \cite{gramain}
nodes.statement_short: Reduce via Prop. 3.8 to the unstructured case, proved by Gramain.

nodes.name: Conformal group $\operatorname{Conf}(2)$
nodes.statement:
Let
\begin{equation} {\operatorname{Conf}}(2) = (\mathbb{Z}/2)\ltimes \mathbb{C}^* \subset GL(2, \mathbb{R})
\end{equation}
be the subgroup of conformal transformations.

nodes.name: Embedding of $\operatorname{Conf}(2)$
nodes.statement: {\operatorname{Conf}}(2) = (\mathbb{Z}/2)\ltimes \mathbb{C}^* \subset GL(2, \mathbb{R})
nodes.label: eq:emb-conf

nodes.name: Coverings of $\operatorname{Conf}(2)$ and $GL(2)$ agree
assumptions: Since the embedding \eqref{eq:emb-conf}

nodes.name: Conformal covering $G_{conf}$
nodes.statement:
We denote
\[
p_{\operatorname{conf}}: G_{\operatorname{conf}}\longrightarrow {\operatorname{Conf}}(2)
\]
the connective covering obtained by restricting $\mathbbm{p}$.

nodes.name: $G_{conf}$-structured surface
nodes.statement:
Similarly to  \S \ref{subsec:c-infty}, by a
$G_{\operatorname{conf}}$-{\em structured surface} we mean a surface $S$ together with a restriction of the structure
group of $\operatorname{Fr}_S$ to $G_{\operatorname{conf}}$. As before, such a structure is a datum of a principal $G_{\operatorname{conf}}$-bundle
$F_{\operatorname{conf}}$ together with a compatible $P_{\operatorname{conf}}$-equivariant map $F_{\operatorname{conf}}\to\operatorname{Fr}_S$.

nodes.name: Groupoid $G_{conf}\operatorname{Str}(S)$
nodes.statement:
The concepts of a structured diffeomorphism between two $G_{\operatorname{conf}}$-structured surfaces and of an isomorphism
between two $G_{\operatorname{conf}}$-structures on a given surface $S$ are defined entirely similar to 
\S \ref{subsec:c-infty}. In particular, we have a groupoid $G_{\operatorname{conf}}\operatorname{Str}(S)$ of $G_{\operatorname{conf}}$-structures on $S$
and their isomorphisms. If $\mathbb{G}$ preserves orientation and $S$ is oriented, we also have the full
subcategory $G_{\operatorname{conf}}\operatorname{Str}^+(S)$ of $G_{\operatorname{conf}}$-structures compatible with the orientation.

nodes.name: Riemann, spin and Klein surfaces
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph{*})] \item An $SO(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}$-structured surface is a {\em Riemann surface}, i.e., a 1-dimensional complex manifold $X$ possibly with boundary. More precisely, an isomorphism class of objects of $SO(2)_{\operatorname{conf}} \operatorname{Str}(S)$ is the same as an almost complex structure $J: T_S\to T_S$, $J^2=-1$, and the automorphism group of any object of $SO(2)_{\operatorname{conf}} \operatorname{Str}(S)$ is trivial. As well known, all almost complex structures in complex dimension $1$ are integrable. For a Riemann surface $X=(S,J)$ we denote by $\overline X = (S, -J)$ the {\em conjugate} Riemann surface. \item A $\operatorname{Spin}_N(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}$-structured surface is a triple $(X, \mathcal{L}, \phi)$ where $X$ is a Riemann surface, $\mathcal{L}$ is a line bundle on $X$, and $\phi: \mathcal{L}^{\otimes N}\to\omega_X$ is an isomorphism. Here $\omega_X$ is the canonical line bundle of $X$. For $N=2$, such line bundles $\mathcal{L}$ are traditionally called {\em theta-characteristics}, and a choice of $\mathcal{L}$ is often referred to as a ``spin structure" on $X$, cf. \cite{atiyah}. For ``higher spin structures" on Riemann surfaces ($N>2$), see \cite{jarvis}. \item An $O(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}$-structured surface is a {\em Klein surface}, i.e., a surface together with an atlas whose transition maps are conformal but do not necessarily preserve orientation. Such maps are called {\em dianalytic} (i.e., analytic or anti-analytic). Thus a Klein surface does not have to be orientable. See \cite{alling-greenleaf, braun} for more background. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Conformal structures split
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate} \item[(a)] For any surface $S$ we have a natural identification of groupoids \[ G_{\operatorname{conf}}\operatorname{Str}(S) \simeq \mathbb{G}\operatorname{Str}(S) \times O(2)_{\operatorname{conf}} \operatorname{Str}(S). \] \item[(b)] The automorphism group of any object of $O(2)_{\operatorname{conf}} \operatorname{Str}(S)$ is trivial. \end{enumerate}
conclusions: we have a natural identification of groupoids
The automorphism group of any object of $O(2)_{\operatorname{conf}} \operatorname{Str}(S)$ is trivial.
nodes.label: prop:prod-of-grpds

nodes.name: Proof of Conformal structures split
nodes.statement: (a) By definition, we have \[ G_{\operatorname{conf}} = \mathbb{G} \times_{GL(2,\mathbb{R})} O(2)_{{\operatorname{conf}}} \] where $O(2)_{{\operatorname{conf}}}={\operatorname{Conf}}(2)$. So given a $\mathbb{G}$-structure $F\to \operatorname{Fr}_S$ and an $O(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}$-structure $F^{O(2)}_{\operatorname{conf}} \to\operatorname{Fr}_S$, we obtain a $G_{\operatorname{conf}}$-structure by forming the fiber product \[ F_{\operatorname{conf}} \,\,=\,\, F\times_{\operatorname{Fr}_S} F^{O(2)}_{\operatorname{conf}} \] which is a principal $G_{\operatorname{conf}}$-bundle. We leave the remaining details to the reader. (b) Follows because $O(2)_{{\operatorname{conf}}}$ is a subgroup of $GL(2,\mathbb{R})$.
nodes.statement_short: $G_{conf}$ is a fiber product, so structures pair up; automorphisms are trivial since $O(2)_{conf}\subset GL(2)$.

nodes.name: Fiber product of structures.
nodes.statement:
(a) By definition, we have
\[
G_{\operatorname{conf}} = \mathbb{G} \times_{GL(2,\mathbb{R})} O(2)_{{\operatorname{conf}}}
\]
where $O(2)_{{\operatorname{conf}}}={\operatorname{Conf}}(2)$. So given a $\mathbb{G}$-structure $F\to \operatorname{Fr}_S$ and an $O(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}$-structure $F^{O(2)}_{\operatorname{conf}} \to\operatorname{Fr}_S$,
we obtain a $G_{\operatorname{conf}}$-structure by forming the fiber product
\[
F_{\operatorname{conf}} \,\,=\,\, F\times_{\operatorname{Fr}_S} F^{O(2)}_{\operatorname{conf}}
\]
which is a principal $G_{\operatorname{conf}}$-bundle. We leave the remaining details to the reader.
nodes.statement_short: Fiber product of structures.

nodes.name: Subgroup of $GL(2,\mathbb{R})$ gives trivial automorphisms.
nodes.statement: (b) Follows  because $O(2)_{{\operatorname{conf}}}$ is a subgroup of $GL(2,\mathbb{R})$.
nodes.statement_short: Subgroup of $GL(2,\mathbb{R})$ gives trivial automorphisms.

nodes.name: Complex structure on the orientation cover of a Klein surface
nodes.statement:
Let $X$ be a Klein surface, and $X^\circ=X-\partial X$. For each $x\in X^\circ$, there are exactly
two complex structures on $T_xX$ compatible with the given conformal structure. The set of all these
structures for all $x\in X^\circ$ is canonically identified with the orientation cover $\widetilde{X^\circ}$.
Thus $\widetilde{X^\circ}$ has a canonical complex structure, making in into a (possibly non-compact)
Riemann surface. Further, the complex structure on $\widetilde{X^\circ}$ extends naturally
to the Schottky double $X^\#= \widetilde{X^\circ}\sqcup \partial X$.
nodes.section: Klein surfaces and algebraic curves over $\mathbb{R}$
assumptions: Let $X$ be a Klein surface

nodes.name: Schottky double of a Riemann surface
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a Riemann surface. Then $X^\# = X\cup_{\partial X} \overline X$.
nodes.section: Klein surfaces and algebraic curves over $\mathbb{R}$

nodes.name: Schottky double is defined over $\mathbb{R}$
nodes.statement:
Thus $X^\#$, being a compact Riemann surface without boundary, can be considered as a smooth
projective algebraic curve over $\mathbb{C}$. Further, the canonical involution $\sigma: X^\#\to X^\#$ is
anti-holomorphic and makes $X^\#$ defined over $\mathbb{R}$, so that the real locus of $X^\#$ is
$X^\#(\mathbb{R})=\partial S$.
nodes.section: Klein surfaces and algebraic curves over $\mathbb{R}$

nodes.name: Klein surfaces and real algebraic curves
nodes.statement: The Schottky double construction establishes an equivalence between the following categories: \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] Non-classical Klein surfaces $X$. \item[(ii)] Pairs $(Y,\sigma)$ where $Y$ is a compact Riemann surface without boundary and $\sigma: Y\to Y$ is an anti-holomorphic involution. \item[(iii)] Smooth projective algebraic curves over $\mathbb{R}$. \qed \end{itemize}
nodes.section: Klein surfaces and algebraic curves over $\mathbb{R}$
conclusions: The Schottky double construction establishes an equivalence between the following categories:

nodes.name: Symmetric Riemann surface
nodes.statement: Pairs $(Y,\sigma)$ as in (ii) are known as {\em symmetric Riemann surfaces}.
nodes.section: Klein surfaces and algebraic curves over $\mathbb{R}$

nodes.name: Space $\operatorname{Riem}^+(S)$
nodes.statement:
We denote by $\operatorname{Riem}^+(S)$ the space of
all complex structures on $S$ compatible with the orientation.
nodes.section: Teichm\"uller spaces of marked Klein surfaces

nodes.name: Classical Teichmüller space
nodes.statement:
Let $\operatorname{Diff}(S,M)_e$ be the identity component of $\operatorname{Diff}(S,M)$. Diffeomorphisms in this component
preserve the orientation, so $\operatorname{Diff}(S,M)_e$ acts on $\operatorname{Riem}^+(S)$. The classical
{\em Teichm\"uller space} of $(S,M)$ is defined as the quotient
\[
\operatorname{Teich}^+(S,M) \,\,=\,\, \operatorname{Diff}(S,M)_e \backslash \operatorname{Riem}^+(S). 
\]
nodes.section: Teichm\"uller spaces of marked Klein surfaces

nodes.name: Classical Teichmüller theory
nodes.statement: Let $g$ be the genus of $S$ and suppose that $(S,M)$ is stable, i.e., $2g-2+|M|>0$. Then: \begin{enumerate} \item[(a)] $\operatorname{Teich}^+(S,M)$ has a natural structure of a complex manifold of dimension $3g-3+|M|$. As a $C^\infty$-manifold, it is diffeomorphic to Euclidean space. \item[(b)] Let $\sigma:S\to S$ be an orientation reversing involution preserving $M$ as a set. Conjugation with $\sigma$ defines an anti-holomorphic involution \[ \sigma_{\operatorname{Teich}}: \operatorname{Teich}^+(S,M) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Teich}^+(S,M). \qed \] \end{enumerate}
nodes.section: Teichm\"uller spaces of marked Klein surfaces
assumptions: Let $g$ be the genus of $S$ and suppose that $(S,M)$ is stable
conclusions: has a natural structure of a complex manifold of dimension $3g-3+|M|$.

nodes.name: Teichmüller space of a marked Klein surface
nodes.statement:
Let now $(S,M)$ be an arbitrary stable marked surface. Denote by $\operatorname{Klein}(S)$ the space of all
possible conformal structures on $S$. The {\em Teichm\"uller space}
of $(S,M)$ is defined by
\[
\operatorname{Teich}(S,M) = \operatorname{Diff}(S,M)\backslash \operatorname{Klein}(S). 
\]
nodes.section: Teichm\"uller spaces of marked Klein surfaces

nodes.name: Teichmüller spaces of Klein surfaces
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate} \item[(a)] If $S$ is classical (i.e., orientable without boundary), then the space $\operatorname{Teich}(S,M)$ is the disjoint union of two connected components, corresponding to the two orientations of $S$. Each component is canonically identified with the corresponding classical Teichm\"uller space $\operatorname{Teich}^+(S,M)$. \item[(b1)] Suppose $S$ is non-classical, let $\pi: S^\#\to S$ be its Schottky double with involution $\sigma$, and let $M^\#=\pi^{-1}(M)$. Let $g^\#$ be the genus of $S^\#$. Then \[ \operatorname{Teich}(S,M) = (\operatorname{Teich}^+(S^\#, M^\#))^{\sigma_{\operatorname{Teich}}} \] is the fixed point locus of the anti-holomorphic involution $\sigma_{\operatorname{Teich}}$. In particular, it is a real analytic manifold of dimension $3g^\#-3+|M^\#|$. \item[(b2)] Suppose $S$ is non-orientable, let $\varpi: \widetilde S\to S$ be its orientation cover with the orientation reversing deck involution $\tau$, and let $\widetilde M=\varpi^{-1}(M)$. Then \[ \operatorname{Teich}(S,M) = (\operatorname{Teich}^+(\widetilde S, \widetilde M))^{\tau_{\operatorname{Teich}}} \] is the fixed point locus of the involution $\tau_{\operatorname{Teich}}$. \item[(c)] In the situation (b1), the manifold $\operatorname{Teich}(S,M)$ is diffeomorphic to Euclidean space. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $\operatorname{Teich}(S,M)$ is two copies of the classical one, or the fixed locus of an involution on the Teichmüller space of the double or orientation cover; it is a cell.
nodes.section: Teichm\"uller spaces of marked Klein surfaces
assumptions: Suppose $S$ is non-classical
conclusions: is the fixed point locus of the anti-holomorphic involution $\sigma_{\operatorname{Teich}}$.
nodes.label: thm:klein-teich

nodes.name: Proof of Teichmüller spaces of Klein surfaces
nodes.statement: Parts (a), (b1-2) are obvious. Part (c) was proved by Natanzon \cite{natanzon} for $\partial S = M=\emptyset$ and Sepp\"al\"a \cite{seppala} for $M=\emptyset$. The extension to the case $M\neq\emptyset$ is can be done by the same methods.
nodes.statement_short: (a),(b) are obvious; (c) is due to Natanzon and Seppälä, extended by the same methods.
nodes.section: Teichm\"uller spaces of marked Klein surfaces

nodes.name: $G_{conf}$-structured marked surface
nodes.statement: A $G_{\operatorname{conf}}$-{\em structured marked surface} is a datum consisting of: \begin{enumerate} \item[(1)] A conformal surface $S$. \item[(2)] A finite subset $M\subset S$. \item[(3)] A $G_{\operatorname{conf}}$-structure on $S-(M\cap S^\circ)$ compatible with the conformal structure restricted from $S$. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Groupoid $G_{conf}\operatorname{Str}(S,M)$
nodes.statement:
Given a $C^\infty$ marked surface $(S,M)$, we have a  topological groupoid   $G_{\operatorname{conf}}\operatorname{Str}(S,M)$
 formed by pairs consisting of a conformal structure on $S$ and a compatible $G_{\operatorname{conf}}$-structure on
 $S-(M\cap S^\circ)$.

nodes.name: Splitting of $G_{conf}\operatorname{Str}(S,M)$
Product decomposition of structures
nodes.statement: G_{\operatorname{conf}}\operatorname{Str}(S,M)\,\,\simeq \,\, \mathbb{G}\operatorname{Str}(S-(M\cap S^\circ))\times O(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}\operatorname{Str}(S).
nodes.label: eq:prod-str

nodes.name: Moduli spaces of $G_{conf}$-structured surfaces
Moduli groupoids
nodes.statement: \begin{gathered} \mathcal{M}^{G_{\operatorname{conf}}}(S,M) \,\,=\,\, \operatorname{Diff}(S,M) \bigl\backslash \hskip -.1cm \bigl\backslash G_{\operatorname{conf}}\operatorname{Str}(S,M)), \\ \mathcal{M}^{G_{\operatorname{conf}}}_{\operatorname{pure}} (S,M) \,\,=\,\, \operatorname{Diff}_{\operatorname{pure}}(S,M) \bigl\backslash \hskip -.1cm \bigl\backslash G_{\operatorname{conf}}\operatorname{Str}(S,M). \end{gathered}

nodes.name: Moduli space as groupoid of structured surfaces
nodes.statement: Equivalently, $\mathcal{M}^{G_{\operatorname{conf}}}(S,M)$ can be seen as the groupoid formed by all $G_{\operatorname{conf}}$-structured marked surfaces of topological type $(S,M)$ and by their structured diffeomorphisms.

nodes.name: Deligne-Mumford moduli of curves
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a finite set and suppose that $2g-2+|M|>0$. Let $\mathcal{M}(g,M)$ be the Deligne-Mumford moduli stack formed by smooth projective algebraic curves $X$ of genus $g$ together with an embedding $M\hookrightarrow X$. Let $(S,M)$ be a classical marked surface of genus $g$. Any choice of an orientation of $S$ identifies $\mathcal{M}^{SO(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}}_{{\operatorname{pure}}}(S,M)$ with the groupoid (orbifold) of $\mathbb{C}$-points $\mathcal{M}(g,M)(\mathbb{C})$. Change of orientation corresponds to the action of $\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb{C}/\mathbb{R})$ on $\mathcal{M}(g,M)(\mathbb{C})$ which comes from the fact that $\mathcal{M}(g,M)$ is defined over $\mathbb{R}$ (in fact, over $\mathbb{Q}$). The orbifold $\mathcal{M}^{SO(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}}$ is therefore the quotient of $\mathcal{M}(g,M)(\mathbb{C})$ by the symmetric group of $M$. As is well known, \[ \mathcal{M}(g,M)(\mathbb{C}) = \operatorname{Mod}^+_{\operatorname{pure}}(S,M) \bigl\backslash \hskip -.1cm \bigl\backslash \operatorname{Teich}^+(S,M) \] is the quotient of the topological cell $\operatorname{Teich}^+(S,M)$ by the mapping class group of orientation preserving diffeomorphisms fixing all points of $M$. In what follows, we realize a general $\mathcal{M}^{G_{\operatorname{conf}}}(S,M)$ in terms of quotients of cells by discrete groups.

nodes.name: Topological moduli groupoid $\mathcal{M}^{\mathbb{G}}(S,M)$
nodes.statement:
Let $(S,M)$ be stable, and define
\begin{equation} \mathcal{M}^{\mathbb{G}}(S,M) = \operatorname{Diff}(S,M)\bigl\backslash \hskip -.1cm \bigl\backslash \mathbb{G}\operatorname{Str}(S-(M\cap S^\circ)) \simeq
	\operatorname{Mod}(S,M) \bigl\backslash \hskip -.1cm \bigl\backslash \mathbb{G}\operatorname{Str}(S-(M\cap S^\circ)) 
\end{equation}
as the ``topological" analog of the moduli space, in which we consider $\mathbb{G}$ instead of $G_{\operatorname{conf}}$ as
a structure group.

nodes.name: Topological moduli groupoid
nodes.statement: \mathcal{M}^{\mathbb{G}}(S,M) = \operatorname{Diff}(S,M)\bigl\backslash \hskip -.1cm \bigl\backslash \mathbb{G}\operatorname{Str}(S-(M\cap S^\circ)) \simeq \operatorname{Mod}(S,M) \bigl\backslash \hskip -.1cm \bigl\backslash \mathbb{G}\operatorname{Str}(S-(M\cap S^\circ))
nodes.label: eq:top-moduli

nodes.name: Moduli space as union of quotients of Teichmüller space
nodes.statement: We have a homotopy equivalence of topological groupoids \[ \mathcal{M}^{G_{\operatorname{conf}}}(S,M) \simeq \coprod_{ \{F\} \in \mathcal{M}^{\mathbb{G}}(S,M)} \operatorname{Mod}^{\mathbb{G}}(S_F, M) \bigl\backslash \hskip -.1cm \bigl\backslash \operatorname{Teich}(S,M) \] and a similar identification of $\mathcal{M}^{G_{\operatorname{conf}}}_{\operatorname{pure}}(S,M)$. Here $\{ F\}$ runs over isomorphism classes of objects of $\mathcal{M}^{\mathbb{G}}(S,M)$, and $S_F$ is the $\mathbb{G}$-structured surface corresponding to $F$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{M}^{G_{conf}}(S,M)$ is a disjoint union over $\mathbb{G}$-structures of quotients of $\operatorname{Teich}(S,M)$ by structured mapping class groups.
conclusions: We have a homotopy equivalence of topological groupoids

nodes.name: Proof of Moduli space as union of quotients of Teichmüller space
nodes.statement: Using \eqref{eq:prod-str}, we have \begin{align*} \mathcal{M}^{G_{\operatorname{conf}}}(S,M) & = \operatorname{Diff}(S,M) \bigl\backslash \hskip -.1cm \bigl\backslash \bigl( \mathbb{G}\operatorname{Str}(S-(M\cap S^\circ)) \times O(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}\operatorname{Str}(S)\bigr)\\ & = \operatorname{Diff}(S,M) \biggl\backslash \hskip -.25cm \biggl\backslash \coprod_{ \{F\}\in \mathbb{G}\operatorname{Str}(S-(M\cap S^\circ))} O(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}\operatorname{Str}(S)\\ & = \coprod _{ \{F\}\in \operatorname{Diff}(S,M) \backslash \hskip -.1cm \backslash \mathbb{G}\operatorname{Str}(S-(M\cap S^\circ))} \biggl( \operatorname{Stab}(F) \bigl\backslash \hskip -.1cm \bigl\backslash O(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}\operatorname{Str}(S)\biggr). \end{align*} Note that at the bottom of last coproduct the quotient by $\operatorname{Diff}(S,M)$ is $\mathcal{M}^{\mathbb{G}}(S,M)$. At the same time, $\operatorname{Stab}(F)$ is the union of connected components of $\operatorname{Diff}(S,M)$, in particular, $\operatorname{Stab}(F)_e = \operatorname{Diff}(S,M)_e$. Therefore the above coproduct can be identified with \[ \begin{gathered} \coprod_{ \{F\}\in\mathcal{M}^{\mathbb{G}}(S,M)} \pi_0 (\operatorname{Stab}(F)) \biggl\backslash \hskip -.25cm \biggl\backslash \biggl( \operatorname{Stab}(F)_e \bigl\backslash \hskip -.1cm \bigl\backslash O(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}\operatorname{Str}(S)\biggr)\,\,= \\ =\,\, \coprod_{ \{F\} \in\mathcal{M}^{\mathbb{G}}(S,M)} \operatorname{Mod}^{\mathbb{G}}(S_F, M) \bigl\backslash \hskip -.1cm \bigl\backslash \operatorname{Teich}(S,M) \end{gathered} \] as claimed. In the last identification, we identified the topological groupoid $O(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}\operatorname{Str}(S)$ with the topological space $\operatorname{Klein}(S)$ of its isomorphism classes. This is possible because all automorphism groups of objects in this groupoid are trivial by Proposition \ref{prop:prod-of-grpds}(b).
nodes.statement_short: Decompose using the product formula, take stabilizers of $\mathbb{G}$-structures, and identify the conformal groupoid with $\operatorname{Klein}(S)$.

nodes.name: Rewrite using the product decomposition.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite using the product decomposition.

nodes.name: Stabilizers are unions of components.
nodes.statement:
Note that at the  bottom of last coproduct the quotient by $\operatorname{Diff}(S,M)$ is $\mathcal{M}^{\mathbb{G}}(S,M)$. At the same time,
$\operatorname{Stab}(F)$ is the union of connected components of $\operatorname{Diff}(S,M)$, in particular,
$\operatorname{Stab}(F)_e = \operatorname{Diff}(S,M)_e$.
nodes.statement_short: Stabilizers are unions of components.

nodes.name: Identify with quotients of $\operatorname{Teich}$ by $\operatorname...
nodes.statement:
Therefore the above coproduct can be identified with
\[
\begin{gathered}
\coprod_{ \{F\}\in\mathcal{M}^{\mathbb{G}}(S,M)} \pi_0 (\operatorname{Stab}(F)) 
\biggl\backslash \hskip -.25cm \biggl\backslash \biggl(  \operatorname{Stab}(F)_e \bigl\backslash \hskip -.1cm \bigl\backslash O(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}\operatorname{Str}(S)\biggr)\,\,=
\\ =\,\,
\coprod_{ \{F\} \in\mathcal{M}^{\mathbb{G}}(S,M)} \operatorname{Mod}^{\mathbb{G}}(S_F, M) \bigl\backslash \hskip -.1cm \bigl\backslash \operatorname{Teich}(S,M)
\end{gathered}
\]
as claimed.
nodes.statement_short: Identify with quotients of $\operatorname{Teich}$ by $\operatorname{Mod}^{\mathbb{G}}$.

nodes.name: Conformal groupoid has trivial automorphisms (Prop. 3.15(b)).
nodes.statement:
In the last identification, we identified the topological groupoid $O(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}\operatorname{Str}(S)$
with the topological space $\operatorname{Klein}(S)$ of its isomorphism classes. This is possible because
all automorphism groups of objects in this groupoid are trivial by Proposition 
\ref{prop:prod-of-grpds}(b).
nodes.statement_short: Conformal groupoid has trivial automorphisms (Prop. 3.15(b)).

nodes.name: Graph
nodes.statement: A {\em graph} $\Gamma$ is a pair of sets $(H,V)$ equipped with \begin{itemize} \item an involution $\tau: H \to H$, \item a map $s: H \to V$. \end{itemize} The elements of $H$ are called {\em halfedges} of $\Gamma$, the fixed points of $\tau$ are called {\em external halfedges}, and the nonfixed points of $\tau$ are called {\em internal halfedges}. The $2$-element orbits of $\tau$, which are hence comprised of a pair of internal halfedges, are called {\em edges}. The elements of $V$ are called the {\em vertices} of $\Gamma$. Given a vertex $v \in V$, we define the set $H(v) = s^{-1}(v)$ of {\em halfedges incident to $v$}. The cardinality $|H(v)|$ is called the valency of $v$.

nodes.name: Incidence category and incidence diagram
nodes.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a graph. The {\em incidence category} $I(\Gamma)$ of $\Gamma$ has, as objects, all the vertices and edges of $\Gamma$ with a non-identity morphism $s(h) \to \{h,\tau(h)\}$ for every internal halfedge $h$. The {\em incidence diagram of $\Gamma$} is the functor \[ I_{\Gamma}: I(\Gamma) \longrightarrow {\mathcal Set} \] given on objects by assigning to a vertex $v$ the set $H(v)$ and to an edge $e$ with half-edges $h,h'$, the $2$-element set $\{h,h'\}$. To a morphism $s(h) \to \{h,h'\}$ we associate the map of sets $H(s(h)) \to \{h,h'\}$ given by mapping $h$ to $h'$ and collapsing the remaining halfedges in $H(s(h))$ (denoted by A in Fig. \ref{fig:F1}) to $h$.

nodes.name: Compact graph
nodes.statement:
We say a graph is {\em compact} if all its halfedges are internal. Unless stated otherwise, we will
assume all graphs to be compact.

nodes.name: Realization of a graph
nodes.statement: Given a graph $\Gamma$, we define its {\em realization} $|\Gamma| = |\operatorname{N}(I(\Gamma)|$ to be the geometric realization of its incidence category. We denote by $\partial |\Gamma|\subset|\Gamma|$ the set of 1-valent vertices and by $|\Gamma|^\circ$ the complement $|\Gamma| - \partial|\Gamma|$.

nodes.name: Midpoints of edges
nodes.statement: Note that the realization $|\Gamma|$ comes equipped with two kinds of $0$-cells. On the one hand, we have a $0$-cell for each vertex $v$ of $\Gamma$, on the other hand, we have a $0$-cell $m(e)$ for each edge $e$ of $\Gamma$ which can be regarded as a chosen midpoint of the geometric edge which connects the two vertices of $\Gamma$ incident to $e$, see Figure \ref{fig:F1}.
nodes.label: rem:midpoint

nodes.name: $\mathcal{G}$-structure on a graph
nodes.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a graph and let ${\mathcal G}$ be a small category equipped with a functor ${\mathcal G} \to {\mathcal Set}$. A {\em ${\mathcal G}$-structure on $\Gamma$} is a lift \[ \xymatrix{ & {\mathcal G} \ar[d] \\ I(\Gamma) \ar[r]^{I_{\Gamma}} \ar[ur]^{\widetilde{I_{\Gamma}}} & {\mathcal Set} } \] of the incidence diagram of $\Gamma$ to ${\mathcal G}$.
nodes.label: defi:ggraph

nodes.name: $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$-structured graph
nodes.statement:
In this context, we will slightly abuse
notation, and refer to ${\mathcal G}$-structured graphs as ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured graphs.

nodes.name: Ribbon, Möbius, framed and $N$-spin graphs
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate} \item A graph with a $\Lambda$-structure is called a {\em ribbon graph}. Explicitly, a $\Lambda$-structure on a graph $\Gamma$ is the datum of a cyclic order on the $H(v)$ for each vertex $v\in V$. Each set $\{h,h'\}$ of half-edges of any edge $e$ has a trivial cyclic order, since it has cardinality 2. Thus, our definition reduces to the usual one \cite{penner:book}. \item A graph with a $\Xi$-structure is called a {\em M\"obius graph}. Explicitly, a $\Xi$-structure on a graph $\Gamma$ consists, first, of a dihedral order on each $H(v)$ and, second, of identification of the orientation torsors \[ O(H(v))\buildrel\sim\over \longleftarrow O(e)\buildrel\sim\over \longrightarrow O(H(v')) \] for each edge $e$ with vertices $v$ and $v'$ (the case $v=v'$ is allowed). This structure is equivalent to the (somewhat more cumbersome) concept of a M\"obius graph defined in terms of ``ribbon graphs with $\mathbb{Z}/2$-grading on edges" as in \cite{braun, mulase-waldron, mulase-yu}. \item A graph with a $\Lambda_{\infty}$-structure is called a {\em framed graph}. \item A graph with a $\Lambda_N$-structure is called an {\em $N$-spin graph}. Very recently, surfaces with 2-spin structure were studied, from a combinatorial point of view by Novak and Runkel \cite{novak-runkel}. They introduced a concept of a combinatorial spin structure on a triangulation $T$ of a surface $S$. Such a structure equips the dual graph of $T$ with a $\Lambda_2$-structure in our sense. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: defi:exggraphs

nodes.name: Circle of directions
nodes.statement:
For a 2-dimensional $\mathbb{R}$-vector space $V$, we denote by
\[
C(V) \,\,=\,\, (V-\{0\})/\mathbb{R}^*_{>0}
\]
the circle of directions of $V$. In particular, for any surface $S$ and any $x\in S$ we have the circle
$C(T_xS)$ of tangent directions at $x$.

nodes.name: Embedding of a graph into a surface
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be a surface. By an {\em embedding} of a graph $\Gamma$ into $S$ we mean an injective, continous map $\gamma: |\Gamma| \to S$ such that \begin{itemize} \item $\gamma(|\Gamma|^\circ)$ is contained in the interior of $S$, and $\gamma(\partial|\Gamma|)\subset\partial S$. \item $\gamma$ is smooth along every edge of $|\Gamma|$. \item For every vertex $x$ of $|\Gamma|$ (corresponding to a vertex or and edge of $\Gamma$), the tangent directions of the edge germs on $S$ which leave $\gamma(x)$, are distinct. \end{itemize}
nodes.label: exa:embedding

nodes.name: Embedded graphs are structured
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be a surface with a $\mathbb{G}$-structure. An embedding of a graph $\Gamma$ into $S$ endows $\Gamma$ with a ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structure.
nodes.statement_short: An embedded graph in a $\mathbb{G}$-structured surface inherits a canonical $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$-structure.
assumptions: Let $S$ be a surface with a $\mathbb{G}$-structure.
conclusions: An embedding of a graph $\Gamma$ into $S$ endows $\Gamma$
nodes.label: prop:emb-graph-str

nodes.name: Proof of Embedded graphs are structured
nodes.statement_short: Tangent circles carry $\operatorname{Homeo}^G(S^1)$-structures giving structured sets of half-edges; structure maps come from a canonical component of lifted homeomorphisms, chosen via Riemannian parallel transport.

nodes.name: Paths of half-edges to edge midpoints.
nodes.statement:
Let $h$ be a half-edge of $\Gamma$ incident to the vertex $v$ and with corresponding edge
	$e=\{h,h'\}$. We denote by $\gamma(|h|)$ the corresponding path in $S$ which runs from
	$\gamma(v)$ to the midpoint $m(e)= \gamma(e)$.
nodes.statement_short: Paths of half-edges to edge midpoints.

nodes.name: Corollary 2.15 makes each $H(v)$ a structured set.
nodes.statement:
A $\mathbb{G}$-structure on $S$ gives, via the homotopy equivalence $\mathbb{G}\to{ \operatorname{Homeo}}^G(S^1)$, a
	${ \operatorname{Homeo}}^G(S^1)$-structure on each circle $C(T_xS)$. Therefore, by Corollary
	\ref{cor:structured-circle-orders}, each finite subset of $C(T_xS)$ becomes, canonically, a
	${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured set. In particular, for each vertex $v \in V$, we have a canonical
	embedding of sets $H(v)\hookrightarrow C(T_{\gamma(v)} S)$ given by association to a
	half-edge $h$ the direction given by the germ of the path $\gamma(|h|)$ leaving $v$.  By
	the above, this provides a canonical ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structure on the set $H(v)$.
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 2.15 makes each $H(v)$ a structured set.

nodes.name: Structure on the two half-edges of an edge.
nodes.statement:
Further, let $e$ be
	an edge of $\Gamma$ given by a pair of half-edges $h, h'$  as above. 
	The two tangent directions to $|\Gamma|$ at $\gamma(m(e))$ correspond to the two half-edges
	$h$ and $h'$ of $e$. As before, the embedding $|\Gamma|\to S$ gives a ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structure on the
	2-element set of these directions, i.e., on $\{h,h'\}$. This defines the values of the
	functor $\widetilde I_\Gamma: I(\Gamma)\to \mathcal{G}$ on objects.
nodes.statement_short: Structure on the two half-edges of an edge.

nodes.name: Set up circles $C_v$, $C_e$ and arcs.
nodes.statement:
To define $\widetilde I_\Gamma$ on morphisms, consider one of the half-edges of $e$, say
	$h$, and let $v=s(h)$ be the corresponding vertex. Consider the ${ \operatorname{Homeo}}^G(S^1)$-structured
	circles
	\[
	C_v = C(T_{\gamma(v)}S), \quad C_e = C(T_{\gamma(m(e))} S). 
	\]
	Let $J_c\subset C_v$ be the union of small non-intersecting closed arcs centered around
	images of elements of $H(v)$.  We write $J_v=A\sqcup B$, where $B$ is the arc corresponding
	to $h\in H(v)$, and $A$ is the union of all the other arcs, see Figure \ref{fig:F2}.
nodes.statement_short: Set up circles $C_v$, $C_e$ and arcs.

nodes.name: Contractible space $\Phi$ of homeomorphisms (Prop. 2.12).
nodes.statement:
Similarly, let $J_e=A'\sqcup B'\subset C_e$ where $A'$ is a small closed arc around the
	image of $h$ in $C_e$ (denoted $a'$) and $B'$ is a small closed arc around the image of $h'$
	in $C_e$ (denoted $b'$). Note that the orientation torsors of $C_v$ and $C_e$ are identified
	by parallel transport along $\gamma(|h|)$. We now consider the space $\Phi$ formed by all
	orientation preserving homeomorphisms
	\[
	\phi: (C_v, J_v) \longrightarrow (C_e, J_e)
	\quad \text{s.t. } \phi(A)\subset A', \, \phi(B)\subset B'.
	\]
	These requirements define $\phi$ uniquely up to an isotopy (i.e., $\Phi$ is connected).
	Further, by Proposition \ref{prop:homeo-contr}, $\Phi$ is contractible.
nodes.statement_short: Contractible space $\Phi$ of homeomorphisms (Prop. 2.12).

nodes.name: Lifts of $\Phi$ form a disjoint union of copies.
nodes.statement:
Consider now the
	unramified covering
	\[
	\pi: { \operatorname{Homeo}}^G(C_v, C_e) \longrightarrow { \operatorname{Homeo}}(C_v, C_e).
	\]
	As $\Phi$ is contractible, $\pi^{-1}(\Phi)$ is a disjoint union of components homeomorphic
	to $\Phi$.
nodes.statement_short: Lifts of $\Phi$ form a disjoint union of copies.

nodes.name: Canonical component
nodes.statement:
We now show that the $\mathbb{G}$-structure on $S$ defines a canonical choice of a
	component $\widetilde\Phi\subset\pi^{-1}(\Phi)$. By Theorem \ref{thm:CG=DG},
	$\widetilde\Phi$ will define a structure morphism $H(v)\to \{e,e'\}$ in $\mathcal{G}$. 

	Choose a Riemannian metric on $S$ (a contractible choice). This reduces the structure group
	of $S$ from $\mathbb{G}$ to $G$. Let $T: C_v\to C_e$ be the Riemannian parallel transport along
	$\gamma(|h|)$.  It lifts canonically to a morphism of ${ \operatorname{Homeo}}^G(S^1)$-structured circles.
	Denote this structured morphism by $\widetilde T$.  Let $\Pi$ be the space of paths
	$(T_s)_{s\in[0,1]}$ in ${ \operatorname{Homeo}}(C_v, C_e)$ starting at $T$ and ending somewhere in $\Phi$.
	Any path $(T_s)\in\Pi$ defines a lift $\widetilde\Phi$ by transporting $\widetilde T$ along
	this path. Clearly, this $\widetilde \Phi$ depends only on the image of $(T_s)$ in
	$\pi_0(\Pi)$.  Note that $\pi_0(\Pi)$ is a torsor over $\mathbb{Z} = \pi_1 \,{ \operatorname{Homeo}}^+(C_v, C_e)$.
	Note that $T$ sends the midpoint $b\in B$ (i.e, the image of $h$ in $C_v$) into the midpoint
	$b'\in B'$ (i.e., the image of $h'$ in $C_e$). Therefore we have a distinguished component
	$\Pi_0$ of $\Pi$ containing paths $(T_s)$ such that $T_s(B)$ meets $B'$ for all $s$. The
	transport of $\widetilde T$ along any path from $\Pi_0$ gives the component
	$\widetilde\Phi$. This concludes the argument.
nodes.statement_short: The structure picks a canonical component, giving the structure morphism.

nodes.name: A component defines a morphism in $\mathcal{G}$.
nodes.statement:
By Theorem \ref{thm:CG=DG},
	$\widetilde\Phi$ will define a structure morphism $H(v)\to \{e,e'\}$ in $\mathcal{G}$.
nodes.statement_short: A component defines a morphism in $\mathcal{G}$.

nodes.name: Parallel transport $T$ and its structured lift.
nodes.statement:
Choose a Riemannian metric on $S$ (a contractible choice). This reduces the structure group
	of $S$ from $\mathbb{G}$ to $G$. Let $T: C_v\to C_e$ be the Riemannian parallel transport along
	$\gamma(|h|)$.  It lifts canonically to a morphism of ${ \operatorname{Homeo}}^G(S^1)$-structured circles.
	Denote this structured morphism by $\widetilde T$.
nodes.statement_short: Parallel transport $T$ and its structured lift.

nodes.name: Paths from $T$ to $\Phi$ transport the lift.
nodes.statement:
Let $\Pi$ be the space of paths
	$(T_s)_{s\in[0,1]}$ in ${ \operatorname{Homeo}}(C_v, C_e)$ starting at $T$ and ending somewhere in $\Phi$.
	Any path $(T_s)\in\Pi$ defines a lift $\widetilde\Phi$ by transporting $\widetilde T$ along
	this path. Clearly, this $\widetilde \Phi$ depends only on the image of $(T_s)$ in
	$\pi_0(\Pi)$.  Note that $\pi_0(\Pi)$ is a torsor over $\mathbb{Z} = \pi_1 \,{ \operatorname{Homeo}}^+(C_v, C_e)$.
nodes.statement_short: Paths from $T$ to $\Phi$ transport the lift.

nodes.name: Distinguished component $\Pi_0$ gives the canonical lift.
nodes.statement:
Note that $T$ sends the midpoint $b\in B$ (i.e, the image of $h$ in $C_v$) into the midpoint
	$b'\in B'$ (i.e., the image of $h'$ in $C_e$). Therefore we have a distinguished component
	$\Pi_0$ of $\Pi$ containing paths $(T_s)$ such that $T_s(B)$ meets $B'$ for all $s$. The
	transport of $\widetilde T$ along any path from $\Pi_0$ gives the component
	$\widetilde\Phi$. This concludes the argument.
nodes.statement_short: Distinguished component $\Pi_0$ gives the canonical lift.

nodes.name: Ribbon, Möbius, framed and spin structures on embedded graphs
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate} \item Suppose ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}=\Lambda$. If $\Gamma$ be embedded into an oriented surface $S$, then it is classical that $\Gamma$ is canonically a ribbon graph. Explicitly, each $H(v)$ has a cyclic order from the embedding into the oriented circle $C(T_{\gamma(v)} S)$, while the set of half-edges of any edge has a unique cyclic order since it has cardinality $2$. \item Suppose ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}=\Xi$. Let $\Gamma$ be embedded into an unoriented surface $S$. Then $\Gamma$ naturally admits the structure of a M\"obius graph. The set $H(v)$ of half-edges incident to $v$ inherits a dihedral order from the embedding into the circle $C(T_{\gamma(v)} S)$. The set $\{h,h'\}$ of half-edges of an edge $e$ is made into a dihedral set by looking at the orientation cover $\varpi: \widetilde \to S$: we define the orientation torsor $O(\{h,h'\})$ of this set to be the set of sections of $\pi$ over the image, under $\gamma$, of the interior of $|e|$. Finally, we have to provide a lift of the incidence map $i: H(s(h)) \to \{h,h'\}$ to a morphism of dihedrally ordered sets. Note that, by the path lifting property of the orientation cover $\pi$, the orientation torsors of $H(s(h))$ and $\{h,h'\}$ are canonically identified. For every choice of orientation, there is now a unique linear order on $i^{-1}(h')$ compatible with the corresponding cyclic order of $H(s(h))$. These two linear orders are opposite providing $i$ with the structure of a morphism in ${\Xi}$. \item Let ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}={\Lambda}_\infty$. Assume that $\Gamma$ is embedded into a framed surface $S$. This means, in particular, that $S$ is oriented so that we have a principal $GL^+(2,\mathbb{R})$-bundle $\operatorname{Fr}^+_S$ of positive frames on $S$. Further, we are given a principal $\widetilde{GL^+(2,\mathbb{R})}$-bundle $\widetilde{\operatorname{Fr}}^+_S$ covering $\operatorname{Fr}^+_S$. Thus, each fiber of $\widetilde{\operatorname{Fr}}^+_S$ is a universal cover of the corresponding fiber of $\operatorname{Fr}^+_S$. Let \[ B^+ \,\,=\,\, \biggl\{ \begin{pmatrix} a&b\\0&c \end{pmatrix}\,\in GL^+(2,\mathbb{R})\bigl\| \,\, a,c >0\biggr\}. \] Then $B^+\backslash GL^+(2,\mathbb{R})=S^1$ is the circle of directions of $\mathbb{R}^2$. Therefore $B^+\backslash \operatorname{Fr}^+_S=C(T_S)$ is the circle bundle of directions of $T_S$. Further, $B^+$, being contractible, lifts canonically to a subgroup $\widetilde B^+\subset\widetilde{GL^+(2,\mathbb{R})}$. The quotient $\widetilde B^+\backslash \widetilde{GL^+(2,\mathbb{R})}\simeq\mathbb{R}$ is the universal covering of $S^1$. So each fiber $\widetilde C(T_xS)= \widetilde B^+\backslash \widetilde{\operatorname{Fr}}^+_{S,x}$ is an oriented real line, equipped with the projection $\pi_x: \widetilde C(T_xS)\to C(T_xS)$ exhibiting it as a universal covering of $C(T_xS)$. Therefore, for each vertex $v\in\Gamma$ the preimage of $H(v)\subset C(T_{\gamma(v)}S)$ is naturally a $\mathbb{Z}$-torsor, thus giving a paracyclic order on $H(v)$. Similarly for each edge $\{h,h'\}$. We leave remaining details to the reader. \item Assume that $\Gamma$ is embedded into a surface $S$ which has an $N$-spin structure. Then, similarly to (3) , we consider an $N$-fold covering $\pi_x: \widetilde C_N(T_xS)\to C(T_xS)$ for each $x\in S$. Taking $\pi_{\gamma(v)}^{-1}(H(v))$, we make each $H(v)$ into an $N$-cyclic set, and similarly for each set $\{h,h'\}$. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Weak equivalence of graphs
nodes.statement: Let $\Gamma$, $\Gamma'$ be graphs. A {\em weak equivalence} between $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma'$ is a functor $\varphi: I(\Gamma) \to I(\Gamma')$ of incidence categories such that \begin{enumerate} \item $\varphi$ induces a bijection of the sets of vertices of valency $1$, \item the induced map $|\varphi|: |I(\Gamma)| \to |I(\Gamma')|$ is homotopy equivalence. \end{enumerate}
nodes.section: Structured graphs and mapping class groups of structured surfaces

nodes.name: Pullback of incidence diagrams
nodes.statement:
Given a weak equivalence $\varphi: \Gamma \to \Gamma'$ of graphs we obtain an induced natural
transformation $\varphi^* I_{\Gamma'} \to I_{\Gamma}$ of incidence diagrams as follows: Given an
object $x$ of $I(\Gamma)$ corresponding to a vertex of $\Gamma$, we may represent each halfedge $e$ 
incident to $\varphi(x)$ by a path $\alpha$ in $|I(\Gamma')|$ which starts at $\varphi(x)$ and 
parametrizes the edge corresponding to $e$. The germ of the pullback of $\alpha$ at $x$ determines a
unique halfedge at $x$. This construction canonically determines a map $I_{\Gamma'}(\varphi(x)) \to
I_{\Gamma}(x)$. By a similar construction, one obtains maps $I_{\Gamma'}(\varphi(y)) \to
I_{\Gamma}(y)$ for every object $y$ corresponding to an edge of $\Gamma$ which assemble to the
desired natural transformation.
nodes.section: Structured graphs and mapping class groups of structured surfaces

nodes.name: Category $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$-Graph
nodes.statement: Let $\Gamma$, $\Gamma'$ be ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured graphs. A {\em weak equivalence} $\varphi: \Gamma \to \Gamma'$ of ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured graphs is a weak equivalence of underlying graphs together with a lift of the pullback morphism $\varphi^* I_{\Gamma'} \to I_{\Gamma}$ to a morphism of ${\mathcal G}$-diagrams $\varphi^* \widetilde{I_{\Gamma'}} \to \widetilde{I_{\Gamma}}$. We define ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}-\operatorname{Graph}$ to be the category with objects given by (compact) ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured graphs without vertices of valency $2$ and morphisms given by weak equivalences.
nodes.section: Structured graphs and mapping class groups of structured surfaces
nodes.label: def:weak-eq-str-graphs

nodes.name: Contractions
nodes.statement: Sometimes we will refer to weak equivalences of structured graphs as {\em contractions}.
nodes.section: Structured graphs and mapping class groups of structured surfaces

nodes.name: Structured graphs classify structured surfaces
nodes.statement: The topological realization $|N({\Delta \mathfrak{G}}-\operatorname{Graph})|$ is a classifying space of $\mathbb{G}$-structured surfaces so that we have a homotopy equivalence \[ |{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}-\operatorname{Graph}| \simeq \coprod_{(S,M)} B\, \operatorname{Mod}^{\mathbb{G}}(S,M), \] where the coproduct is taken over all topological types of stable marked $\mathbb{G}$-structured surfaces $(S,M)$.
nodes.statement_short: The nerve of $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$-Graph is homotopy equivalent to the disjoint union of classifying spaces of structured mapping class groups.
nodes.section: Structured graphs and mapping class groups of structured surfaces
nodes.label: thm:g-graph

nodes.name: Spanning graph and poset $P(S,M)$
nodes.statement: Let $(S,M)$ be a stable marked surface. A {\em spanning graph} for $(S,M)$ is a graph $\Gamma$ together with an embedding $\gamma: |\Gamma|\to S$ such that: \begin{enumerate} \item $\gamma$ is a homotopy equivalence. \item The restriction of $\gamma$ defines a homotopy equivalence between $\partial |\Gamma|$ (a finite set of points) and $\partial S - M$ (a finite set of open intervals). \end{enumerate} We define the category $P(S,M)$ whose objects are isotopy classes of spanning graphs for $(S,M)$ and with a unique morphism $[\Gamma] \to [\Gamma']$ if $[\Gamma']$ is obtained from $[\Gamma]$ by collapsing a forest. Note that $P(S,M)$ is in fact a poset.
nodes.section: Structured graphs and mapping class groups of structured surfaces

nodes.name: Contractibility of the spanning graph poset
nodes.statement: For any stable marked surface $(S,M)$ the poset $P(S,M)$ is contractible.
nodes.section: Structured graphs and mapping class groups of structured surfaces
assumptions: For any stable marked surface $(S,M)$
nodes.label: thm:graph-contr

nodes.name: Functor $\rho: P(S,M)\to\Delta\mathfrak{G}$-Graph
nodes.section: Structured graphs and mapping class groups of structured surfaces

nodes.name: Functor $\rho$
nodes.statement: \rho: P(S,M) \longrightarrow {\Delta \mathfrak{G}}-\operatorname{Graph}
nodes.section: Structured graphs and mapping class groups of structured surfaces
nodes.label: eq:rho

nodes.name: Augmented structured graph
nodes.statement: An {\em augmented ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured graph} is a possibly noncompact ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured graph $\Gamma$ equipped with \begin{itemize} \item for every external halfedge $e \in H(v)$, an {\em augmentation map} $\varphi_e: H(v) \to [1]$ of ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured sets, satisfying $\varphi_e^{-1}(\varphi(e)) = \{e\}$, \end{itemize} such that every vertex of $\Gamma$ has valency $\ge 2$.

nodes.name: Incoming and outgoing halfedges
nodes.statement:
Given an augmented ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured graph $\Gamma$, we obtain a partition of the set of external
halfedges into {\em incoming} ($\varphi_e(e) = 1$) and {\em outgoing} ($\varphi_e(e) = 0$).

nodes.name: Contraction of augmented graphs
nodes.statement:
A {\em contraction} of augmented
${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured graphs is a contraction of the underlying ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured graphs which commutes with
the augmentations.

nodes.name: Interval
nodes.statement:
A noncompact {\em interval} is a connected graph with two external halfedges and all vertices of valency $2$:   
\[
	\xymatrix{
		\ar@{-}[r] & \bullet \ar@{-}[r] & \bullet \ar@{-}[r]  & \cdots \ar@{-}[r] & \bullet
		\ar@{-}[r]  & 
	}
\]

nodes.name: One-vertex augmented interval
nodes.statement:
Consider an augmented ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured interval $\Gamma$ with one vertex $v$, $H(v) = \{e,f\}$ and incidence diagram given by
\begin{equation} [1] \overset{\varphi_e}{\longleftarrow} H(v) \overset{\varphi_f}{\longrightarrow} [1]
\end{equation}
where $e$ is incoming and $f$ is outgoing.

nodes.name: Augmented interval with one vertex
nodes.statement: [1] \overset{\varphi_e}{\longleftarrow} H(v) \overset{\varphi_f}{\longrightarrow} [1]
nodes.label: eq:interval

nodes.name: Category of augmented intervals
nodes.statement:
We define $\operatorname{Tr}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1)$ to be the category of augmented ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured intervals with external
halfedges labelled by $0$ (outgoing) and $1$ (incoming) and with contractions as morphisms.

nodes.name: Components of augmented intervals
nodes.statement:
We denote 
by $\pi_0\operatorname{Tr}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1)$ the set of isomorphism classes in the groupoid completion of $\operatorname{Tr}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1)$ so 
that two objects $\Gamma$,$\Gamma'$ are in the same class if and only if there exists a chain of zigzag 
contractions 
\[
	\Gamma \longleftarrow \Gamma_1 \longrightarrow \Gamma_2 \longleftarrow \dots \longrightarrow \Gamma'.
\]

nodes.name: Concatenation monoid
nodes.statement:
The above concatenation operation endows the set $\pi_0 \operatorname{Tr}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1)$ with the structure of a
monoid.

nodes.name: Monoid of intervals is $\mathfrak{G}_1^0$
nodes.statement: The monoid $\pi_0 \operatorname{Tr}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1)$ can be canonically identified with the group $\mathfrak{G}_1^0$.
conclusions: can be canonically identified with the group $\mathfrak{G}_1^0$.

nodes.name: Proof of Monoid of intervals is $\mathfrak{G}_1^0$
nodes.statement: Given an augmented ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured interval as in \eqref{eq:interval}, note that $\varphi_e$ and $\varphi_f$ are isomorphisms in ${\mathcal G}$. Using $\varphi_e$ to identify $H(v)$ with $[1]$, we obtain that the augmented ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-strutured interval is isomorphic to \[ [1] \overset{\operatorname{id}}{\longleftarrow} [1] \overset{g}{\longrightarrow} [1] \] where $g$ is an automorphism of $[1]$ which induces the identity on the underlying set $\{0,1\}$. Therefore, we have $g \in \mathfrak{G}_1^0$ where $\mathfrak{G}_1^0$ denotes the kernel of the map $\lambda: \mathfrak{G}_1 \to S_2$ from Proposition \ref{prop:forget}. It is immediate to verify that this identitication is compatible with the group law on $\mathfrak{G}_1^0$.
nodes.statement_short: Normalize the augmentations to see each interval is determined by an automorphism of $[1]$ over the identity.

nodes.name: Augmentations are isomorphisms.
nodes.statement:
Given an augmented ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured interval as in \eqref{eq:interval}, note that
	$\varphi_e$ and $\varphi_f$ are isomorphisms in ${\mathcal G}$.
nodes.statement_short: Augmentations are isomorphisms.

nodes.name: Normalize to $[1]\leftarrow[1]\to[1]$ with $g$.
nodes.statement:
Using $\varphi_e$ to identify $H(v)$
	with $[1]$, we obtain that the augmented ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-strutured interval is isomorphic to \[ [1]
	\overset{\operatorname{id}}{\longleftarrow} [1] \overset{g}{\longrightarrow} [1] \] where $g$ is an automorphism of $[1]$ which
	induces the identity on the underlying set $\{0,1\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Normalize to $[1]\leftarrow[1]\to[1]$ with $g$.

nodes.name: $g\in\mathfrak{G}_1^0$, compatibly with the group law.
nodes.statement:
Therefore, we have $g \in \mathfrak{G}_1^0$
	where $\mathfrak{G}_1^0$ denotes the kernel of the map $\lambda: \mathfrak{G}_1 \to S_2$ from Proposition
	\ref{prop:forget}. It is immediate to verify that this identitication is compatible with the
	group law on $\mathfrak{G}_1^0$.
nodes.statement_short: $g\in\mathfrak{G}_1^0$, compatibly with the group law.

nodes.name: Proof of Monoid of intervals is $\mathfrak{G}_0$
nodes.statement:
Since, for a planar crossed simplicial groups ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$, we have $\mathfrak{G}_1^0 \cong \mathfrak{G}_0$, we obtain the
following result.
nodes.statement_short: Combine Proposition 4.16 with $\mathfrak{G}_1^0\cong\mathfrak{G}_0$ for planar groups.

nodes.name: Monoid of intervals is $\mathfrak{G}_0$
nodes.statement: For a planar crossed simplicial group, the monoid $\pi_0 \operatorname{Tr}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1)$ is canonically isomorphic to the group $\mathfrak{G}_0$.
assumptions: For a planar crossed simplicial group
conclusions: is canonically isomorphic to the group $\mathfrak{G}_0$.

nodes.name: Category of augmented trees
nodes.statement:
Let $\operatorname{Tr}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(n)$ denote the category of augmented ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured trees with
external halfedges labelled by $0,1,\dots,n$ such that the halfedge $0$ is outgoing and all
remaining halfedges are incoming. The morphisms in $\operatorname{Tr}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(n)$ are given by contractions of
augmented ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured graphs.

nodes.name: Sets $P_{\Delta\mathfrak{G}}(n)$
nodes.statement:
We define $P_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(n)$ to be the set $\pi_0 \operatorname{Tr}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(n)$ of
isomorphism classes in the groupoid completion of $\operatorname{Tr}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(n)$.

nodes.name: Operadic composition of trees
nodes.statement:
Given augmented ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured trees
$\Gamma$, $\Gamma'$, an outgoing halfedge $e \in H(v)$ of $\Gamma$, and an incoming halfedge $e' \in
H(v')$ of $\Gamma'$, we obtain a canonical diagram of ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured sets
\[
	H(v) \overset{\varphi_e}{\longrightarrow} [1] = \{e,e'\} = [1] \overset{\varphi_{e'}}{\longleftarrow} H(v')
\]
so that we can concatenate $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma'$ forming an augmented ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured tree with
internal edge $\{e,e'\}$. Similarly, given an augmented ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured tree $\Gamma$, an outgoing (resp.
incoming) halfedge $e$, and $g \in P_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1) = \mathfrak{G}_1^0$, we can postcompose the augmentation
$\varphi_e$ with $g$ (resp. $g^{-1}$). This equips the family of sets $\{P_{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}(n)\}_{n\geq 1}$
with operations
\[
 m_{a_1, \dots, a_n}:  P_{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}(n) \times P_{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}(a_1)\times \cdots \times P_{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}(a_n) \longrightarrow 
 P_{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}(a_1+\cdots + a_n), \quad n, a_1, \dots, a_n \geq 1. 
\]

nodes.name: Operad of augmented structured trees
nodes.statement: Let ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ be a crossed simplicial group. \begin{enumerate} \item The action of $S_n$ on $P_{\mathcal{G}}(n)$ by relabelling the incoming external halfedges and the maps $\{ m_{a_1, \dots, a_n} \}$ make $P_{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}= \{P_{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}(n)\}_{n\geq 1}$ an operad in the category of sets. \item Assume that ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ is planar. Then algebras over $P_{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ are precisely monoids with a twisted action of $\mathfrak{G}_0$ in the sense of \S \ref{section:semiconstant}. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Augmented structured trees form an operad whose algebras, for planar $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$, are monoids with twisted $\mathfrak{G}_0$-action.

Assume that ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ is planar.
