nodes.name: Proof of Operad of augmented structured trees
nodes.statement: Part (1) is clear. We show (2). Given an augmented ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured tree $\Gamma$ in $\operatorname{Tr}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(n)$ with augmented incidence diagram $I(\Gamma) \to {\mathcal G}$, we first argue that we can contract all internal edges to obtain a corolla. To this end, we note that, given an internal edge $\{e,e'\}$ incident to vertices $v$ and $v'$, the corresponding diagram \[ H(v) \longrightarrow \{e,e'\} \longleftarrow H(v') \] has a limit in ${\mathcal G}$ whose underlying set is given by $(H(v)\setminus \{e\}) \cup (H(v') \setminus \{e'\})$. This holds for all planar crossed simplicial groups and can be verified using the topological model of ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ from \S \ref{sec:topmodel}. We can use the cone diagram of this limit in ${\mathcal G}$ to produce a morphism of ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured graphs $\Gamma \to \Gamma'$ which collapses the edge $\{e,e'\}$. After collapsing all internal edges of $\Gamma$, we obtain an augmented ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured $n$-corolla $\Gamma_0$. Using the labels we can identify the set $H(v)$ of halfedges incident to the single vertex of $\Gamma_0$ with $\{0,1,\dots,n\}$. We can find an isomorphism of ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured sets $f: (\{0,1,\dots,n\}, {\mathcal O}) \cong [n]$ and since, for planar crossed simplicial groups, $\mathfrak{G}_n$ acts (simply) transitively on $\operatorname{Hom}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}([0],[n])$ we may assume that $f$ maps $0$ to $0$. Therefore, after permuting the labels $1,2, \dots, n$, we may assume that $H(v) = [n]$. Every morphism $[n] \to [1]$ such that $\varphi^{-1}(0) = \{0\}$ (corresponding to the outgoing halfedge labeled $0$) can be written as a composite $\varphi g$ where $\varphi: [n] \to [1]$ is the morphism in $\Delta$ which maps $0$ to $0$ and all remaining elements to $1$, and $g \in \operatorname{Stab}(0) \subset \mathfrak{G}_n$. Therefore, we can assume that the augmentation $H(v) = [n] \to [1]$ of the single outgoing halfedge $0$ is given by $\varphi$. For every $1 \le i \le n$, the subset of $\operatorname{Hom}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}([n],[1])$ given by those morphisms such that $\varphi^{-1}(1) = \{i\}$ forms a torsor under the action of $\mathfrak{G}_1^0 \cong \mathfrak{G}_0$. Note that this action of $\mathfrak{G}_0$ is precisely the operadic action of the monoid $P_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1)$ on the incoming halfedges. Therefore, the collection of isomorphism classes of labelled augmented ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured $n$-corollas forms a torsor under the action of \[ \underbrace{P_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1) \times P_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1) \times \dots \times P_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1)}_n \times S_{n}. \] We will now trivialize this torsor, for every $n$, by choosing a specific ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured $n$-corolla in such a way that these chosen $n$-corollas are closed under operadic composition (for $n>1$). To this end, choose a duality functor $D: {\Delta \mathfrak{G}} \to {\Delta \mathfrak{G}}^{{\operatorname{op}}}$ and consider the diagram \[ \xymatrix{ [1] \ar[drr]_{\{0,1\}}& [1] \ar[dr]^{\{1,2\}} & \dots & [1] \ar[dl]^{\{n-1,n\}}\\ & & [n] & \\ & & [1]\ar[u]^{\{0,n\}} & } \] in $\Delta \subset {\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ and apply $D$ to obtain the incidence diagram of a labeled augmented ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured $n$-corolla which we define to be our chosen trivialization. It is easy to verify that, due to the functoriality of $D$, the collection of corollas thus obtained is closed under operadic composition. This exhibits a copy of the associative operad $\operatorname{Ass}$ in $P$ such that every element of $P$ can be uniquely expressed as an element of $\operatorname{Ass}$ precomposed with elements of the monoid $P_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1)$ acting on the incoming halfedges. An explicit computation of the action of $P_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1)$ on the outgoing halfedges of $\operatorname{Ass}$ in terms of the actions on the incoming halfedges implies the claim that $P$ parametrizes algebras with twisted $\mathfrak{G}_0$-action.
nodes.statement_short: Contract internal edges to corollas, normalize labels and augmentations, and trivialize the torsor of corollas by a duality functor, exhibiting $\operatorname{Ass}$ inside $P$ with twisted $\mathfrak{G}_0$-action.

nodes.name: Operad axioms are clear.
nodes.statement: Part (1) is clear.
nodes.statement_short: Operad axioms are clear.

nodes.name: Algebras over $P$
nodes.statement:
We show (2). Given an augmented ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured tree $\Gamma$ in
	$\operatorname{Tr}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(n)$ with augmented incidence diagram $I(\Gamma) \to {\mathcal G}$, we first argue that we
	can contract all internal edges to obtain a corolla. To this end, we note that, given an
	internal edge $\{e,e'\}$ incident to vertices $v$ and $v'$, the corresponding diagram
	\[
		H(v) \longrightarrow \{e,e'\} \longleftarrow H(v') 
	\]
	has a limit in ${\mathcal G}$ whose underlying set is given by $(H(v)\setminus \{e\}) \cup (H(v')
	\setminus \{e'\})$. This holds for all planar crossed simplicial groups and can be 
	verified using the topological model of ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ from \S \ref{sec:topmodel}.
	We can use the cone diagram of this limit in ${\mathcal G}$ to produce a morphism of
	${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured graphs $\Gamma \to \Gamma'$ which collapses the edge $\{e,e'\}$. After
	collapsing all internal edges of $\Gamma$, we obtain an augmented ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured 
	$n$-corolla $\Gamma_0$. Using the labels we can identify the set $H(v)$ of halfedges
	incident to the single vertex of $\Gamma_0$ with $\{0,1,\dots,n\}$. We can find an
	isomorphism of ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured sets $f: (\{0,1,\dots,n\}, {\mathcal O}) \cong [n]$ and since, for planar
	crossed simplicial groups, $\mathfrak{G}_n$ acts (simply) transitively on $\operatorname{Hom}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}([0],[n])$ we
	may assume that $f$ maps $0$ to $0$. Therefore, after permuting the labels $1,2, \dots, n$,
	we may assume that $H(v) = [n]$. Every morphism $[n] \to [1]$ such that $\varphi^{-1}(0) =
	\{0\}$ (corresponding to the outgoing halfedge labeled $0$) can be written as a composite 
	$\varphi g$ where $\varphi: [n] \to [1]$ is the morphism in $\Delta$ which maps $0$ to $0$
	and all remaining elements to $1$, and $g \in \operatorname{Stab}(0)
	\subset \mathfrak{G}_n$. Therefore, we can assume that the augmentation $H(v) = [n] \to [1]$ of the
	single outgoing halfedge $0$ is given by $\varphi$. 
	For every $1 \le i \le n$, the subset of $\operatorname{Hom}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}([n],[1])$ given by those morphisms such
	that $\varphi^{-1}(1) = \{i\}$ forms a torsor under the action of $\mathfrak{G}_1^0 \cong \mathfrak{G}_0$. 
	Note that this action of $\mathfrak{G}_0$ is precisely the operadic action of the monoid
	$P_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1)$ on the incoming halfedges. Therefore, the collection of isomorphism classes of
	labelled augmented ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured $n$-corollas forms a torsor under the action of 
	\[
		\underbrace{P_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1) \times P_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1) \times \dots \times P_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1)}_n \times S_{n}.
	\]
	We will now trivialize this torsor, for every $n$, by choosing a specific ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured
	$n$-corolla in such a way that these chosen $n$-corollas are closed under operadic
	composition (for $n>1$). To this end, choose a duality functor $D: {\Delta \mathfrak{G}} \to {\Delta \mathfrak{G}}^{{\operatorname{op}}}$ and consider the
	diagram
	\[
		\xymatrix{ [1] \ar[drr]_{\{0,1\}}& [1] \ar[dr]^{\{1,2\}} & \dots & [1] \ar[dl]^{\{n-1,n\}}\\
			& & [n] & \\
			& & [1]\ar[u]^{\{0,n\}} & 
		}
	\]
	in $\Delta \subset {\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ and apply $D$ to obtain the incidence diagram of a labeled augmented
	${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured $n$-corolla which we define to be our chosen trivialization. It is easy to
	verify that, due to the functoriality of $D$, the collection of corollas thus obtained is
	closed under operadic composition. This exhibits a copy of the associative operad $\operatorname{Ass}$
	in $P$ such that every element of $P$ can be uniquely expressed as an element of $\operatorname{Ass}$
	precomposed with elements of the monoid $P_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1)$ acting on the incoming halfedges. An
	explicit computation of the action of $P_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1)$ on the outgoing halfedges of $\operatorname{Ass}$
	in terms of the actions on the incoming halfedges implies the claim that $P$ parametrizes
	algebras with twisted $\mathfrak{G}_0$-action.
nodes.statement_short: Show algebras are monoids with twisted $\mathfrak{G}_0$-action.

nodes.name: Reduce trees to corollas.
nodes.statement:
Given an augmented ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured tree $\Gamma$ in
	$\operatorname{Tr}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(n)$ with augmented incidence diagram $I(\Gamma) \to {\mathcal G}$, we first argue that we
	can contract all internal edges to obtain a corolla.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce trees to corollas.

nodes.name: Limits in $\mathcal{G}$ collapse internal edges.
nodes.statement:
To this end, we note that, given an
	internal edge $\{e,e'\}$ incident to vertices $v$ and $v'$, the corresponding diagram
	\[
		H(v) \longrightarrow \{e,e'\} \longleftarrow H(v') 
	\]
	has a limit in ${\mathcal G}$ whose underlying set is given by $(H(v)\setminus \{e\}) \cup (H(v')
	\setminus \{e'\})$. This holds for all planar crossed simplicial groups and can be 
	verified using the topological model of ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ from \S \ref{sec:topmodel}.
	We can use the cone diagram of this limit in ${\mathcal G}$ to produce a morphism of
	${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured graphs $\Gamma \to \Gamma'$ which collapses the edge $\{e,e'\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Limits in $\mathcal{G}$ collapse internal edges.

nodes.name: Normalize the corolla and outgoing augmentation.
nodes.statement:
After
	collapsing all internal edges of $\Gamma$, we obtain an augmented ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured 
	$n$-corolla $\Gamma_0$. Using the labels we can identify the set $H(v)$ of halfedges
	incident to the single vertex of $\Gamma_0$ with $\{0,1,\dots,n\}$. We can find an
	isomorphism of ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured sets $f: (\{0,1,\dots,n\}, {\mathcal O}) \cong [n]$ and since, for planar
	crossed simplicial groups, $\mathfrak{G}_n$ acts (simply) transitively on $\operatorname{Hom}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}([0],[n])$ we
	may assume that $f$ maps $0$ to $0$. Therefore, after permuting the labels $1,2, \dots, n$,
	we may assume that $H(v) = [n]$. Every morphism $[n] \to [1]$ such that $\varphi^{-1}(0) =
	\{0\}$ (corresponding to the outgoing halfedge labeled $0$) can be written as a composite 
	$\varphi g$ where $\varphi: [n] \to [1]$ is the morphism in $\Delta$ which maps $0$ to $0$
	and all remaining elements to $1$, and $g \in \operatorname{Stab}(0)
	\subset \mathfrak{G}_n$. Therefore, we can assume that the augmentation $H(v) = [n] \to [1]$ of the
	single outgoing halfedge $0$ is given by $\varphi$.
nodes.statement_short: Normalize the corolla and outgoing augmentation.

nodes.name: Corollas form a torsor under $P(1)^n\times S_n$.
nodes.statement:
For every $1 \le i \le n$, the subset of $\operatorname{Hom}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}([n],[1])$ given by those morphisms such
	that $\varphi^{-1}(1) = \{i\}$ forms a torsor under the action of $\mathfrak{G}_1^0 \cong \mathfrak{G}_0$. 
	Note that this action of $\mathfrak{G}_0$ is precisely the operadic action of the monoid
	$P_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1)$ on the incoming halfedges. Therefore, the collection of isomorphism classes of
	labelled augmented ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured $n$-corollas forms a torsor under the action of 
	\[
		\underbrace{P_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1) \times P_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1) \times \dots \times P_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1)}_n \times S_{n}.
	\]
nodes.statement_short: Corollas form a torsor under $P(1)^n\times S_n$.

nodes.name: Trivialize the torsor by a duality functor.
nodes.statement:
We will now trivialize this torsor, for every $n$, by choosing a specific ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured
	$n$-corolla in such a way that these chosen $n$-corollas are closed under operadic
	composition (for $n>1$). To this end, choose a duality functor $D: {\Delta \mathfrak{G}} \to {\Delta \mathfrak{G}}^{{\operatorname{op}}}$ and consider the
	diagram
	\[
		\xymatrix{ [1] \ar[drr]_{\{0,1\}}& [1] \ar[dr]^{\{1,2\}} & \dots & [1] \ar[dl]^{\{n-1,n\}}\\
			& & [n] & \\
			& & [1]\ar[u]^{\{0,n\}} & 
		}
	\]
	in $\Delta \subset {\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ and apply $D$ to obtain the incidence diagram of a labeled augmented
	${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured $n$-corolla which we define to be our chosen trivialization. It is easy to
	verify that, due to the functoriality of $D$, the collection of corollas thus obtained is
	closed under operadic composition.
nodes.statement_short: Trivialize the torsor by a duality functor.

nodes.name: Copy of $\operatorname{Ass}$ with twisted action; conclude.
nodes.statement:
This exhibits a copy of the associative operad $\operatorname{Ass}$
	in $P$ such that every element of $P$ can be uniquely expressed as an element of $\operatorname{Ass}$
	precomposed with elements of the monoid $P_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1)$ acting on the incoming halfedges. An
	explicit computation of the action of $P_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(1)$ on the outgoing halfedges of $\operatorname{Ass}$
	in terms of the actions on the incoming halfedges implies the claim that $P$ parametrizes
	algebras with twisted $\mathfrak{G}_0$-action.
nodes.statement_short: Copy of $\operatorname{Ass}$ with twisted action; conclude.

nodes.name: Topological operad of augmented trees
nodes.statement: Proposition \ref{prop:Gc-operad} can be enhanced by considering the geometric realization of the categories $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}(n)$ instead of the set $P_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}}(n)$ of its connected components. In this way, we obtain an operad $\operatorname{N}\operatorname{Tr}_{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$ in the category of topological spaces which describes $A_\infty$-monoids with a twisted coherent action of $\mathfrak{G}_0$.

nodes.name: Modular operadic interpretation
nodes.statement: The results of this section suggest that augmented ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured {\em graphs} can be interpreted in modular operadic terms generalizing the well-known approaches to $2$-dimensional topological field theories in the cyclic and dihedral cases (cf. \cite{costello-TFT, braun}). We leave the systematic treatment of these generalizations to future work.

nodes.name: $d$-cell
nodes.statement:
By a $d$-{\em cell} we mean a topological space $\sigma$ homeomorphic to
  an open ball  $B^d \subset \mathbb{R}^d$.

nodes.name: $d$-orbicell
nodes.statement:
By a $d$-{\em orbicell} we mean a topological groupoid equivalent
  to $D\backslash \hskip -.1cm \backslash\sigma$ where $\sigma\simeq B^d$ is a $d$-cell and $D$ is a discrete group acting on $\sigma$ via a
  homomorphism $\phi: D\to{ \operatorname{Homeo}}(\sigma)$ whose image is identified with  a finite group  
   of linear transformations of $B^d$.

nodes.name: Orbicell decomposition
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a topological groupoid. An {\em orbicell decomposition} of $X$ is a finite filtration \[ \mathcal{X} = \bigl( \mathcal{X}_0\subset\mathcal{X}_1 \subset\cdots\subset \mathcal{X}_n = X) \] of $X$ by closed topological subgroupoids $\mathcal{X}_d$ such that: \begin{enumerate} \item[(1)] Each $\mathcal{X}_d$ is a full subcategory in $X$. \item[(2)] Each component of $\mathcal{X}_d-\mathcal{X}_{d-1}$ is a disjoint union of $d$-orbicells. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Orbicell decompositions from equivariant cell decompositions
nodes.statement: Let $Y$ be a topological space with a cell decomposition ${\mathcal Y}$. Let $D$ be a discrete group acting on $Y$, preserving ${\mathcal Y}$ and such that for each cell $\sigma$ of ${\mathcal Y}$ the stabilizer $\operatorname{Stab}(\sigma)$ acting on $\sigma$, makes $\operatorname{Stab}(\sigma)\backslash \hskip -.1cm \backslash\sigma$ into an orbicell. Then the groupoid $D\backslash \hskip -.1cm \backslash Y$ has an orbicell decomposition into orbicells $\operatorname{Stab}(\sigma)\backslash \hskip -.1cm \backslash\sigma$ where $\sigma$ runs over orbits of $D$ on the set of cells of ${\mathcal Y}$.
nodes.label: ex:regular-cell

nodes.name: Regular cell decomposition
nodes.statement:
Recall that for ordinary spaces (not groupoids) $Y$ there is a concept of a {\em regular cell decomposition}
  which is a cell decomposition ${\mathcal Y}$ such that the closure of each $d$-cell $\sigma$ of ${\mathcal Y}$ is
  homeomorphic to a closed ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$ (whose boundary is therefore a $(d-1)$-sphere with
  further cell decomposition induced by ${\mathcal Y}$).

nodes.name: Quotient-regular orbicell decomposition
nodes.statement: An orbicell decomposition $\mathcal{X}$ of a topological groupoid $X$ is called {\em quotient-regular}, if there is an equivalence of $X$ with a quotient groupoid $D\backslash \hskip -.1cm \backslash Y$ and a regular $D$-invariant cell decomposition ${\mathcal Y}$ of $Y$ as in Example \ref{ex:regular-cell}, which induces $\mathcal{X}$.

nodes.name: Category of cells
nodes.statement:
For a quotient-regular cell decomposition $\mathcal{X}$ we have a category ${\operatorname{Cell}}(\mathcal{X})$ whose objects
  are cells of ${\mathcal Y}$ and morphisms are induced by action of $D$ and inclusion of cells.
  In other words, ${\operatorname{Cell}}(\mathcal{X})$ is the semi-direct product of $D$ and the poset of cells of ${\mathcal Y}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Classifying space of the cell category
nodes.statement:
The following is then straightforward
  and follows from Proposition \ref{prop:nerve-classical}.
nodes.statement_short: Follows from the classical nerve theorem (Proposition A.6).

nodes.name: Classifying space of the cell category
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{X}$ is a quotient-regular orbicell decomposition of $X$, then the classifying space of the (non-topological) category ${\operatorname{Cell}}(\mathcal{X})$ is homotopy equivalent to the classifying space of $X$ as a topological category. \qed
assumptions: If $\mathcal{X}$ is a quotient-regular orbicell decomposition of $X$
conclusions: is homotopy equivalent to the classifying space of $X$
nodes.label: prop:orbicell-cell

nodes.name: Proof of Structured graphs classify structured surfaces
nodes.statement:
We now prove the following fact which, in virtue of Proposition 
\ref {prop:orbicell-cell}, implies Theorem \ref{thm:g-graph}.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 4.25 together with Proposition 4.24 implies Theorem 4.12.
nodes.section: Decompositions of the structured moduli spaces

nodes.name: Orbicell decomposition of structured moduli spaces
nodes.statement: Consider the orbifold \[ \mathcal{M}^{G_{\operatorname{conf}}} \,\,=\,\,\coprod_{(S,M)} \mathcal{M}^{G_{\operatorname{conf}}}(S,M) \] where $(S,M)$ runs over all possible topological types of stable marked surfaces. Then $\mathcal{M}^{G_{\operatorname{conf}}}$ has a quotient-regular orbicell decomposition $\mathcal{X}$ such that we have an equivalence of categories ${\operatorname{Cell}}(\mathcal{X})\simeq {\Delta \mathfrak{G}}-\operatorname{Graph}$.
nodes.statement_short: The structured moduli orbifold has a quotient-regular orbicell decomposition whose cell category is $\Delta\mathfrak{G}$-Graph.
nodes.section: Decompositions of the structured moduli spaces
conclusions: has a quotient-regular orbicell decomposition $\mathcal{X}$ such that we have an equivalence
nodes.label: thm:decomp

nodes.name: Proof of Orbicell decomposition of structured moduli spaces
nodes.statement_short: Oriented and unoriented cases from Harer's triangulation of Teichmüller space; the general case by pulling back along the unramified covering to the unoriented moduli space and comparing fibers via Lemma 4.26.
nodes.section: Decompositions of the structured moduli spaces

nodes.name: Oriented case: Harer's ribbon graph decomposition.
nodes.statement:
\underbar{(a) Oriented case } $G=SO(2)$. In this case, the statement (that the usual
	moduli space of stable marked {\em Riemann surfaces} has an orbicell decomposition labelled
	by ribbon graphs) is well known, see, e.g., \cite{arbarello, penner:book} and references
	therein. We indicate here the main steps which we later analyze to deduce the general case.
 
	First, each component of $\mathcal{M}^{SO(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}}$ is a quotient groupoid 
	\[
	 \mathcal{M}^{SO(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}}(S,M) \,\,=\,\, \operatorname{Mod}^+(S,M)\bigl\backslash \hskip -.1cm \bigl\backslash\operatorname{Teich}^+(S,M).
	\]
	Second, $\operatorname{Teich}^+(S,M)$  has a $\operatorname{Mod}^+(S,M)$-invariant regular cell decomposition
	(triangulation)  constructed by Harer \cite{harer} and described in Appendix \ref
	{subsub:harer}.  Denote this cell decomposition by ${\mathcal Y}$.  The simplices of ${\mathcal Y}$ correspond
	to tesselations of $(S,M)$ or, dually, to isotopy classes of spanning graphs for $(S,M)$.
	Inclusions of simplices correspond to coarsenings of tesselations or, dually, to contractions of
	spanning graphs.  Any spanning graph for $(S,M)$ carries an induced ribbon structure.
	Therefore, orbicells in the quotient orbicell decomposition, which we denote $\mathcal{X}_{S,M}$,
	form a full subcategory in $\Lambda-\operatorname{Graph}$ with objects those graphs that appear as
	spanning graphs for $(S,M)$.  Finally, each ribbon graph $\Gamma$ gives rise to an oriented
	marked surface $(S,M)$ obtained by ``thickening" $\Gamma$, so that $\Gamma$ becomes a
	spanning graph for $(S,M)$, see, e.g., \cite{HSS-triangulated} \S 3.3.4. This shows that for
	$\mathcal{X}=\coprod_{(S,M)} \mathcal{X}_{S,M}$, we have ${\operatorname{Cell}}(\mathcal{X})\simeq {\Lambda}-\operatorname{Graph}$. 

	Note that Costello \cite{costello-dual} introduced another topological groupoid $\mathcal{N}$ with
	an orbicell decomposition labelled by ${\Lambda}-\operatorname{Graph}$ which is homotopy equivalent,
	but not homeomorphic to $\mathcal{M}^{SO(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Oriented case: Harer's ribbon graph decomposition.
nodes.section: Decompositions of the structured moduli spaces

nodes.name: Unoriented case: Möbius graphs from the triangulation of $\operator...
nodes.statement:
\underbar{(b) Unoriented case} $G=O(2)$. It is treated similarly to the oriented case, using
	the identification \[ \mathcal{M}^{O(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}}(S,M) \,\,=\,\,\operatorname{Mod}(S,M) \bigl\backslash \hskip -.1cm \bigl\backslash \operatorname{Teich}(S,M) \] and the
	triangulation ${\mathcal Y}$ of $\operatorname{Teich}(S,M)$ described in \S \ref{subsub:harer}. As before, the
	simplices of ${\mathcal Y}$ correspond to triangulations of $(S,M)$ and give M\"obius graphs as
	$\operatorname{Mod}(S,M)$-orbits. Further, any M\"obius graph $\Gamma$ can be ``thickened" producing an
	unoriented surface $(S,M)$ in which it is spanning. So, for the resulting quotient orbicell
	decomposition $\mathcal{X}$ of $\mathcal{M}^{O(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}}$ we have ${\operatorname{Cell}}(\mathcal{X})\simeq {\Xi}-\operatorname{Graph}$. 

	Note that an analog of Costello's approach \cite{costello-dual} for Klein surfaces was developed
	by Braun \cite{braun}.
nodes.statement_short: Unoriented case: Möbius graphs from the triangulation of $\operatorname{Teich}(S,M)$.
nodes.section: Decompositions of the structured moduli spaces

nodes.name: General case by pulling back along the forgetful covering.
nodes.statement:
\underbar{(c) General case:} $G$ an arbitrary planar Lie group. Depending on whether $G$
	preserves orientation or not, we consider one of the two projections
	\[
	\pi: \mathcal{M}^{G_{\operatorname{conf}}} \longrightarrow \mathcal{M}^{SO(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}}, \quad  \pi: \mathcal{M}^{G_{\operatorname{conf}}} \longrightarrow \mathcal{M}^{O(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}}
	\]
	obtained by forgetting the extra structure. In each case, the projection $\pi$ is an
	unramified covering of orbifolds, so the preimage of any orbicell in the target is a
	disjoint union of orbicells in the source.  We thus obtain an orbicell decomposition of
	$\mathcal{M}^{G_{\operatorname{conf}}}$ which we now analyze. We sketch the case when $G$ does not preserve the
	orientation, the other case being similar but easier. 
	Denote by $\mathcal{X}$ the orbicell decomposition of $\mathcal{M}^{O(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}}$ and by $\mathcal{X}^G$ the preimage
	decomposition of $\mathcal{M}^{G_{\operatorname{conf}}}$. Since any $G_{\operatorname{conf}}$-structured marked surface is
	$\mathbb{G}$-structured, any tessellation $\mathcal{P}$ of the surface makes the dual graph of $\mathcal{P}$ into
	a ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured graph. We obtain therefore a commutative diagram of categories
	\[
	\xymatrix{
	{\operatorname{Cell}}(\mathcal{X}^G)
	\ar[d]_{q_G} \ar[r]^{\pi} & {\operatorname{Cell}}(\mathcal{X})
	\ar[d]^q
	\\
	{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}-\operatorname{Graph} \ar[r]_\varpi & {\Xi}-\operatorname{Graph}
	}
	\]
	where $q$ is an equivalence by the case (b) above. We prove that $q_G$ is an equivalence as well.
	For this, we note that any morphism $\Gamma \to \Gamma'$ in ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}-\operatorname{Graph}$ can be expressed
	uniquely as the composition of a contraction of a set of $I$ of edges of $\Gamma$ (which
	results in a canonical contraction morphism $\Gamma \to \Gamma_I$) followed by an isomorphism 
	$\Gamma_I \to \Gamma'$. This implies that, assuming $\operatorname{Hom}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}-\operatorname{Graph}}(\Gamma,\Gamma') \ne
	\emptyset$, any
	fiber of the map 
	\[
		\operatorname{Hom}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}-\operatorname{Graph}}(\Gamma,\Gamma') \longrightarrow
		\operatorname{Hom}_{{\Xi}-\operatorname{Graph}}(\varpi(\Gamma),\varpi(\Gamma'))
	\]
	is acted upon simply transitively by the group $\operatorname{Aut}\nolimits(\Gamma'/\varpi(\Gamma'))$ of automorphisms of $\Gamma'$ which induce
	the identity on $\varpi(\Gamma')$. A similar analysis of the morphisms in ${\operatorname{Cell}}(\mathcal{X}^G)$
	implies that the fibers of the map 
	\[
		\operatorname{Hom}_{{\operatorname{Cell}}(\mathcal{X}^G)}(\sigma,\sigma') \longrightarrow
		\operatorname{Hom}_{{\operatorname{Cell}}(\mathcal{X})}(\pi(\sigma),\pi(\sigma'))
	\]
	are torsors for the group $\operatorname{Aut}\nolimits(\sigma'/\pi(\sigma'))$ of automorphisms of $\sigma'$
	inducing the identity on $\pi(\sigma')$.
	Since we already know that the map $q$ is fully faithful, to show that $q^G$ is fully
	faithful, it therefore suffices to show that the induced map 
	\[
		\operatorname{Aut}\nolimits(\sigma'/\pi(\sigma')) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Aut}\nolimits(q^G(\sigma')/q^G(\pi(\sigma')))
	\]
	is bijective. Showing this statement and the essential surjectivity of $q^G$ amounts to  
	showing that $q^G$ induces an equivalence of all strict fiber categories of $\pi$ and
	$\varpi$. This is shown in the following lemma.
nodes.statement_short: General case by pulling back along the forgetful covering.
nodes.section: Decompositions of the structured moduli spaces

nodes.name: The forgetful projection is an unramified covering.
nodes.statement:
Depending on whether $G$
	preserves orientation or not, we consider one of the two projections
	\[
	\pi: \mathcal{M}^{G_{\operatorname{conf}}} \longrightarrow \mathcal{M}^{SO(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}}, \quad  \pi: \mathcal{M}^{G_{\operatorname{conf}}} \longrightarrow \mathcal{M}^{O(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}}
	\]
	obtained by forgetting the extra structure. In each case, the projection $\pi$ is an
	unramified covering of orbifolds, so the preimage of any orbicell in the target is a
	disjoint union of orbicells in the source.  We thus obtain an orbicell decomposition of
	$\mathcal{M}^{G_{\operatorname{conf}}}$ which we now analyze. We sketch the case when $G$ does not preserve the
	orientation, the other case being similar but easier.
nodes.statement_short: The forgetful projection is an unramified covering.
nodes.section: Decompositions of the structured moduli spaces

nodes.name: Commutative square of cell categories and graph categories.
nodes.statement:
Denote by $\mathcal{X}$ the orbicell decomposition of $\mathcal{M}^{O(2)_{\operatorname{conf}}}$ and by $\mathcal{X}^G$ the preimage
	decomposition of $\mathcal{M}^{G_{\operatorname{conf}}}$. Since any $G_{\operatorname{conf}}$-structured marked surface is
	$\mathbb{G}$-structured, any tessellation $\mathcal{P}$ of the surface makes the dual graph of $\mathcal{P}$ into
	a ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structured graph. We obtain therefore a commutative diagram of categories
	\[
	\xymatrix{
	{\operatorname{Cell}}(\mathcal{X}^G)
	\ar[d]_{q_G} \ar[r]^{\pi} & {\operatorname{Cell}}(\mathcal{X})
	\ar[d]^q
	\\
	{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}-\operatorname{Graph} \ar[r]_\varpi & {\Xi}-\operatorname{Graph}
	}
	\]
	where $q$ is an equivalence by the case (b) above. We prove that $q_G$ is an equivalence as well.
nodes.statement_short: Commutative square of cell categories and graph categories.
nodes.section: Decompositions of the structured moduli spaces

nodes.name: Compare fibers; reduce to Lemma 4.26.
nodes.statement:
For this, we note that any morphism $\Gamma \to \Gamma'$ in ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}-\operatorname{Graph}$ can be expressed
	uniquely as the composition of a contraction of a set of $I$ of edges of $\Gamma$ (which
	results in a canonical contraction morphism $\Gamma \to \Gamma_I$) followed by an isomorphism 
	$\Gamma_I \to \Gamma'$. This implies that, assuming $\operatorname{Hom}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}-\operatorname{Graph}}(\Gamma,\Gamma') \ne
	\emptyset$, any
	fiber of the map 
	\[
		\operatorname{Hom}_{{\Delta \mathfrak{G}}-\operatorname{Graph}}(\Gamma,\Gamma') \longrightarrow
		\operatorname{Hom}_{{\Xi}-\operatorname{Graph}}(\varpi(\Gamma),\varpi(\Gamma'))
	\]
	is acted upon simply transitively by the group $\operatorname{Aut}\nolimits(\Gamma'/\varpi(\Gamma'))$ of automorphisms of $\Gamma'$ which induce
	the identity on $\varpi(\Gamma')$. A similar analysis of the morphisms in ${\operatorname{Cell}}(\mathcal{X}^G)$
	implies that the fibers of the map 
	\[
		\operatorname{Hom}_{{\operatorname{Cell}}(\mathcal{X}^G)}(\sigma,\sigma') \longrightarrow
		\operatorname{Hom}_{{\operatorname{Cell}}(\mathcal{X})}(\pi(\sigma),\pi(\sigma'))
	\]
	are torsors for the group $\operatorname{Aut}\nolimits(\sigma'/\pi(\sigma'))$ of automorphisms of $\sigma'$
	inducing the identity on $\pi(\sigma')$.
	Since we already know that the map $q$ is fully faithful, to show that $q^G$ is fully
	faithful, it therefore suffices to show that the induced map 
	\[
		\operatorname{Aut}\nolimits(\sigma'/\pi(\sigma')) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Aut}\nolimits(q^G(\sigma')/q^G(\pi(\sigma')))
	\]
	is bijective. Showing this statement and the essential surjectivity of $q^G$ amounts to  
	showing that $q^G$ induces an equivalence of all strict fiber categories of $\pi$ and
	$\varpi$. This is shown in the following lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Compare fibers; reduce to Lemma 4.26.
nodes.section: Decompositions of the structured moduli spaces

nodes.name: Structures on surfaces and on spanning graphs
nodes.statement: Let $(S,M)$ be a stable marked surface and $\Gamma$ be a spanning graph for $(S,M)$. Then the functor \[ q_\Gamma: \mathbb{G}\operatorname{Str}(S-(M\cap S^\circ) )\to {\Delta \mathfrak{G}}\operatorname{Str}(\Gamma) \] is an equivalence of categories.
nodes.section: Decompositions of the structured moduli spaces
assumptions: Let $(S,M)$ be a stable marked surface and $\Gamma$ be a spanning graph for $(S,M)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Structures on surfaces and on spanning graphs
nodes.statement_short: Essential surjectivity by extending circle-bundle structures from the graph to the homotopy equivalent surface; full faithfulness by comparing the automorphism local systems.
nodes.section: Decompositions of the structured moduli spaces

nodes.name: Essential surjectivity
nodes.statement:
We first show that $q_\Gamma$ is essentially surjective. Let $F_\Gamma$ be a
	${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structure on $\Gamma$.  By Theorem \ref{thm:CG=DG}, $F_\Gamma$ can be seen as a datum,
	for each $x\in\Gamma\subset S'$, of a ${ \operatorname{Homeo}}^G(S^1)$-structure on the circle of directions
	$C_x(S)$. Moreover, these structures are compatible as $x$ moves in $\Gamma$, thus providing
	a ${ \operatorname{Homeo}}^G(S^1)$-structure on $C(T_S)|_\Gamma$, the restriction to $\Gamma$ of the circle
	bundle $C(T_S)$. Since $\Gamma$ is homotopy equivalent to $S-M$ and hence to $S-(M\cap
	S^\circ)$, we get a unique, up to isomorphism, ${ \operatorname{Homeo}}^G(S^1)$-structure on $C(T_{S-(M\cap
	S^\circ)})$. Finally, since $\mathbb{G}\to{ \operatorname{Homeo}}^G(S^1)$ is a homotopy equivalence, we obtain from
	this a $\mathbb{G}$-structure on $S-(M\cap S^\circ)$. Thus $q_\Gamma$ is essentially surjective.
nodes.statement_short: Show $q_\Gamma$ is essentially surjective.
nodes.section: Decompositions of the structured moduli spaces

nodes.name: Theorem 2.13 gives a structured circle bundle over $\Gamma$.
nodes.statement:
Let $F_\Gamma$ be a
	${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structure on $\Gamma$.  By Theorem \ref{thm:CG=DG}, $F_\Gamma$ can be seen as a datum,
	for each $x\in\Gamma\subset S'$, of a ${ \operatorname{Homeo}}^G(S^1)$-structure on the circle of directions
	$C_x(S)$. Moreover, these structures are compatible as $x$ moves in $\Gamma$, thus providing
	a ${ \operatorname{Homeo}}^G(S^1)$-structure on $C(T_S)|_\Gamma$, the restriction to $\Gamma$ of the circle
	bundle $C(T_S)$.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 2.13 gives a structured circle bundle over $\Gamma$.
nodes.section: Decompositions of the structured moduli spaces

nodes.name: Extend to $S-(M\cap S^\circ)$ and lift to $\mathbb{G}$.
nodes.statement:
Since $\Gamma$ is homotopy equivalent to $S-M$ and hence to $S-(M\cap
	S^\circ)$, we get a unique, up to isomorphism, ${ \operatorname{Homeo}}^G(S^1)$-structure on $C(T_{S-(M\cap
	S^\circ)})$. Finally, since $\mathbb{G}\to{ \operatorname{Homeo}}^G(S^1)$ is a homotopy equivalence, we obtain from
	this a $\mathbb{G}$-structure on $S-(M\cap S^\circ)$. Thus $q_\Gamma$ is essentially surjective.
nodes.statement_short: Extend to $S-(M\cap S^\circ)$ and lift to $\mathbb{G}$.
nodes.section: Decompositions of the structured moduli spaces

nodes.name: Full faithfulness
nodes.statement:
Second, we show that $q_\Gamma$ induces bijections on Hom-sets. Because $\mathbb{G}\operatorname{Str}(S)$ is a
	 groupoid, it is enough to show that for each $\mathbb{G}$-structure $F$ on $S-(M\cap S^\circ)$ the
	 induced map of automorphism groups
	 \[
		 q_*: \operatorname{Aut}\nolimits(F)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}\nolimits(F_\Gamma)
	 \]
	 is an isomorphism. Note that $q_*$ actually comes (by passing to global sections) from a
	 homomorphism of sheaves of groups on $\Gamma$ formed by local isomorphisms:
	 \[
		  \underline q_*: \underline {\operatorname{Aut}\nolimits}(F)\longrightarrow\underline {\operatorname{Aut}\nolimits}(F_\Gamma). 
	 \]
	 So it is enough to prove that $  \underline q_*:$ is an isomorphism of sheaves. By
	 Proposition \ref{prop:G-structures}(b1), $\underline{\operatorname{Aut}\nolimits}(F)=\underline K^{\operatorname{or}}$ is the local
	 system obtained by the orientation twist of $K=\operatorname{Ker}\nolimits\{\mathbb{G}\to GL(2,\mathbb{R})\}$. Now note that $K$
	 can also be identified with $\operatorname{Ker}\nolimits\{\mathfrak{G}_n\to D_{n+1}\}$ for any $n$ by Theorem
	 \ref{thm:crossed-groups}(b2). An automorphism of the ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structure $F_\Gamma$ (identical
	 on $\Gamma$) is therefore a section of a local system $\mathcal{L}$ on $\Gamma$ whose stalk at each
	 point is isomorphic to $K$. The final identification of $\mathcal{L}$ with $\underline K^{\operatorname{or}}$ and
	 of $q_*$ with the identity of  $\underline K^{\operatorname{or}}$ is left to the reader.
nodes.statement_short: Show $q_\Gamma$ is fully faithful.
nodes.section: Decompositions of the structured moduli spaces

nodes.name: Reduce to automorphism groups.
nodes.statement:
Because $\mathbb{G}\operatorname{Str}(S)$ is a
	 groupoid, it is enough to show that for each $\mathbb{G}$-structure $F$ on $S-(M\cap S^\circ)$ the
	 induced map of automorphism groups
	 \[
		 q_*: \operatorname{Aut}\nolimits(F)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}\nolimits(F_\Gamma)
	 \]
	 is an isomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to automorphism groups.
nodes.section: Decompositions of the structured moduli spaces

nodes.name: Reduce to sheaves of automorphisms.
nodes.statement:
Note that $q_*$ actually comes (by passing to global sections) from a
	 homomorphism of sheaves of groups on $\Gamma$ formed by local isomorphisms:
	 \[
		  \underline q_*: \underline {\operatorname{Aut}\nolimits}(F)\longrightarrow\underline {\operatorname{Aut}\nolimits}(F_\Gamma). 
	 \]
	 So it is enough to prove that $  \underline q_*:$ is an isomorphism of sheaves.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to sheaves of automorphisms.

nodes.name: Both sheaves are the local system with stalk $K$.
nodes.statement:
By
	 Proposition \ref{prop:G-structures}(b1), $\underline{\operatorname{Aut}\nolimits}(F)=\underline K^{\operatorname{or}}$ is the local
	 system obtained by the orientation twist of $K=\operatorname{Ker}\nolimits\{\mathbb{G}\to GL(2,\mathbb{R})\}$. Now note that $K$
	 can also be identified with $\operatorname{Ker}\nolimits\{\mathfrak{G}_n\to D_{n+1}\}$ for any $n$ by Theorem
	 \ref{thm:crossed-groups}(b2). An automorphism of the ${\Delta \mathfrak{G}}$-structure $F_\Gamma$ (identical
	 on $\Gamma$) is therefore a section of a local system $\mathcal{L}$ on $\Gamma$ whose stalk at each
	 point is isomorphic to $K$. The final identification of $\mathcal{L}$ with $\underline K^{\operatorname{or}}$ and
	 of $q_*$ with the identity of  $\underline K^{\operatorname{or}}$ is left to the reader.
nodes.statement_short: Both sheaves are the local system with stalk $K$.

nodes.name: Functor categories $\mathbf{C}^I$, $\mathbf{C}_I$
Opposite Yoneda embedding $\Upsilon$
nodes.statement:
More precisely, let 
\[
	\Upsilon: \Delta^{{\operatorname{op}}} \to ({\mathcal Set}_{\Delta})^{{\operatorname{op}}}
\]
be the opposite of the Yoneda embedding.

nodes.name: Object of $K$-membranes
nodes.statement:
We introduce the notation
$(K,X) := \Upsilon_* X (K)$ and refer to it as the {\em object of $K$-membranes in $X$}.

nodes.name: Derived object of $K$-membranes
nodes.statement:
We call $(K,X)_R := R \Upsilon_* X(K)$ the {\em derived
object of $K$-membranes in $X$}.

nodes.name: Subdivided interval $I[n]$
nodes.statement: For $n \ge 1$, we denote by $I[n] \subset \Delta^n$ the simplicial subset corresponding to the subdivided interval \[ \begin{tikzpicture}[>=stealth,scale=1.5] \begin{scope}[ >=stealth] \coordinate (A0) at (0,0); \coordinate (A1) at (1,0); \coordinate (B1) at (2,0); \coordinate (DOTS) at (2.5,0); \coordinate (A2) at (3,0); \coordinate (A3) at (4,0); \begin{scope}[decoration={ markings, mark=at position 0.55 with {\arrow{>}}} ] \draw[postaction={decorate}] (A0) -- (A1); \draw[postaction={decorate}] (A1) -- (B1); \draw[postaction={decorate}] (A2) -- (A3); \end{scope} {\scriptsize \draw (A0) node[anchor=south] {$0$}; \draw (A1) node[anchor=south] {$1$}; \draw (B1) node[anchor=south] {$2$}; \draw (DOTS) node {$\cdots$}; \draw (A2) node[anchor=south] {$n-1$}; \draw (A3) node[anchor=south] {$n$}; } \fill (A0) circle[radius=1pt]; \fill (A1) circle[radius=1pt]; \fill (B1) circle[radius=1pt]; \fill (A2) circle[radius=1pt]; \fill (A3) circle[radius=1pt]; \end{scope} \end{tikzpicture} \] which can be more formally described as the pushout of simplicial sets \[ \textstyle \Delta^1 \coprod_{\Delta^0} \Delta^1 \coprod_{\Delta^0} \dots \coprod_{\Delta^0} \Delta^1. \]

nodes.statement: Let $P_{n+1}$ be a convex plane $(n+1)$-gon with the set of vertices labelled counterclockwise by $M = \{0,1,\cdots , n\}$. A geometric triangle $\sigma$ of $\mathcal{T}$ with vertices $i,j,k$ gives rise to a unique full simplicial subset $\Delta^2 \subset \Delta^n$ with vertices $\{i\}, \{j\},\{k\}$.
